Players have to keep track of whose go it is.

pairs.tendency: When everyone moves at once, an extra turn means one player gets a second choice in the same round.
pros: A player gets two choices in one round.
The round is longer for them.
cons: The others sit through it.
The shared reveal stops being even.

pairs.tendency: With no turns at all, a rule that gives another go has nothing to attach to, since the quickest hands already get more moves.
pros: Quick hands move often anyway.
Nobody waits for a go.
cons: The rule gives no way to tell who is owed one.
Players may argue over who moved last.

pairs.tendency: A clock runs on each turn, and an extra turn gives a second clock. Two moves come under pressure.
pros: Two moves under a clock.
The extra turn adds a scramble.
cons: Mistakes can pile up.
Others wait for both clocks to finish.

pairs.tendency: In a game played over days, an extra turn means two moves on the same morning.
pros: A player moves again at once.
Waiting is cut short.
cons: Others wake to a changed board.
The slow rhythm of one move a day is broken.

pairs.tendency: The game slows down with a pause before each move, and an extra turn means another pause.
pros: Each go comes with its own breath.
A second turn is a second slow move.
cons: Others wait longer.
The pace stretches.

pairs.tendency: As the game speeds up, extra turns speed it more. A lucky player can finish a round in a rush.
pros: The game ends sooner.
Late rounds are crammed.
cons: Players cannot keep up with the changes.
A leader can race out of reach.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn in the first stage gives a player more to carry into the second, so one lucky go can shape the whole game.
pros: A first-stage run carries forward.
Stage rules can decide what a turn is worth.
cons: An early lucky turn can decide too much.
Players in the later stage feel the effects of early luck.

pairs.tendency: In a model of a real system, an extra turn means one actor changes it twice before the others respond.
pros: Changes can run ahead of the reaction.
It shows how fast one actor can act.
cons: The system may be damaged before others answer.
The balance of the system is hard to read.

pairs.tendency: A group that gets an extra turn can press its case twice. The others see how a second chance changes the table.
pros: One group's case gets a second move.
Unequal turns show unequal power.
cons: Other groups sit and wait.
The group with the extra turn may crowd out the rest.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets a player draw twice from the shared store before the others take their share.
pros: A player can take more in one round.
Others see the store drop fast.
cons: The store shrinks sooner.
Players may race to win extra turns.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn adds a move whose effect shows up later, so two actions can land in the same delay.
pros: Two actions can pay off together.
The delay is less of a wait.
cons: Cause and effect can blur.
Which of the two moves did what is unclear.

pairs.tendency: The table tries extra turns as a new rule and sees what changes.
pros: A new rule can be tested in play.
Lucky streaks show up quickly.
cons: The effect depends on the dice.
One test may not show what a rule does.

pairs.tendency: After a game with extra turns, the talk can start from the lucky runs. What did they change, and was it the dice or a choice?
pros: Lucky runs give the talk something to start with.
Players compare notes on what the extra turns changed.
cons: Hard to tell what was luck.
The talk may drift to who was lucky.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn gives a second change that cannot be undone, so a hasty move is doubled.
pros: Two permanent changes in one go.
The next game starts further along.
cons: A mistake is carried twice.
Others inherit the result.

pairs.tendency: Rules that give extra turns for some acts say that those acts matter. The game makes a point by what it rewards.
pros: The reward says something about the world.
Players can ask why the rule is there.
cons: Players may read the rule as a message.
The rule can seem to favour one kind of act.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn with real money or promises at stake makes a lucky run matter beyond the table.
pros: A lucky run counts for something.
The stakes make a repeat go count.
cons: A friend's lucky run can sting.
Others watch their own stake sit idle.

pairs.tendency: Extra turns give more chances to gather points that stand for something like kindness, so the points pile up fast.
pros: The count rises quickly.
A player can chase the number.
cons: The value behind the number may be forgotten.
A lucky run can look like virtue.

pairs.tendency: In a rehearsal, an extra turn lets one person try a way of living twice while the rest watch.
pros: A person can test an idea twice.
The rehearsal shows the idea in action.
cons: Others watch and do not join.
Lucky people get to rehearse more.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage players choose a path or a piece, and in the second they roll and race along it.
pros: Early choices shape the later race.
The dice have something to carry out.
cons: A choice made before the dice can be wasted.
The second stage can feel short after a long first.

pairs.tendency: Stage one is a draft of cards from a shared row, and stage two is played with what you took.
pros: Drafting gives the second stage its tools.
Each pick has a later use.
cons: A pick that looks fine can fail later.
Drafting takes a long time before play starts.

pairs.tendency: An auction opens the game, and what each player wins is used in the second stage.
pros: Bids decide what a player has to work with.
Money spent early shapes later play.
cons: A player who overspends starts the second stage short.
Auctions can take a long time.

pairs.tendency: A first stage builds up a stake and a second stage lets players risk it.
pros: Risks are taken with something earned.
The first stage gives the risk a size.
cons: A bust in the second stage wipes out the first.
Risk-takers and careful players may split.

pairs.tendency: Pieces go onto the map in the first stage, and the second stage is the fight over who holds what.
pros: Early setup decides the later fight.
A map with a plan behind it.
cons: Late arrivals find it already full.
The second stage can feel decided by the first.

pairs.tendency: Workers collect goods in the first stage, and the goods are spent in the second.
pros: The jobs and the spending are separate.
The first stage sets a budget.
cons: A wrong job in the first stage cannot be fixed.
Players wait for the second stage to find out if jobs paid.

pairs.tendency: The first stage collects pieces and the second lays them in patterns.
pros: Patterns grow from a pile gathered earlier.
The second stage is calm.
cons: A thin pile limits the patterns.
Gathering may feel like a chore.

pairs.tendency: Before the real play starts, a first stage fills the hand, and the second plays it out.
pros: Hands have time to be shaped.
Choices in the first stage affect the second.
cons: A mistake in the first stage sits in the hand.
A hand built for the wrong stage cannot be used.

pairs.tendency: Players state their aims in the first stage, and tricks are played to meet them in the second.
pros: Aims are set before playing.
Hands are fixed before the tricks begin.
cons: A wrong plan shows by the third trick.
A hand fixed in the first stage cannot be swapped once tricks begin.

pairs.tendency: The first stage is a round of talk and deals, and the second is play with what was agreed.
pros: Talk sets up what play will be.
Promises are tested when play starts.
cons: A broken deal can sour the second stage.
Long talks can wear on the table.

pairs.tendency: One stage gathers cards and a later stage turns them into sets for points.
pros: Gathering and scoring are separate jobs.
The second stage has a clear aim.
cons: A set missed in the first stage cannot be bought later.
Gathering can feel long.

pairs.tendency: The first stage lays out the map and the second stage uses it.
pros: The ground is laid before anyone moves on it.
Early tiles decide where play happens.
cons: A tile laid in the first stage may block a plan.
Players in the second stage inherit a map they did not choose.

pairs.tendency: The first stage sets the words or moves, and the second stage chains them in answers.
pros: The first call gives the chain a start.
The rules for answering are clear.
cons: A short first stage leaves little to answer.
Players may run out of things to say.

pairs.tendency: Talk and agreed signals fill the first stage, and the second stage goes silent.
pros: Players can agree on a code.
The silence has a reason.
cons: A code forgotten in the second stage cannot be asked about.
Players who talk a lot may find the silence hard.

pairs.tendency: The first stage fixes a rule set, and the second stage lets players change it.
pros: The rules to change are known.
Changes are made with a plan in mind.
cons: Changes in the second stage may break the first.
Players argue about which rules are open.

pairs.tendency: Characters are made in the first stage, and the scene is played in the second.
pros: Characters have time to form.
The scene has a shape.
cons: Making a character takes a long time before play.
A character who does not fit the scene feels awkward.

pairs.tendency: A tower or a set of targets goes up in the first stage, and the second stage knocks or tests it.
pros: Building and testing are two jobs.
Hands get a rest in between.
cons: A shaky first stage ends the second early.
The build may take longer than the test.

pairs.tendency: The land is drawn in the first stage and lived on in the second.
pros: The map exists before anyone walks it.
Players know the ground.
cons: A map drawn in a hurry limits the second stage.
Drawing may take longer than play.

pairs.tendency: The first stage picks a starting place and the second stage is the race.
pros: Early choices set the starting line.
The race is clear.
cons: A late start can be hard to recover from.
A chosen route might be too long.

pairs.tendency: Resources build up in the first stage, and the second stage counts points from them.
pros: Points depend on early gathering.
The score is not settled until the second stage.
cons: A thin first stage leaves little to count.
Points from the second stage can overturn the first.

pairs.tendency: A calm build comes first, then a fight in which players drop out.
pros: Players enter the fight with a plan.
The knock-outs have a start.
cons: A player with a thin start leaves early.
The first stage can seem a long wait before the fight.

pairs.tendency: Supplies are prepared in the first stage, and the danger is faced together in the second.
pros: Preparing makes the danger easier to take in.
The group has a shared plan.
cons: A shortage from the first stage hurts all.
Preparing may take too long.

pairs.tendency: Parts are gathered in the first stage and assembled towards a goal in the second.
pros: Everyone adds a piece.
The goal is built in steps.
cons: A missing piece shows up late.
Players may blame each other.

pairs.tendency: Secret aims are handed out in the first stage and played towards in the second.
pros: Aims are fixed before moves.
The second stage has a reason for each move.
cons: A secret aim cannot be changed once play starts.
A player who forgets the aim loses the thread.

pairs.tendency: The first stage sets the scene and the second plays to the end of the story.
pros: The beginning has time to settle.
The ending has something to answer.
cons: A long setup delays the story.
A story that changes in the second stage may leave the first unused.

pairs.tendency: The first stage builds something and the second stage looks at it. No winner is needed.
pros: The second stage is a time to look.
Building has a purpose.
cons: Nothing marks the end of the first stage.
Players may not know when to switch.

pairs.tendency: Each player picks a goal in the first stage and plays towards it in the second.
pros: Goals are chosen before play.
The second stage holds many aims.
cons: A goal may seem wrong once play starts.
Players cannot compare their results.

pairs.tendency: A build-up comes first, then a run towards one loser.
pros: Players have something to protect.
The second stage cuts it down.
cons: Players may spend the first stage dreading the second.
The loser is known only at the end.

pairs.tendency: A change of stage can keep the game going by giving it new rules when the first set wears out.
pros: A second stage renews play.
The game does not stop at its first end.
cons: A stage may be hard to leave.
Players who liked the first stage lose it.

pairs.tendency: In a game nobody can win, a change of stage tells players the rules have shifted again.
pros: Each stage shows a new side of the game.
The game refuses a winner in both stages.
cons: Stages do not lead to a finish.
Players may tire of changes with no end.

pairs.tendency: Each player goes through both stages alone, side by side with the others.
pros: Players share a pace but not a board.
Each stage is the same for all.
cons: Players cannot affect each other.
A player who falls behind in the first stage has no help.

pairs.tendency: Forces are prepared in the first stage, and in the second players hit each other.
pros: There is time to prepare before the clash.
The second stage has weight.
cons: A hit in the second stage can undo the first.
Players may feel the first stage was wasted.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage players shape the board, and in the second they feel what others built.
pros: The board holds the first stage's work.
Players see each other's effects.
cons: A block built early can stop a plan late.
Nothing can be changed in between.

pairs.tendency: The group plans together in the first stage and faces the game together in the second.
pros: Planning has a real use.
The group works as one.
cons: The plan may fail on contact.
Players may talk too long in the first stage.

pairs.tendency: Shared supplies are built up first, and then players pull for themselves.
pros: Cooperation comes first and rivalry after.
Private reasons are held back until the second stage.
cons: A group that trusted may be let down.
Players may sabotage in the second stage.

pairs.tendency: Teams prepare in the first stage and are set against each other in the second.
pros: Each team shapes its plan.
The clash has a build-up.
cons: A team with a thin first stage starts behind.
The first stage can be a long wait.

pairs.tendency: Everyone works together in the first stage, and in the second the traitor is named or acts.
pros: Trust is built before it is broken.
The second stage has a twist.
cons: The traitor's plans from the first stage are hard to see.
Players may stop trusting in the second.

pairs.tendency: In a game by post, one stage might take a month of setup and the next a month of play.
pros: Each stage has its own pace.
Waiting is part of the shape.
cons: Players may forget the first stage.
A long wait for a stage to start.

pairs.tendency: The absent player might be present in the first stage and gone in the second, or the other way round.
pros: The game has a past and a present.
The absent player's move is remembered.
cons: The rules for the absent player change.
Players may forget who is missing.

pairs.tendency: The game master runs the first stage as a setup and the second stage as an adventure.
pros: The world is prepared.
Players enter a place that already exists.
cons: The game master has more work in the first stage.
Players wait while the world is made.

pairs.tendency: A street game with stages lets passers-by join at the start of the second.
pros: Newcomers join at a clean point.
Stages give a game a start and a middle.
cons: A newcomer has missed the first stage.
Regulars have to explain.

pairs.tendency: A stage of dice rolls can set up a stage where choices count, or the other way round.
pros: Luck can set the board before choosing starts.
A game of luck can end on a stage of choice.
cons: A low roll in the first stage follows a player.
Choice in the second stage may not count for much.

pairs.tendency: The first stage rolls the dice and the second stage lets players soften the results.
pros: Luck is met by a plan.
Players can see what needs fixing.
cons: Softening a result can feel like repair.
Players may wait for the second stage to fix a roll.

pairs.tendency: The luck comes in the first stage, like a deal, and skill shows in the second.
pros: Players start with luck and then use skill.
Skill has a clear stage.
cons: A lucky start can matter more than skill.
A skilful player may be stuck with a thin deal.

pairs.tendency: Both stages are all choices, so a plan from the first is open to study in the second.
pros: Plans can be read.
Careful players get the most from the stages.
cons: Players who see more of the board win more.
A mistake in the first stage cannot be blamed on luck.

pairs.tendency: A throw is read as a sign in the first stage, and the second stage plays out what it says.
pros: The sign gives the play a start.
A player acts on a message.
cons: Players may argue over what the sign means.
A reading made early may fit badly later.

pairs.tendency: The first stage lets players get to know each other's timing, and the second tests it.
pros: There is time to get in tune.
The second stage shows what was learned.
cons: A stranger who joins late misses it.
Rushing the first stage spoils the second.

pairs.tendency: The first stage rolls up the world and the second stage tells what happens in it.
pros: A rolled world gives the story something to meet.
The tale starts from a surprise.
cons: A strange roll can leave the story with no way in.
The story may drift from the roll.

pairs.tendency: Both stages are open, so every player can see how the first stage sets up the second.
pros: Plans can be read from the first stage.
Nobody is surprised by a rule change.
cons: Nothing is hidden about a choice.
Players can be slow to choose because they see everything.

pairs.tendency: Hidden hands are dealt and built in the first stage, and played out in the second.
pros: A hand is known only to its holder.
The second stage is a reveal.
cons: A hand built for the wrong plan cannot be changed.
Players wait for the second stage to find out.

pairs.tendency: Secret roles are handed out in the first stage and played in the second.
pros: Roles are set before moves.
Players can start slowly.
cons: A role revealed early can wreck the second stage.
Players may spend the first stage guessing.

pairs.tendency: Clues are gathered in the first stage, and in the second players put them together.
pros: Clues can be gathered at leisure.
The second stage has an answer to find.
cons: Players may forget a clue from the first stage.
A missed clue cannot be gathered again.

pairs.tendency: A position to bluff from is built in the first stage, and the bluff comes in the second.
pros: The bluff has something behind it.
Rivals can see the position build.
cons: A bluff fails if the first stage showed too much.
A player who was honest in the first stage may be doubted.

pairs.tendency: A few rules are taught in the open in the first stage, and the second stage hides a rule to be found.
pros: Newcomers get a footing before the secret.
Discovery has a start.
cons: A player who missed the first stage is lost.
The hidden rule may clash with the known ones.

pairs.tendency: The one who knows learns the answer in the first stage and hints at it in the second.
pros: The answer is fixed before hints begin.
The hinting stage is clear.
cons: A hard answer is chosen with no chance to change it.
The hinter holds the secret through a long first stage.

pairs.tendency: Players explore in the first stage and use what they found in the second.
pros: Exploring has a use.
The map is known when it counts.
cons: Explorers who find little reach the second stage short.
Players wait to see what they have found.

pairs.tendency: A turn in the first stage might be a different kind of move from a turn in the second.
pros: Turns change meaning when the stage changes.
The order can be learned once.
cons: Players have to recall which stage they are in.
A long first stage can try patience.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses at once in the first stage, then takes turns in the second.
pros: A fast stage then a slow one.
Nobody waits at the start.
cons: Moving from one to the other can confuse.
Simultaneous choices may be forgotten by the time turns start.

pairs.tendency: There are no turns in the first stage, so anyone can grab, and the second stage may bring turns in.
pros: A rush then a calm.
Quick players get first pick.
cons: Slow players start behind.
Players may be unsure when the second stage starts.

pairs.tendency: A clock can run in the first stage and be taken off in the second, or the other way round.
pros: Fast thinking in one stage and slow in the other.
The change of pace is clear.
cons: A player who likes one pace is slowed in the other.
The untimed stage may seem to drag.

pairs.tendency: The first stage runs over days to set things up, and the second stage runs in a short sitting.
pros: The slow part leaves a mark.
The sitting has a shape.
cons: Players may lose track in the long stage.
A player who misses days falls behind.

pairs.tendency: A slow first stage with a pause before each move can lead to a quick second stage.
pros: The slow stage gives time to think.
The quick stage puts that thinking to use.
cons: Impatient players find the first stage long.
The second stage can feel rushed.

pairs.tendency: Each stage can run faster than the one before, so the end comes quickly.
pros: Pace rises with the stages.
The last stage is short.
cons: Players may not follow the later stages.
Early choices may count more than late ones.

pairs.tendency: The system is set up in the first stage and players act in it in the second.
pros: The system is known before action.
Moves in the second stage show how it works.
cons: A setup error spreads.
Players wait for the system to be built.

pairs.tendency: Groups and their needs are assigned in the first stage, and their dealings are played in the second.
pros: Each group's needs are clear before play.
The dealings have a reason.
cons: A group with thin needs has little to do.
Roles assigned late can feel arbitrary.

pairs.tendency: A shared store is filled in the first stage and drawn from in the second.
pros: The store is known.
Players plan from a clear amount.
cons: A small first stage leaves a short second.
Players may argue over how much is enough.

pairs.tendency: Choices are planted in the first stage whose effects show in the second.
pros: Early moves show up later.
The change of stage marks the delay.
cons: Cause and effect are separated by the stage.
Players may forget what they did.

pairs.tendency: The first stage plays normally and the second stage plays with a new rule, so a table can compare.
pros: The change is visible.
A rule is tested against a plain stage.
cons: Players are in a different frame the second time.
The first stage may colour how the new rule looks.

pairs.tendency: The talk after the game can be a stage of its own, with rules about who speaks and what is asked.
pros: The talk has a place.
Players leave with questions.
cons: Players may be tired by then.
The talk may be hurried.

pairs.tendency: What happens in the first stage leaves marks that the second stage has to use.
pros: Marks tell the story of the game.
The second stage starts from the first one's end.
cons: A mistake cannot be erased.
A new group cannot start fresh.

pairs.tendency: Stages change the rules, so a game can make one point in the first stage and a different one in the second.
pros: The game can argue two things.
Players see the change.
cons: The two points can pull apart.
The argument may be unclear.

pairs.tendency: A change of stage might make the stakes real in the second stage only.
pros: Players practise before the stakes.
The second stage matters.
cons: Players who join late face stakes without practice.
Friends can feel the shift.

pairs.tendency: Points that stand for something that matters are gathered in the first stage, and the second stage asks what they were for.
pros: Players can look at what they chased.
Points have a life and then a test.
cons: The gap between number and value shows.
Players may feel foolish for chasing points.

pairs.tendency: A new way of living is set up in the first stage and tried in the second.
pros: The new way is described before it is lived.
Players know what they are testing.
cons: A way that looks fine on paper may fail in the second stage.
The first stage can run long.

pairs.tendency: Players roll and move, and a rewarding space pays out something that helps the next roll count for more, so early luck snowballs along the track.
pros: Early luck shows how gains compound.
Easy to follow at a glance.
cons: A lucky start can settle the game.
Players behind have little to do.

pairs.tendency: Each card you pick makes the next pick stronger, so players who start a combination keep taking cards for it, and the cards left for others thin out.
pros: Picks build into a plan.
Players see their choices compound.
cons: Early picks lock players in.
Late players are left with scraps.

pairs.tendency: Winning an auction brings money or goods that win the next one, so one player slowly gains the power to outbid everybody else.
pros: Shows how wealth buys more wealth.
Prices tell the story clearly.
cons: One bidder can run away with it.
Poorer players stop bidding.

pairs.tendency: Each safe push earns a reward that makes the next push feel cheaper, so players keep going, and one bust can wipe out a long streak.
pros: Streaks build real tension.
Players feel the pull of the loop.
cons: One bust ends the run.
Careful players never see the loop.

pairs.tendency: Holding an area brings in the pieces that win the next area, so the leader's map keeps growing while others lose ground.
pros: Leads grow in a way players can see.
Map shows where the loop runs.
cons: Early leaders are hard to catch.
Trailing players give up.

pairs.tendency: A rich action space gives you more workers or goods, which lets you take the top spaces first next round.
pros: Planning has a visible payoff.
Players see their engine grow.
cons: Slow starters stay behind all game.
Gains in round one decide round ten.

pairs.tendency: Each piece placed makes the next placement score more, so a small pattern grows into a large one while a messy start stays small.
pros: Patterns reward steady building.
Growth is easy to see.
cons: Early mistakes stay on the board.
A messy start is hard to mend.

pairs.tendency: Cards you play bring cards or points that fill your hand with stronger options, so a strong hand tends to stay strong.
pros: Players plan how to build an engine.
Saving and spending both matter.
cons: Weak hands stay weak.
Leaders are hard to stop.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick lets you lead the next, and the leader picks the suit, so the player who wins early tends to keep winning.
pros: Streaks are easy to read.
Leading matters in every trick.
cons: Losing early is hard to recover from.
Some players only follow.

pairs.tendency: Each deal made leaves a player with more to trade next time, so those who do well in talks gain more bargaining power.
pros: Shows how power gathers around deals.
Talk has lasting effects.
cons: Players who lose a deal lose weight.
Everyone starts to gang up on the leader.

pairs.tendency: Each set you finish unlocks cards or tokens that help finish the next, so one player's collection speeds up while others stall.
pros: Progress feels earned.
Easy to see who is pulling ahead.
cons: A player with no set gets stuck.
Others' sets can be impossible to catch.

pairs.tendency: Each tile you place opens stronger spots for the next, so a connected player builds faster, and a player cut off stays small.
pros: The map shows growth plainly.
Placement choices pay off later.
cons: Cut-off players stay cut off.
The leader's land keeps growing.

pairs.tendency: Each answer feeds the next call, so one player's tone or pace catches on, and the chain grows louder or quieter turn by turn.
pros: Shows how tone spreads in a group.
Players build on each other.
cons: A shy start can shut the chain down.
Loud players set the pace.

pairs.tendency: With no talk, each small signal gets copied by the others, so a pace or a habit spreads through the group without anyone saying so.
pros: Habits spread where everyone can feel them.
Calm way to see a loop.
cons: Players may not notice the loop at all.
One slip can set everyone off course.

pairs.tendency: A rule change that helps its author gives them more power to change the next rule, so the rulebook slowly bends toward one player.
pros: Shows how power writes rules.
Players see rules shape play.
cons: The game can tilt for the rest of play.
Arguments grow.

pairs.tendency: A character's success gives them more standing, and more standing makes the next success easier, so some characters grow while others fade.
pros: Character arcs grow on their own.
Players feel the rise and fall.
cons: Fading characters lose their part.
Players can feel left out of the story.

pairs.tendency: A steady hand builds a tall stack, and a tall stack shakes more, so a long run raises the risk of the next move.
pros: Tension builds with every move.
Easy to explain.
cons: One shake can end a long run.
Nerves spread across the table.

pairs.tendency: Each place a player draws brings people and roads to it, so busy areas keep growing on the page while empty ones stay empty.
pros: The map shows growth as it happens.
Players see their own effects.
cons: Crowded areas hide the rest.
The page can fill up fast.

pairs.tendency: Each card you win tells you more about hands and gives you more to ask for, so the player who asks well keeps asking.
pros: Learning feeds more asking.
Gains are easy to track.
cons: One lucky ask can snowball.
Players who lose cards lose clues too.

pairs.tendency: A winning bet gives you more to wager and a losing one leaves less, so each player's stake grows or shrinks with their last throw.
pros: Shows how stakes compound.
Easy to follow with chips.
cons: Losing players run out of chips.
One streak can end a player's game.

pairs.tendency: A win gives you more to bet, a loss gives you less, so luck on one throw changes how much the next throw can matter.
pros: Stakes rise and fall in plain view.
Quick rounds.
cons: Early losses leave players out.
Chance decides who is left.

pairs.tendency: Chips won in one hand buy bigger bets in the next, so a chip leader can bully the table while short stacks fold early.
pros: Shows how money buys power.
Bluffs gain weight.
cons: Short stacks lose their say.
The chip leader can end hands by betting.

pairs.tendency: Each win lets you add to your army or deck, so a side that starts strong keeps getting stronger, and a weak side struggles.
pros: Players watch their own build grow.
Choices at the start count.
cons: Weak starts are hard to mend.
Wins and builds feed each other.

pairs.tendency: Making a contract earns points and confidence for bolder calls, while a missed one costs enough that the next call gets timid.
pros: Shows how success changes nerve.
Calls reveal how players read themselves.
cons: A miss can shake a player.
Bold callers pull ahead.

pairs.tendency: A capture adds a piece to your side and removes one from theirs, so one strong move pulls the game two ways at once.
pros: Swings are quick and plain to see.
Every capture matters.
cons: The loop can end a game fast.
Players behind give up.

pairs.tendency: Each player caught leaves the team short, making the next catch easier, but a rescue can break the cycle and restore the team.
pros: Rescues give a way out of the loop.
Teams share the swing.
cons: Players in jail wait.
A team can crumble quickly.

pairs.tendency: A group that holds more space can surround more stones, and more captures free up more space, so a lead on the board tends to grow.
pros: Territory shows the loop on the board.
Quiet, slow growth.
cons: Early lead is hard to undo.
Small groups get squeezed.

pairs.tendency: Help for the player behind works against the loop that makes leaders pull away, so each push forward meets a pull back.
pros: Shows one loop balancing another.
Games stay close.
cons: The leader may feel punished.
Help can feel like a rule to dodge.

pairs.tendency: Dice or cards decide each gain, and each gain changes what the next draw is worth, so luck stacks on luck with no player choice to steer it.
pros: Easy to play with no thinking.
The loop is clear to watch.
cons: Players cannot change what happens.
Winners may not learn anything.

pairs.tendency: The tagged player becomes It and chases, so being slow gets you caught and being caught keeps you slow, while fast players stay safe.
pros: Players feel the loop in their legs.
Simple to start.
cons: Slower players stay It.
Some are never free of the chase.

pairs.tendency: The player who is ahead gets picked on, which brings them down, and the one who is hit again and again falls out, so targets feed on themselves.
pros: Shows how a crowd chooses a target.
Picks reveal how players think.
cons: One player can be picked on all game.
Players may gang up for no reason.

pairs.tendency: A chain that has begun to cross the board gets longer with each stone, and the blocking player has to spend moves to cut it.
pros: Progress is easy to see.
One move can swing the whole chain.
cons: The player behind has to keep blocking.
Late cuts can come too late.

pairs.tendency: Each choice beats one and loses to another, so a winning habit gets noticed and countered, and the loop turns round and round.
pros: Shows a loop that corrects itself.
Easy to learn.
cons: Players can go round and round.
A pattern can wear thin.

pairs.tendency: Points from a declared pair buy you tricks or cards, which make more pairs to declare, so a strong hand keeps scoring.
pros: Early points open up more.
Players can plan a run.
cons: Players with no pairs get nothing.
Early declarers get ahead.

pairs.tendency: A player whose power fits the game well gains faster, and each gain makes that power matter more, so some roles run away.
pros: Shows how one edge can grow.
Roles feel different.
cons: Some powers will snowball.
Players with weaker powers feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: A player who is winning doubles the stakes, which raises the cost for the player behind, so a lead can push the other out.
pros: Pressure rises in plain view.
A lead has a use.
cons: Trailing players give up the game.
A double can end play early.

pairs.tendency: A forced capture can pull a piece out of position, which gives the other player a bigger capture next, so one trade can start a chain.
pros: One move can start a chain.
Players learn to read ahead.
cons: Players can be forced into a loss.
A single slip can run on.

pairs.tendency: Each win makes your character stronger, and strength makes the next win easier, so the gap between strong and weak players widens.
pros: Growth feels earned.
Players watch their own rise.
cons: The weak fall far behind.
Late challenges can be too easy or too hard.

pairs.tendency: Every added item makes the list harder to recall, which makes the next slip more likely, and each slip knocks a player out of the loop.
pros: Simple and funny.
Tension builds each round.
cons: One slip ends a run.
The list gets harder on those least able.

pairs.tendency: A start with less gives the weaker player room to gain on a stronger one, so the loop that favours the leader gets a brake.
pros: Shows a loop being balanced.
Close games.
cons: Handicaps can be argued over.
A strong player can feel held back.

pairs.tendency: Each clue found narrows the search and makes the next clue easier, while a hider who is spotted early gets caught fast.
pros: Search speeds up as it goes.
Tension for the hider.
cons: Hiders can lose in seconds.
The end can come quickly.

pairs.tendency: A jump that leaves a piece in a strong spot sets up the next jump, so one strong move can chain into several.
pros: Chains are fun to find.
Players see what one move starts.
cons: Players behind watch long chains.
Early jumps decide a lot.

pairs.tendency: Dice you keep make the next roll easier, so a strong first roll tends to give stronger second and third rolls, and a poor start stays poor.
pros: Each roll builds on the last.
Quick to learn.
cons: A poor first roll is hard to mend.
Luck stacks up.

pairs.tendency: A piece sent back loses ground and so is easier to hit again, while the hitter moves on, so setbacks pile up on one side.
pros: Setbacks are easy to see.
Drama in each landing.
cons: Players hit often can feel picked on.
Comebacks can take a long time.

pairs.tendency: A row lets you take a piece, which makes the other side's rows harder, so the player with the first row has an edge.
pros: One row can start a run.
Players watch both sides.
cons: The first mill is hard to answer.
Losing pieces makes new rows harder.

pairs.tendency: A long word scores more and uses letters that open longer words for you, so the player in the strongest position keeps scoring.
pros: Words build on words.
Players learn each other's vocabulary.
cons: Strong word players pull ahead.
Letters left over can pile up.

pairs.tendency: A tile played shapes the ends the next player has to match, so the loop passes around the table, and a player stuck with no match falls behind.
pros: Easy to follow.
Each tile changes the next move.
cons: Stuck players pass turn after turn.
Hands can end up with no match at all.

pairs.tendency: A set laid down can take more cards from your hand, so a player who melds early builds a larger set and empties their hand faster.
pros: Early sets pay off.
Players watch growth on the table.
cons: Others cannot catch up.
Players with no meld hold on to points.

pairs.tendency: Spending a power early brings a gain that makes later gains easier, but it is gone, so the loop pays out once.
pros: Shows the cost of going early.
Timing matters.
cons: Spent powers cannot be mended.
Early users can run out of steam.

pairs.tendency: The other player's answer to an offer shapes what each side has next, so a gain given or refused feeds on itself over time.
pros: Offers carry weight.
Players read each other closely.
cons: Refusals can start a loop of refusing.
Hard to see who is gaining.

pairs.tendency: Each person who changes a message makes the next change easier to believe, so a small slip grows into a large one by the end.
pros: Shows how small errors grow.
Funny and quick.
cons: Nobody can check it midway.
Players can blame each other.

pairs.tendency: The cards you pass shape the hand your neighbour plays, and their hand shapes what comes back, so a strong pass feeds back to you.
pros: Passing has a lasting effect.
Players notice what they give.
cons: Players pass in the dark.
Hard to trace what went wrong.

pairs.tendency: The split a player makes sets up the whole game, and whichever side is chosen then gains first, so a lopsided split would feed a lasting lead.
pros: Shows why an even start matters.
Starts are fair.
cons: A close split can still feed a lead.
Players spend long on the first step.

pairs.tendency: A piece that reaches the end gains power, and a powerful piece wins more pieces, so one early promotion can tip a whole game.
pros: Gives a reason to push forward.
Strong pieces grow the loop.
cons: The first promotion can decide it.
Players hold back from risk.

pairs.tendency: A team that gets ahead on one leg hands over earlier and starts the next leg with more room, so a small lead tends to grow.
pros: Teams feel the lead build.
Easy to run.
cons: Teams far behind lose heart.
One slow runner affects every leg.

pairs.tendency: A safe shape cannot be captured, so it lets you spend moves elsewhere and build more safe shapes, while a player without one stays under pressure.
pros: Safe ground frees up play.
Players have a clear aim.
cons: Players without shapes feel squeezed.
The first safe shape can decide the game.

pairs.tendency: Winning a named card gives you points and the lead in the next trick, so the player who takes the first prize tends to take more.
pros: Prizes make loops easy to find.
Players plan for the big cards.
cons: Early prizes can decide a hand.
Others can be shut out.

pairs.tendency: Cards in the middle help every player, but the one who uses them most cleverly gains the most, so the lead feeds on shared help.
pros: Everyone gets some help.
Easy to read.
cons: The sharpest player gains from shared cards most.
Others can feel they are feeding the leader.

pairs.tendency: A pot that nobody wins grows, so the next round is worth more, and bigger pots draw bigger risks from every player.
pros: The prize growing is plain to see.
Tension rises each round.
cons: One round can end the game.
Players feel the pull to chase it.

pairs.tendency: Seeds you gather become seeds you can sow, so a big pit feeds the next big sow, and a thin side runs dry.
pros: The loop is easy to see in the pits.
Short turns.
cons: A thin side stays thin.
Players can be cleared out quickly.

pairs.tendency: The extra hand goes to the player who chooses it, and a stronger hand wins more, so the first pick can feed on itself.
pros: Choice at the start has weight.
Players think carefully.
cons: The spare hand can give an early lead.
A poor pick is hard to undo.

pairs.tendency: A bonus square helps you reach the next bonus, and a penalty square holds you back from escaping the next one, so the track pulls both ways.
pros: Squares show the loop plainly.
Easy to learn.
cons: Players stuck on penalties stay stuck.
Luck decides which squares you land on.

pairs.tendency: Spending on a strong item brings in more to spend, so the first player to invest tends to out-buy the rest, while a saver waits.
pros: Shows how investing pays.
Players weigh cost against gain.
cons: Saving too long can lose the lead.
Early buyers pull away.

pairs.tendency: Winning a place where you put most of your force frees your force for the next place, while a loss leaves you thin everywhere.
pros: Shows how winning frees up force.
Every split is a choice.
cons: A loss in one place spreads.
Players can be stretched too thin.

pairs.tendency: Each round the slowest player is caught, and being caught leaves them out of the next, so a slow start can end in a quick exit.
pros: Easy to start.
Lots of movement.
cons: Players out early sit and watch.
The same players are caught.

pairs.tendency: Cards you swap for improve your hand and what you can swap next, so a player with strong options keeps getting stronger ones.
pros: Players shape their own hand.
Swaps are easy to follow.
cons: Rich hands keep growing.
Others can be left with poor choices.

pairs.tendency: A big pile gets bigger as players throw in cards, and the one who picks it up gets a lot to use, so a big pile draws bold plays.
pros: The pile grows in plain view.
Tension builds.
cons: Picking up can swing a whole game.
Players with a big hand stay slow.

pairs.tendency: A player with many trumps wins more tricks, and tricks won give more cards of the trump suit to hold, so strength feeds strength.
pros: Shows why one suit matters.
Plans are easy to set.
cons: Players with no trumps struggle.
The trump suit can be dealt out.

pairs.tendency: A lead on one board gives you pieces and time for the other, so an edge on one board tends to spread to both.
pros: Players watch two loops at once.
Each move counts twice.
cons: Players can lose both at once.
Hard to keep track of two boards.

pairs.tendency: A wild card completes a set that earns more wild cards or points, so the player who gets one early can keep finishing sets.
pros: Wilds make loops easy to start.
Players enjoy using them.
cons: Early wilds can decide a hand.
Players with none feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: With joined edges, a lead can reach round to the other side, so a strong player's reach grows in every direction.
pros: No safe corner exists.
Leads show up all over.
cons: A leader cannot be avoided.
Players cannot run to an edge.

pairs.tendency: Each answer cuts the list of possibilities, and a smaller list makes the next question sharper, so the guesser speeds up as the game goes on.
pros: Answers build on each other.
Easy to start.
cons: Slow early guesses can drag.
A wrong start can mislead for many rounds.

pairs.tendency: Each step forward makes the next step easier for the front runner, so the leader pulls away and the others fall further behind.
pros: The loop is easy to see.
Clear target.
cons: Leaders are hard to catch.
Players behind have little reason to go on.

pairs.tendency: Points earned this round buy things that earn more points next round, so the score gap between players grows each turn.
pros: Scores show the loop clearly.
Players can plan growth.
cons: An early lead can decide the game.
Others may drop out of the race.

pairs.tendency: Each player knocked out takes strength from the others, and the strongest players pick on the weak, so players drop out faster and faster.
pros: Tension rises each round.
A clear end.
cons: Players knocked out wait.
The first one out gets a long wait.

pairs.tendency: Each loss weakens the team's next defence, so a poor turn makes the following turn harder, and a strong turn makes things easier.
pros: Shared tension.
A team can feel a spiral.
cons: Spirals can feel hopeless.
One poor turn can sink everyone.

pairs.tendency: Each step the group makes toward the goal frees up time and means for the next, so progress speeds up once it begins.
pros: Teamwork pays off.
Early steps matter to all.
cons: A slow start is hard to escape.
Players can feel stuck waiting.

pairs.tendency: Each player works toward a secret goal, and each gain makes the next move toward it easier, but nobody can see another's loop.
pros: Mystery makes loops hard to spot.
Players guess at each other's gains.
cons: Hidden loops are hard to stop.
Players can wrongly think they lead.

pairs.tendency: Each event in the story makes the next event more likely, so a happy start tends to stay happy and a sad one deepens.
pros: Story and loop reinforce each other.
Easy to remember.
cons: The story can feel set in advance.
A sad start can turn the story one way.

pairs.tendency: Without a goal the loop still runs, so players see what grows and what fades, and can talk about it with no score to defend.
pros: Players can watch the loop freely.
Calm, slow pace.
cons: Players may not know what to try.
The loop can drift with no purpose.

pairs.tendency: A player who sets a goal they can reach feels the reward, and aims higher next time, while a distant goal can feel out of reach.
pros: Players learn from their own gains.
Goals suit each person.
cons: Easy goals teach little.
Hard to compare players.

pairs.tendency: The player falling behind gets less to work with, which keeps them behind, so one loser tends to show early and stay the loser.
pros: The slide is plain to see.
Everyone else is safe.
cons: Early losers sit out the rest.
One player takes all the weight.

pairs.tendency: The more players join in, the more there is to keep going, so energy feeds itself, and a few drop-outs can pull others down.
pros: Shows how a group keeps itself going.
Players feel part of a whole.
cons: A few dropouts can end it.
A group may carry on after it is fun.

pairs.tendency: The loop runs with no winner to stop it, so players watch gains and losses grow and learn that no move ends the cycle.
pros: Makes the loop the point.
Players notice more.
cons: Players may feel the game is pointless.
The loop can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: Each card cleared opens more moves, but a stuck layout closes them, so the game tends to run smoothly or jam.
pros: Easy to play alone.
Progress feeds progress.
cons: A jam can end the game early.
Early choices can seal a loss.

pairs.tendency: A win in game one gives the winner confidence and the loser a push to change plans, so the loop can run across games.
pros: Players learn between games.
Loops show over many rounds.
cons: A winner can run away with the set.
A loser can give up early.

pairs.tendency: Points taken early make later moves harder, so the player with the most points has to take even more, while a clean start stays clean.
pros: Gains show as costs.
Easy to read.
cons: Early points are hard to shed.
Players behind may give up.

pairs.tendency: Getting near the target makes every move a risk, so the player closest to the target moves least and the others catch up.
pros: A lead can slow itself down.
Tension near the end.
cons: Leaders can wait many turns.
A lead can slip away.

pairs.tendency: A player who gives away pieces gains room to give more away, so the loop runs toward emptiness, and the winner is the one who gets there first.
pros: The loop runs backward.
Players enjoy the twist.
cons: Players may mix up what grows.
Rules can be hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: Each player runs a loop of their own, so a gain at one place does not change the others, and gaps show from comparing side by side.
pros: Players can compare loops.
Calm, steady play.
cons: Little to do with others.
Gaps grow without anyone to stop them.

pairs.tendency: An attack takes something from one player and gives it to another, so the winner of a fight gets stronger for the next, and the loser weaker.
pros: Conflict has visible effects.
Players feel each hit.
cons: Losers can be picked on.
Fights can take over the game.

pairs.tendency: Each move changes the board for the next player, so one player's growth shapes what the others can do, with no attack at all.
pros: Shows loops without fighting.
Quiet, clear links.
cons: Effects can be hard to trace.
Players may blame the board.

pairs.tendency: When the whole team gains, every player has more to give, and when it loses, every player has less, so team morale rides on the loop.
pros: Everyone shares the swing.
Teamwork shows.
cons: A team can slide fast.
One person can steer the others.

pairs.tendency: Gains that help the team also help whoever takes them, so players enjoy the shared loop but each pulls it toward themselves.
pros: Shows self and group pulling apart.
Interesting trust choices.
cons: Selfish play can stop the loop.
Players can suspect each other.

pairs.tendency: A team that gets ahead has more help and so pulls further ahead, while the other team has to work harder to hold on.
pros: Teams feel the swing together.
Talk inside each team.
cons: Trailing teams can lose heart.
One strong player can run the loop.

pairs.tendency: The traitor's damage makes the team's next turn harder, so one sabotage gives the saboteur more room, and the team sinks.
pros: Suspicion grows with each loss.
Tense and suspicious.
cons: Players may blame the loop, not the traitor.
Wrong accusations can add to the spiral.

pairs.tendency: Each letter answers the last and sets up the next, so a friendly note leads to friendlier ones and a sharp note makes the reply sharper.
pros: Tone builds over weeks.
Slow and thoughtful.
cons: A cold letter can be hard to take back.
Waiting makes loops hard to see.

pairs.tendency: The absent player cannot react, so the loop runs only on what the others do for them, and gains or losses can pile up unchecked.
pros: Shows a loop with no one steering.
Players think of the missing one.
cons: The absent player cannot answer back.
Loops can run unchecked.

pairs.tendency: The game master's reply to each move sets the next, so a bold move may be met with more openings, and a poor one with more trouble.
pros: Players feel the world answer.
Every choice has an echo.
cons: One person shapes the whole loop.
Players can feel steered.

pairs.tendency: A game in a street draws onlookers, who draw more, so a crowd can grow around a lively game and vanish when it dies down.
pros: Shows how interest feeds itself.
Easy to join.
cons: A quiet game can lose everyone.
Hard to run when the crowd grows.

pairs.tendency: The lone player gets paid more for winning, and every win makes the next easier, while the team starts to fall out.
pros: Payoffs raise the stakes.
Clear sides.
cons: The team can fall apart.
The lone player can be buried by early losses.

pairs.tendency: You play against a loop with no one to compare against, so an early gain or loss runs on to the end of the game.
pros: Easy to set up.
The loop is easy to follow.
cons: A poor start leaves nobody to help.
Little to compare with others.

pairs.tendency: Luck gives a gain that changes the next roll's worth, so players watch the loop run with almost no say in it.
pros: The loop shows plainly.
Light and quick.
cons: Players feel their choices do not matter.
Early luck decides most of it.

pairs.tendency: Poor luck feeds a loop of loss, but a re-roll or a saved card can stop it, so players learn when to step in.
pros: Players can break a loop.
Some control.
cons: Rules for stopping can be many.
A stop can come too late.

pairs.tendency: A skilled player turns small gains into bigger ones, and luck now and then shakes the loop up, so skill grows but not without surprises.
pros: Skill is rewarded in the loop.
Surprise keeps it lively.
cons: Skilled players still pull ahead.
Beginners lose ground quickly.

pairs.tendency: Each strong move leads to a stronger position, and a mistake feeds the other player, so the gap between players grows with every move.
pros: Every result has a reason.
Players learn from mistakes.
cons: A single slip can decide a game.
Beginners fall behind fast.

pairs.tendency: A throw read as a sign shapes what a player does next, and what they do next shapes how the next sign is read, so meaning feeds itself.
pros: Shows how belief grows from signs.
Players reflect.
cons: A reading can feed on itself.
Players can take it too far.

pairs.tendency: When players stay in step, each reads the others more easily, so closeness grows, while a missed beat makes the next beat harder to catch.
pros: Closeness shows quickly.
Warm and close.
cons: A slip can shake the group.
Hard to tell why it broke.

pairs.tendency: A roll on the table shapes the story, and the story changes which table is used next, so one lucky roll can steer many scenes.
pros: Dice open new directions.
Stories surprise players.
cons: One roll can steer too much.
Hard to tell the loop from chance.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees how each gain feeds the next, so the leader's growth is plain, and the others can plan to stop it.
pros: Loops can be read and discussed.
Fair to everyone.
cons: Players can see the loss coming.
Little surprise.

pairs.tendency: A hand that grows stronger stays hidden, so players cannot see a loop building and only learn of it when it pays out.
pros: Surprise when it pays out.
Keeps an air of mystery.
cons: Players cannot plan against the loop.
A hidden leader can surprise everyone.

pairs.tendency: A player with a secret role gains more as the group's trust grows, so a trusted player can keep making trust work for them.
pros: Shows how trust can be used.
Tense and wary.
cons: Players cannot tell loop from lie.
Early trust can decide who wins.

pairs.tendency: Each clue found helps in finding the next, so the player who solves one part tends to solve the rest fast.
pros: Clues build on clues.
Satisfying when it clicks.
cons: One slow start can lose a hunt.
A leader may be copied by everyone.

pairs.tendency: A bluff that works makes the next bluff easier to believe, while a bluff caught makes every claim harder to trust.
pros: Shows how trust rises and falls.
Players watch faces.
cons: One caught bluff can ruin a player.
Lying can run out of control.

pairs.tendency: Each rule learned helps find the next, so players who learn fast learn faster, while those who break a rule early learn little.
pros: Learning builds on itself.
Easy for the knower to run.
cons: Slow learners fall further behind.
The knower can feel too important.

pairs.tendency: Each hint that lands helps the guessers read the next, so a strong start tends to build, and a poor start gets stuck.
pros: A hint can open the game up.
Quiet fun.
cons: A wrong first read can mislead.
The hint giver can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: A rich find reveals more map and more finds, so lucky explorers go further while the unlucky see only dead ends.
pros: Exploring feels rewarded.
Surprises keep coming.
cons: Early finds can decide the game.
Unlucky players can run out of map.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows how a loop could grow, so players can see a gain feed itself and plan their own around it.
pros: Learning from an open hand.
Easy to follow.
cons: Hands can feel played for you.
Others can copy the plan.

pairs.tendency: A growing score stays hidden, so players cannot see who is pulling away, and a leader can keep gaining without anyone noticing.
pros: Nobody can tell who is ahead.
Keeps an air of mystery.
cons: Players can feel in the dark.
The end can be a shock.

pairs.tendency: Each turn builds on the last, so the loop runs one step at a time, and players watch another player's gain before their own turn.
pros: The loop is easy to follow.
Time to think.
cons: Waiting while a leader pulls ahead.
The leader gets many turns of advantage.

pairs.tendency: Everyone gains at the same moment, so the loop runs for every player together, and the gaps between them grow without anyone seeing.
pros: The loop runs for all at once.
Quick to play.
cons: Hard to see who is gaining.
Players can miss early signs.

pairs.tendency: The quickest player grabs more, which makes them quicker again, so fast players run the loop and slow ones are left out.
pros: Speed and gain feed each other.
Lively and loud.
cons: Slow players barely take part.
A fast start decides it.

pairs.tendency: A player who is behind has less time to think, which makes mistakes, which puts them further behind, while a calm leader gets calmer.
pros: Pressure shows in the loop.
Quick play.
cons: A rush can cause mistakes.
Slower players fall behind.

pairs.tendency: Moves made over days build on each other, so a small gain on day one is still growing by the end, and a slip is seen for weeks.
pros: Loops show over a long time.
Players come back to see.
cons: Players can forget the loop.
Early moves outweigh late ones.

pairs.tendency: A slower game gives players time to watch a loop and see each gain feed the next, and each pause can help them tell what drives it.
pros: Players can see the loop clearly.
Calm, thoughtful pace.
cons: Slow play can feel dull.
The loop can pass unnoticed in the wait.

pairs.tendency: The game speeds up as it goes, so gains and losses come quicker, and the loop runs faster until it ends in a rush.
pros: Pace and loop rise together.
Exciting end.
cons: Players cannot keep up.
A leader can run away at the end.

pairs.tendency: A lucky extra turn brings gains that may bring another, so one player can take many moves in a row while others wait.
pros: Shows a loop in a burst.
Exciting final stretch.
cons: Others can watch for a long time.
A run can end a game.

pairs.tendency: What you gain in the first stage sets how strong you start the second, so an early lead carries into the later rules.
pros: The first stage has weight.
Players plan for both.
cons: A poor first stage is hard to mend.
The second stage can feel decided.

pairs.tendency: The board works like a real system, so a gain feeds the next gain the way it would in life, such as more farms bringing more money for farms.
pros: Players learn how real loops grow.
Cause and effect show clearly.
cons: Players may race the loop and not study it.
Leaders are hard to catch.

pairs.tendency: Each group's gain gives it more say, and more say wins it more gain, so the strong groups keep growing, as real groups with power tend to.
pros: Shows how power gathers.
Each role feels a different loop.
cons: Weak groups can feel shut out.
Players can feel unfairly treated.

pairs.tendency: The more one player takes, the more they can take next, while the shared stock shrinks, so the loop speeds up as it runs down.
pros: Shows how a shared stock is drained.
Everyone feels the cost.
cons: Players may take quickly to be first.
The stock can run out before anyone sees it.

pairs.tendency: A gain today builds a loop whose bigger effect arrives rounds later, so players act without seeing the full result of their move.
pros: Players learn to look ahead.
Shows how loops can surprise.
cons: Players can lose the thread.
Cause and effect are hard to link.

pairs.tendency: A new rule may help one side gain, and the gain makes the rule matter more, so players see a rule's effect grow over several rounds.
pros: Safe place to test a rule.
Players see its effects build.
cons: A rule can feel judged too soon.
A strong player can bend the rule.

pairs.tendency: After play, the talk can trace which gains fed which, so players name the loop they were in and where it could have turned.
pros: Players name the loop.
Links to real life come out.
cons: Players may blame each other.
Short talks miss the loop.

pairs.tendency: A gain that cannot be undone is carried into the next game, so the loop stretches across many games and players inherit their last result.
pros: Loops carry over between games.
Choices feel heavy.
cons: A poor game affects later ones.
New players join at a disadvantage.

pairs.tendency: The rules reward gains that feed more gains, which says something about the world, such as that wealth tends to gather.
pros: The loop makes a point.
Players can argue about it.
cons: Players can feel lectured.
The point may be too plain.

pairs.tendency: A loop that favours one player can carry into real life, such as who always gets the seat by the window, so the loop's effect stays after the game.
pros: Players see the loop touch real life.
Choices feel weighty.
cons: A leader can carry the win home.
Hard to stop a real loop.

pairs.tendency: Points earned for something that matters help earn more points, so players may chase the number and the value behind it can fade.
pros: Shows how numbers take over.
Easy to see the pull.
cons: The value can drop out.
Players may enjoy the loop too much.

pairs.tendency: Players see how a new way of living might feed itself, such as sharing making more sharing, or fail if trust drops.
pros: Players feel how change can grow.
A safe test.
cons: A short game may hide long loops.
Loops may feel too tidy.

pairs.tendency: A loop runs quietly until it crosses a line, then it speeds up, so a slow build suddenly turns into a collapse or a boom.
pros: Shows why small gains can matter.
Sudden turns feel real.
cons: The line can pass unnoticed.
Players can feel it was out of their hands.

pairs.tendency: A stock grows because it is large, such as debt adding interest, and the loop makes the pile bigger each turn.
pros: Piles show the loop plainly.
Players watch it grow.
cons: Piles can grow past control.
Hard to bring a stock down.

pairs.tendency: Between turns the system moves by a fixed rule, and the rule feeds on what players did, so the world pushes a loop on without anyone choosing it.
pros: Shows the loop running on its own.
Players see their effect later.
cons: Players can feel they have little say.
Some may blame the rule.

pairs.tendency: A shock hits the weakest hardest, which leaves them less able to face the next, so one event can set off a run of losses.
pros: Shows how shocks spread.
Players have to respond together.
cons: Shocks can seem unfair.
Players can feel crushed.

pairs.tendency: A round covers a long span, so a loop shows its full growth in a few turns, such as a farm's income compounding over a decade.
pros: Years pass in minutes.
Slow loops become clear.
cons: Details are squeezed out.
Players may miss the small steps.

pairs.tendency: A gauge rising feeds the next move, so players watch the loop move on the dial and learn which actions push it up or down.
pros: Loops are easy to read.
Players can discuss together.
cons: Players can watch a dial instead of thinking.
The gauge can hide what causes it.

pairs.tendency: Players with more at the start gain more, and more gain brings still more, so the loop widens a gap that was there from the beginning.
pros: Shows how a small gap grows.
Feels true to life.
cons: Poorer players may give up.
Rich players may feel it is not earned.

pairs.tendency: Whoever is ahead writes rules that help them stay ahead, so the loop gets stronger each time the leader changes a rule.
pros: Shows how power protects itself.
Players feel the unfairness.
cons: Players behind can lose heart.
The game can stop being playable.

pairs.tendency: Each role's gain can feed its own goal and hurt another's, so the loops pull against each other, such as catch and fish stock.
pros: Shows opposing loops.
Players know why they clash.
cons: Players can get stuck in a standoff.
One loop can swamp the others.

pairs.tendency: The opening situation decides which loops start, such as who has the money and who has the land, and players see them run from the first move.
pros: Players see where loops start.
Easy to begin.
cons: The start can seem to decide all.
Players may think the end was set.

pairs.tendency: A move that is argued well gives a player credit, and credit helps win the next argument, so talkers can feed their own influence.
pros: Players practise making a case.
Loops form around persuasion.
cons: Quiet players lose ground.
The judge can be swayed.

pairs.tendency: Each pause lets players spot a loop while it runs, so they may change course before a gain or loss gathers pace.
pros: Loops can be named in time.
Players learn as they go.
cons: Pauses can break the flow.
A pause can come too late to help.

pairs.tendency: Players run the game twice with one change, and compare how the loop grew each time, so the effect of that change shows.
pros: Shows which change matters.
Players can test an idea.
cons: Needs time to play twice.
Players may remember too much from the first game.

pairs.tendency: The game says which loops it has kept and which it left out, so players know the real system has others that could change the result.
pros: Players know where the model ends.
Honest about its limits.
cons: Players can dismiss the whole model.
A list of gaps can feel long.

pairs.tendency: The people who live the situation check that the loops feel true, such as farmers saying how debt really feeds on itself.
pros: Loops ring true to those who live them.
Players learn from the experts.
cons: Design takes longer.
Different people may see different loops.

pairs.tendency: A late order makes the next link hold more stock, which makes its next order larger, so a small change at the shop swells up the chain.
pros: Shows how small orders grow upstream.
Every link feels the others.
cons: Players blame the link next to them.
Hard to see the cause from one seat.

pairs.tendency: Each player sees only their own part of the loop, so a gain or loss spreads without anyone seeing the whole, and each has to guess.
pros: Shows why loops are hard to see.
Players learn to ask questions.
cons: Players can feel in the dark.
Players may blame the wrong link.

pairs.tendency: A slow step makes work pile up before it, and the pile slows the steps before it too, so one bottleneck can spread through the whole line.
pros: Shows where the loop is stuck.
Players find the real cause.
cons: Speeding up other steps wastes effort.
One player can hold up the rest.

pairs.tendency: Goods pushed down the line pile up in stock, which delays new orders and makes the next batch a guess, while pull-made goods follow demand.
pros: Shows how pushing and pulling differ.
Players feel the stock.
cons: Pulling can leave shelves empty.
Pushed stock can swamp the line.

pairs.tendency: A big batch fills the line, which makes later batches wait longer, so choosing big or small feeds into delay, stock and cost.
pros: Players see the cost of big batches.
Choices have clear effects.
cons: Small batches can mean many set-ups.
Waiting can pile up before anyone notices.

pairs.tendency: A breakdown delays the next step, which backs up stock and slows repairs, so one failure can start a run of failures on the line.
pros: Shows how one failure spreads.
Players plan for trouble.
cons: Random breaks can feel unfair.
Plans can fall apart at once.

pairs.tendency: Running out causes lost sales and less money for stock, while holding too much costs every round, so each mistake feeds the next.
pros: Players feel both sides of the loop.
Balance is easy to see.
cons: One mistake can lead to another.
Players can swing between too much and too little.

pairs.tendency: Players roll and move round the track while a slow change builds on the board, and one roll that carries it over the line flips everything at once.
pros: Easy to follow while the change builds.
The sudden flip is hard to forget.
cons: Dice make the crossing moment feel random.
Players may blame luck, not the slow build.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards each round that nudge a slow change a little further, and one late pick tips the whole table into something new.
pros: Small picks add up in plain view.
Everyone shares in the final push.
cons: Nobody feels responsible for the last pick.
Early picks seem to do almost nothing.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for things that each push a slow change along, and the bid that pushes it past the line changes what every later bid is worth.
pros: Prices show the pressure rising.
Late bids feel tense.
cons: Bidders may hold back and wait for others.
The flip can come as a surprise.

pairs.tendency: Each extra push adds a little to a slow change that seems harmless, until one push crosses the line and the whole board turns at once.
pros: Every extra push feels more daring.
The turning point is tense.
cons: Careful players may never see the line.
The flip can feel unfair to the one who pushed.

pairs.tendency: Players take areas on a map while a slow change spreads under them, and one area going over the line sends the change across the whole map.
pros: Links between places show up clearly.
Early quiet play pays off later.
cons: Fighting over areas can hide the slow change.
Whoever holds the last area takes the blame.

pairs.tendency: Workers go onto action spaces that each add a little to a slow change, and one placement that crosses the line changes what every space does.
pros: Small jobs add up to something large.
Planning around a coming flip feels real.
cons: Players can miss that the line is near.
Blocked spaces slow the build-up unevenly.

pairs.tendency: Players build patterns piece by piece while a slow change creeps in, and one piece that completes the shape changes the whole pattern at once.
pros: The slow build is easy to watch.
The final piece lands with weight.
cons: Calm building can hide the line.
The flip can undo many turns of work.

pairs.tendency: Players hold cards and play them one by one into a slow change, and the card that crosses the line changes what the rest of every hand can do.
pros: Saving cards feels weighty near the line.
Planning around the flip is rewarding.
cons: Players hold back, so the line stays far off.
The flip can make held cards useless.

pairs.tendency: Each trick adds a little to a slow change, and the trick that crosses the line changes the value of every card still to be played.
pros: Tricks carry meaning beyond who wins them.
A late flip keeps play tense.
cons: The slow change is easy to forget in a trick.
Late players cannot respond to the flip.

pairs.tendency: Players trade and promise while a slow change builds, and talk turns urgent when someone sees the line, because one deal can tip it.
pros: Deals feel urgent near the line.
Players talk about shared warning signs.
cons: Talk can drift from the slow change.
Each side blames the other after the flip.

pairs.tendency: Players collect sets while a slow change adds up in the background, and the set that crosses the line changes what the other sets are worth.
pros: Collecting gives a calm start.
Late sets feel important.
cons: Collecting can take attention from the change.
Half-built sets can lose their value at once.

pairs.tendency: Players lay tiles that each add a little to a slow change on the map, and one tile that crosses the line changes the whole landscape at once.
pros: The change grows in front of everyone.
Each tile carries a small cost.
cons: Tile luck can hide who caused the flip.
The final tile can feel unearned.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other in a chain while a slow change builds in what is said, until one reply shifts the whole tone of the game.
pros: Small answers add up quietly.
The shift is felt by everyone.
cons: The line is hard to see in words.
The chain can break when it flips.

pairs.tendency: Nobody speaks while a slow change builds, so players sense the line only from each other's moves, and one card crosses it with no warning.
pros: Shared silence makes the flip dramatic.
Players pay close attention to each other.
cons: Nobody can warn the others.
The flip can feel like a trick.

pairs.tendency: Players change rules one at a time, each with little effect alone, until one rule crosses the line and the game becomes something else.
pros: Players watch small rules add up.
The flip is a shared surprise.
cons: Rule changes can hide the line.
A late flip can cancel earlier rules.

pairs.tendency: Characters go on with their lives while a slow change builds around them, and one action crosses the line, so the story turns at once.
pros: Slow change feels real through a character.
A turning point gives the story weight.
cons: The group may not notice the build-up.
The flip can override what a character chose.

pairs.tendency: Players stack, flick or balance while a slow change builds, such as a tower leaning more each turn, and one touch crosses the line and everything falls.
pros: Everyone can see the line coming.
The collapse is loud and shared.
cons: Shaky hands can crash it too early.
The flip is physical, not chosen.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the map as they go while a slow change builds on the page, and one added line crosses the threshold and changes what the whole map means.
pros: The change is visible on paper.
Players share the story of the flip.
cons: Drawn changes are hard to measure.
Players may not agree on where the line was.

pairs.tendency: Players ask each other for cards while a slow change builds in what is known, and one answer crosses the line and exposes everyone's hand at once.
pros: Questions slowly reveal what others hold.
The reveal moment is sharp.
cons: Asking can hide the slow change.
One answer can make the rest of the game dull.

pairs.tendency: Players bet against a bank while a slow change shifts the odds a little each round, until one throw crosses the line and the odds change for the rest of the game.
pros: Shifting odds can be watched and worked out.
The flip hits bank and bettors together.
cons: Odds drift too slowly to notice.
The player holding the bank takes the blame.

pairs.tendency: Players bet on each throw while a slow change adds to the stakes, and one throw crosses the line and changes what every later bet means.
pros: Bets show who senses the line.
Late throws feel heavy.
cons: Nobody can steer a throw, so the flip is luck.
Bettors cannot tell if the line is near.

pairs.tendency: Players bet on hidden hands while a slow change raises the pot, and one raise crosses the line and makes dropping out cost far more.
pros: Rising bets show the pressure building.
The crossing is a tense moment.
