pairs.tendency: You play every year yourself, so a whole lifetime passes at your own pace and you can compare your years with a friend's afterwards.
pros: You set the pace of the years.
Comparing afterwards is easy.
cons: Nobody to share the years with.
Years can pass with no surprise.

pairs.tendency: Dice decide most years, so the span reads like weather with lean and rich times nobody earned, and skill barely changes a year.
pros: Years feel like weather.
Quick rounds across a long span.
cons: Players do not shape their own years.
Little to learn from a year.

pairs.tendency: Luck brings hard years, but players can soften them, so a long span shows who prepared and who did not.
pros: Preparing for hard years pays off.
Players can recover from a hard run.
cons: Softening costs something every year.
Luck can still undo careful years.

pairs.tendency: Choices shape most years with a little luck on top, so a long span rewards steady play but still holds surprises, as real years do.
pros: Steady choices count over many years.
Surprise keeps years from repeating.
cons: Early luck can echo for years.
Tracking skill over a long span is hard.

pairs.tendency: With no dice, each year follows from earlier choices, so a long span shows exactly what each player did and there is no weather to blame.
pros: Each year follows from the one before.
Plans can be traced over decades.
cons: Years can feel too cold.
One early slip stays for the whole span.

pairs.tendency: Each year's throw is read as a message, so players give every season a meaning and look back to see what the signs said.
pros: Years take on meaning as signs.
Looking back adds a story.
cons: Meaning may be forced onto chance.
Players may read the same sign differently.

pairs.tendency: Players sense when others are about to act, so a long span of shared years builds a quiet understanding, as friends learn one another.
pros: Years together build understanding.
No dice to blame.
cons: A year gives little to see.
New players have no shared years.

pairs.tendency: Each year's roll is looked up on a table that says what happens, so the table writes the span of years, one event after another.
pros: A table gives each year its event.
Years read like a story.
cons: Table events may repeat across years.
The table sets the story, not the players.

pairs.tendency: Everything is open each year, so players can see how every year changed the whole board and trace the long span back step by step.
pros: Every year can be traced.
Players see how change adds up.
cons: Open boards can feel like a spreadsheet.
Many years make a lot to take in.

pairs.tendency: Cards stay hidden while the years pass, so players guess what others are planning and a year may show only part of what happened.
pros: Hidden plans give each year suspense.
Looking back reveals what was held.
cons: Players cannot tell what a year held.
Hidden cards can sit unused for many years.

pairs.tendency: Roles stay secret across the years, so a quiet year may hide a plan and the long span gives a spy time to work.
pros: Long spans give secrets time.
Looking back changes what a year meant.
cons: Players may wait for years doing nothing.
A late reveal can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: A clue comes in each year, so players piece together what happened over a long span as an investigator does.
pros: Clues pile up over years.
Looking back makes sense of the span.
cons: Some years bring few clues.
Players may lose the thread.

pairs.tendency: Each year players claim more or less than they hold, so a long run of claims is tested against what the years prove.
pros: Claims are tested over time.
Bluffs are remembered across years.
cons: Early lies can unravel later.
Long spans give a lot to remember.

pairs.tendency: Players learn the secret rule by breaking it, so years go by while they find out what the world allows, like learning how a new place works.
pros: Learning feels like growing up.
Rules found over years stay known.
cons: Early years can be frustrating.
Players may not guess the rule in time.

pairs.tendency: One player knows how the years go but cannot say, so hints stand in for history and the others work out what the long span held.
pros: Hints turn years into puzzles.
One player holds the whole span.
cons: Hints cannot cover many years.
Players may guess wrongly.

pairs.tendency: Areas are revealed year by year, so exploration takes seasons and the map becomes a record of what each year found.
pros: Each year reveals more.
Exploration feels slow, as it is.
cons: Unknown areas wait a long time.
Early years show little.

pairs.tendency: One hand lies face up, so players see what that figure does across the years and can plan around it while their own hands stay secret.
pros: The open hand shows one path across years.
Players plan around a known path.
cons: The open hand can steer all the years.
Players may ignore it.

pairs.tendency: Scores stay secret across the years, so nobody knows who is ahead until the end and a long span finishes in surprise.
pros: Years end in a surprise.
Players guess who is ahead.
cons: Players cannot tell how a year went.
Guessing can mislead for years.

pairs.tendency: One player acts each year in turn, so the long span is told in order and each player's year follows the last.
pros: Years follow in a clear order.
Each player's year is told.
cons: Waiting while other years pass.
One slow year holds up the rest.

pairs.tendency: All players choose a year's move together, so the span moves as one, like a village deciding the season's planting at the same time.
pros: A year happens for everyone at once.
Nobody waits for their year.
cons: Choices cannot answer each other within a year.
Many choices at once are hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: Anyone may act at any moment, so a year is whatever happens before time is called and the span feels like events piling up.
pros: Years feel busy and alive.
Quick players meet every moment.
cons: A year is hard to mark.
Slow players fall behind the years.

pairs.tendency: A clock limits each year, so a long span is lived under pressure and each year is decided before it is thought through.
pros: Time pressure makes years feel short.
Rounds stay brisk.
cons: Rushed years can feel wrong.
Clock time and year time get mixed up.

pairs.tendency: The game runs over real days or weeks while each round also stands for a year, so two kinds of time overlap and waiting is part of play.
pros: Real waiting makes years feel long.
Players can think between moves.
cons: Two kinds of time can confuse.
Players may drop out over weeks.

pairs.tendency: The game is slowed on purpose, so each year takes a breath and the span feels long, with a pause before every move.
pros: Years feel like years.
Pauses let players notice change.
cons: A slow year can feel dull.
A long game may never reach its end.

pairs.tendency: The game speeds up as it goes, so years pass faster each round and the last decades rush by in a few turns.
pros: Late years rush like old age.
Tension rises as time shrinks.
cons: Early years get more care than late ones.
Rushing hides what the later years held.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets one player pass several years while the others wait, so one player's span can run ahead of the rest.
pros: Luck can move a player years ahead.
Extra turns surprise.
cons: Others wait while years pass for one player.
Players' years run out of step.

pairs.tendency: The game comes in stages with different rules, so each stage is an era and what you built in one carries into the next.
pros: Each stage feels like an era.
Early choices set up later eras.
cons: A stage change can feel sudden.
Players have to relearn rules between eras.

pairs.tendency: The board copies a real system and each round is a year, so water, soil or prices change at about the pace the real thing does.
pros: Systems show their real slow pace.
A lifetime of change fits in an afternoon.
cons: A year skips what happens inside it.
Players may take the model for the real thing.

pairs.tendency: Each group plays its own year, so a farmer's year is a harvest and a council's year is a budget, and one round carries all of them.
pros: Each role sees its own year.
Different years sit side by side.
cons: One round cannot hold every year's details.
Roles may not agree what a year is.

pairs.tendency: A year's taking from the common stock adds up, so over many years the water or fish runs low and the slow slide shows only in hindsight.
pros: Slow loss shows over years.
Players see how a common stock is shared.
cons: A single year looks harmless.
Warning signs can come too late.

pairs.tendency: What you do now shows up some years later, and a round is a year, so the delay is counted in rounds players have to wait through.
pros: Waits feel like years.
Players see cause and effect over time.
cons: Players forget old choices.
A long delay can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: A new rule is tried for a stretch of years, so players watch how it works out over a decade rather than a single turn.
pros: A rule's effect shows over years.
Players test before trying it for real.
cons: A short test may miss late effects.
Early rounds may not show the change.

pairs.tendency: After the years have passed, players talk through what happened, and the round-by-round record helps them say which year things turned.
pros: Looking back is easier with years marked.
Players can say which year mattered.
cons: Many years to recall.
Talk can drift from the real thing.

pairs.tendency: A change made in one year stays for all the years after, so a torn card or a sticker on the board marks one season's choice for ever.
pros: Marks of old years stay on the board.
Each year's choice feels weighty.
cons: One year's slip lasts a whole span.
The next game begins with the old marks.

pairs.tendency: The rules say what each year is worth, so how a game counts time makes a point about growth, loss and patience.
pros: Years are shaped to make a point.
Players can read the argument in how time is counted.
cons: Players may disagree with how years are counted.
The point can hide behind the fast pace.

pairs.tendency: What is staked is real, but the game runs through many years in an afternoon, so real promises meet fast, made-up time.
pros: Real stakes make a short span matter.
Players take the years seriously.
cons: Real friends can feel hurt by quick years.
Real money against pretend time can sting.

pairs.tendency: Each year adds or takes points that stand for something like health, so players watch a value rise and fall across a lifetime.
pros: A value's rise and fall is visible.
Players feel what years cost.
cons: Players chase points, not the value.
Years get reduced to numbers.

pairs.tendency: Players live through years of a way of life that does not exist yet, so a decade of sharing fits into an afternoon and can be felt in advance.
pros: A future can be felt in an afternoon.
Years show where it may hold or crack.
cons: A year is a thin stand-in for a real one.
Things that take decades cannot be tried.

pairs.tendency: Gauges update each year, so players read the water level or trust as a line over many rounds and see the slow trend.
pros: Trends show over years.
Everyone reads the same gauge.
cons: A gauge hides what happened inside a year.
Players may watch gauges, not each other.

pairs.tendency: Players begin with different land or money, so years pass at different speeds for each of them and the gap can widen or close over a long span.
pros: Years treat players differently, as in life.
Gaps can be watched widening.
cons: Players with little may give up.
Starting gaps can dominate many years.

pairs.tendency: Whoever leads writes the rules for the next years, so rule-making builds up over a long span and shapes what later years allow.
pros: Rules written by the leader show power over time.
Players see how a lead is kept.
cons: Rule changes pile up over many years.
Players behind may feel shut out.

pairs.tendency: Each role measures a year by its own goal, so the same year looks like a gain to one role and a loss to another.
pros: One year reads two ways.
Roles see how others weigh time.
cons: Years can end in argument.
One goal may rule over many years.

pairs.tendency: The opening situation sets year one and every later round follows from it, so a long span grows from a few lines of set-up.
pros: A clear year one gives the years a base.
Players read the start together.
cons: A weak start echoes over many years.
The first year can feel fixed.

pairs.tendency: Players argue what a year of effort achieves, so how long a thing takes is decided by the table, not by a rule.
pros: Players decide what a year can do.
Arguments make time matter.
cons: Years differ from table to table.
Debates over a year slow the game.

pairs.tendency: Play stops between years, so players can say what changed in that stretch before the next year begins.
pros: Each year gets a short look back.
Players notice slow change.
cons: Pauses break the flow of the years.
Players may have little to say.

pairs.tendency: Playing again with one change lets players compare how the same years go, so a decade run twice shows what one thing did.
pros: The same years run twice show differences.
Comparing eras is easy.
cons: Luck can look like the effect.
A long span takes time to replay.

pairs.tendency: The game says what one round per year leaves out, such as what happened in each month, so players know where the picture stops being true.
pros: Players know what a year skips.
Gaps inside a year are named.
cons: A long list of gaps takes time.
Players may not read the list.

pairs.tendency: The people whose lives the game models say how long a year feels and what happens in it, so the round fits their real seasons.
pros: Years match real seasons.
Players check the pace of time.
cons: People may disagree about what a year holds.
Their year may not fit one game round.

pairs.tendency: Orders and stock move one link each year, so a change at the maker reaches the shop years later and the chain answers demand slowly.
pros: The slow reaction of a chain is easy to see.
Players feel how far away the shop is.
cons: A year is too long for weekly orders.
Players may not see the stock between links.

pairs.tendency: Each player sees only their own stock and orders for a year, so nobody sees how the whole span added up until the end.
pros: Years look different from each corner.
The full picture arrives as a surprise.
cons: Players guess what other years held.
Little to compare between corners.

pairs.tendency: The slowest step sets the pace, and over a year it shows as a pile waiting before it, so speeding up any other step changes nothing across the span.
pros: A year shows where the pile waits.
Years of waiting make the slow step plain.
cons: Years may pass before the pile is noticed.
A year hides which step is slowest.

pairs.tendency: Stock made ahead to a guess meets a year's demand, or stock made on order waits for it, so players feel what a year of forecasting costs.
pros: Guessing a year ahead feels risky.
Making on order shows the wait.
cons: A year is long to guess ahead.
Yearly guesses can be far off.

pairs.tendency: Players choose a big batch or one at a time, and a year is long enough that a big batch sits and a small one is set up again and again.
pros: A year shows what a big batch costs.
Setting up again is easy to count.
cons: One batch can fill a whole year.
The pace inside a year goes unseen.

pairs.tendency: A breakdown can strike in any round, so a year with a broken machine is a year lost, and a plan that assumes it works fails.
pros: A lost year shows the cost of repairs.
Failures feel like real misfortune.
cons: Failures are frequent against years.
One breakdown can empty a whole year.

pairs.tendency: Holding stock costs something every year and running out costs more, so players balance the two across many years of changing demand.
pros: Years show what holding stock costs.
Running short is easy to feel.
cons: One year of demand is hard to guess.
Players may overstock for fear of a shortage.

pairs.tendency: Players roll and move while gauges on the board shift with every landing, so a lucky or unlucky throw shows up in the water level or the trust gauge.
pros: Each landing has a visible effect.
Easy to read at a glance.
cons: Dice can make gauge swings feel random.
Pieces on the track and gauges compete for attention.

pairs.tendency: Each card a player picks moves a gauge, and the next player sees the new reading before choosing from what is left.
pros: Picks have an immediate, visible result.
Players read the state of play.
cons: Players may pick only to move a gauge.
Hard to track many cards and gauges together.

pairs.tendency: Bids are paid in the same stock the gauges track, so a winning bid shows at once as the level falling or the pollution rising.
pros: Prices and gauges tell one story.
Players see what a win costs everybody.
cons: Bidders can watch gauges and ignore each other.
Whoever bids high may seem to blame.

pairs.tendency: Each extra push shifts a gauge a little further toward its danger mark, and players decide whether to push again while watching it creep.
pros: Risk is easy to see.
Tension builds on every push.
cons: Players may stop only when a gauge looks low.
A bust can feel like the gauge's doing.

pairs.tendency: Taking or holding an area moves the gauges, such as pollution rising where a district is built up, so the map and the dials tell one story.
pros: Local moves show wider effects.
Map and gauges explain each other.
cons: Fights for areas can drown out the readings.
Two displays to watch at once.

pairs.tendency: Each placed worker runs a job that moves a gauge, so players see the whole round's work add up on the dials.
pros: Every job has a visible result.
Planning can follow the gauges.
cons: Full boards and gauges are a lot to read.
Everyone may crowd the same few spaces.

pairs.tendency: Players build patterns quietly in front of them while the gauges show what the group's building adds up to.
pros: Small builds show their combined effect.
Calm play with a clear shared picture.
cons: Patterns and gauges may feel unconnected.
Gauges can stay still for long stretches.

pairs.tendency: Cards played from the hand nudge the gauges, so players weigh what a card does to the dials before spending it.
pros: Holding a card means weighing a visible effect.
Timing choices have clear stakes.
cons: Players may hoard cards while gauges drift.
Hidden hands and open gauges mix awkwardly.

pairs.tendency: Tricks are won and lost as usual while gauges beside the table move with what is played, such as a rising price as strong cards come out.
pros: A familiar game gains a shared readout.
Players see what each trick costs.
cons: The gauges can feel stuck on to the tricks.
Trick play can pull attention from the dials.

pairs.tendency: Players trade and promise while gauges show what each deal does to the shared world, so a deal that looks fair can be seen to harm the whole.
pros: Deals can be checked against the gauges.
Talk has something shared to point at.
cons: Players may argue over how to read a gauge.
Loud players can steer how a reading is told.

pairs.tendency: Players collect sets for themselves while the gauges show what the collecting is doing to the world around them.
pros: Private goals show a public cost.
Easy to see when collecting has gone too far.
cons: Sets can feel separate from the gauges.
Gauges may be ignored until they run out.

pairs.tendency: Each tile laid moves a gauge, so players watch the map grow and the readings change together, such as more fields lowering the water level.
pros: Map and dials grow together.
Players link building to its effect.
cons: Players may place tiles to suit the gauge only.
Lots to look at once.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other in turn while the gauges quietly record what the exchange is doing, so the conversation and the world are seen together.
pros: Talk gets a shared record.
Players answer what the gauges show.
cons: Talk can fade into the background.
Gauges may feel like a referee.

pairs.tendency: With no talking, the gauges become the only shared voice, and players read each other's moves in how the dials shift.
pros: Dials stand in for speech.
Players watch closely.
cons: Misreading a dial cannot be talked through.
Quiet players may miss a change.

pairs.tendency: Players change rules that decide how fast the gauges move, so each rule change shows its effect on the dials straight away.
pros: Rule changes show their effects.
Players can see what a rule really does.
cons: Rule changes can break how the gauges are read.
Moving gauges are hard to compare across changes.

pairs.tendency: Players act as characters while the gauges show how their choices affect a shared world, and the dials can prompt what a character says next.
pros: Dials give characters something to react to.
Choices in character have visible results.
cons: Dials can pull players out of character.
Numbers may cut across the story.

pairs.tendency: A flick, stack or balance decides what happens, and each result moves a gauge, so a steady hand or a slip is read on the dial.
pros: Physical moves get a clear readout.
Excitement shows in the numbers.
cons: Slips can feel unfair on a gauge.
Hands busy with play may miss the dials.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the world as they go, and gauges beside the sheet track how that world is doing, such as how stretched a community is.
pros: The drawn map and the dials explain each other.
Players decide what the gauges measure.
cons: Drawing can take longer than the dials move.
Gauges can feel too tidy for a hand-drawn world.

pairs.tendency: Players ask for cards in turn, and the gauges track what the asking does to the supply, so a run on one rank shows as a falling level.
pros: Asking has a visible cost.
The shrinking supply is easy to follow.
cons: Gauges add little to a quick card game.
Players follow cards more than dials.

pairs.tendency: Bets are paid in stock the gauges track, so the bank's winnings and the players' losses show up on shared dials.
pros: Where the money goes is plain.
Everyone sees what the bank is taking.
cons: Fixed odds leave little to move the gauges.
Gauges can feel like a score by another name.

pairs.tendency: Players stake something before a throw, and the throw's result moves a gauge, so the luck of the dice shows up in the world's readings.
pros: Luck has a visible effect on the system.
Wins and losses are easy to follow.
cons: Players cannot steer the gauges beyond the bet.
Gauges may swing for no reason players chose.

pairs.tendency: Players put chips in as their hidden cards allow, and the pot's growth is read as a gauge for the table.
pros: Bets show how confident the table feels.
Raising has a visible price.
cons: Gauges add little beyond the pot.
Players may watch the pot more than the world.

pairs.tendency: Each player arrives with a side of their own, and the gauges show the total effect of all those different sides on one world.
pros: Different sides add up in one place.
Players see whose plan moved the dials.
cons: Strong builds can swamp the readings.
Hard to tell which side caused a change.

pairs.tendency: Players state a goal before play, then watch the gauges as the hand unfolds to see whether the contract is being kept or the world is slipping.
pros: A promise can be checked against the dials.
Plans and readings sit side by side.
cons: Gauges can disagree with the contract.
Contracts can ignore what the dials say.

pairs.tendency: Pieces change sides when captured, and gauges show how the balance of the whole world shifts with each conversion.
pros: Shifts in power are easy to read.
Swings do not hide behind the board.
cons: A gauge can swing more than players follow.
Leaders can fall behind in one move.

pairs.tendency: Players are caught and freed by teammates while gauges show how the group is doing as a whole, such as how many are still free.
pros: Group state is shown at a glance.
Rescues feel important.
cons: Players waiting in jail watch dials alone.
Gauges may count what the chase already shows.

pairs.tendency: Players close in on pieces by surrounding them, and gauges track what the captures take from the world, such as space or supplies.
pros: Captures show a cost to the whole.
Quiet, slow play can still be read.
cons: Gauges can be hard to tie to single captures.
The board already shows the standings.

pairs.tendency: Help for players who are behind is read off the gauges, so who gets a boost depends on what the dials say about the world, not only the scores.
pros: Help can follow a clear reading.
Players see why aid was given.
cons: Gauges and scores can point different ways.
Players may stay low to earn help.

pairs.tendency: A throw or a card decides every turn, and the gauges simply show what luck did to the world, with nothing for players to change.
pros: The dials show luck at work.
Quick and light to follow.
cons: Gauges can only be watched, not changed.
Players may stop paying attention.

pairs.tendency: One player chases the rest while gauges on the side track the effect, such as how tired the group is or how much space is left.
pros: The chase has a visible price.
Tension can be read by all.
cons: Running players seldom stop to read gauges.
Gauges can slow a fast game.

pairs.tendency: Each turn a player picks who to hit or help, and the gauges show what that choice does to the shared world as well as to the target.
pros: Targets and wider effects both show.
Picks reveal what players care about.
cons: Players may attack to move a gauge instead.
A grudge can outweigh the dials.

pairs.tendency: Players try to link two sides of a board, and gauges show what each link or cut costs the wider world, such as flow through a network.
pros: Links show what they carry.
Cuts have a clear effect.
cons: The chain on the board is easier to read than dials.
Gauges can feel like decoration.

pairs.tendency: Each choice beats one and loses to another, and the gauges show which choice the table has leaned on most, such as which has run low.
pros: Patterns of choosing become visible.
Players may adjust to what the dials show.
cons: Gauges can give hints about what others will play.
Rock-paper-scissors choices rarely move a world.

pairs.tendency: Players declare pairs and runs while still holding the cards, and gauges show what each declaration adds up to for the table.
pros: Declared sets have a visible total.
Scoring and world are seen together.
cons: Declaring may matter more than the gauges.
Hands stay hidden while gauges are open.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a power that bends a rule, and the gauges show which powers are moving the world most.
pros: Different powers become easy to compare.
Players see what each role really does.
cons: Strong powers may hog the dials.
Many powers and gauges are hard to learn together.

pairs.tendency: Players may double what the game is worth, and gauges show how close things are to the limit, so each offer is made with the dials in view.
pros: Offers can be judged against a reading.
Stakes and state show together.
cons: Doubling can matter more than the gauges.
Gauges may decide when to quit.

pairs.tendency: A player has to take a capture when one is on offer, and gauges show what the forced move costs the world around the board.
pros: Forced moves show their cost.
Traps become clear to read.
cons: Gauges can look idle during forced play.
Forced captures can hide the dials.

pairs.tendency: Characters gain power as the game goes on, and gauges show the price of that growth, such as the resources a stronger group has used up.
pros: Growth shows what it costs.
Later challenges can be read against the dials.
cons: Powerful players may ignore the gauges.
Gauges can fill up with each new level.

pairs.tendency: The list grows every turn and gauges track how much the group is carrying, such as the length of the list or the effort it takes.
pros: The load is easy to see.
Players watch the list and the dials.
cons: A growing list is already visible and needs no gauge.
Gauges can distract players from remembering.

pairs.tendency: A weaker player starts with less, and gauges show the effect on the shared world of that unequal start.
pros: The gap is plain to see.
Players discuss fairness with the dials in view.
cons: Gauges may show the handicap but not close the gap.
The stronger player may feel watched.

pairs.tendency: Someone hides while others search, and gauges show how far the hunt has gone, such as the time left or the ground covered.
pros: Progress of the search can be read.
The hunt gets a shared clock.
cons: Gauges can give away where the hider is.
Dials do little while no one is looking.

pairs.tendency: Pieces hop over each other, and gauges show what the hops add up to for the world, such as the number of pieces that remain.
pros: Hopping has a visible total.
Players see how play is thinning out.
cons: The board already shows what is left.
Gauges and hops rarely connect.

pairs.tendency: Players keep some dice and roll the rest, and the final result moves a gauge, so each turn's gamble can be read on the dial.
pros: Gambles have a visible result.
Players can see when luck helped.
cons: Rerolls can move gauges more than players mean to.
Dice fall quickly while gauges need reading.

pairs.tendency: Landing on a piece sends it back to the start, and gauges show the wider cost of every send-back, such as time lost for a whole team.
pros: Setbacks show their larger cost.
Hits are easy to follow.
cons: Players can attack just to shift a gauge.
Sent-back players watch dials turn against them.

pairs.tendency: Players make rows to take pieces, and gauges show how the loss of pieces is changing the shared world.
pros: Captures show a wider cost.
Makes the effects of a mill clear.
cons: The board already tells most of the story.
Gauges can feel tacked on.

pairs.tendency: Players build words from letters while gauges show the total effect of the words, such as how much of a shared stock has been used.
pros: Words have a visible cost.
A shared pool can be tracked.
cons: Players may focus on words and miss the dials.
Gauges add little to a spelling game.

pairs.tendency: Tiles are added to a line whose open ends match, and gauges show how the line is shaping up, such as how many ends are left open.
pros: Open ends become easy to count.
A growing line can be read.
cons: Skipped turns can leave gauges unmoving.
A line on the table is already visible.

pairs.tendency: Players lay sets down on the table, and gauges show what the melds are doing to the shared world, such as the pile or cards left.
pros: Laid sets have a visible total.
Everyone sees the state of the table.
cons: Melds add to the table and the dials.
Gauges can be left to the end of the round.

pairs.tendency: Each power works once, and the gauges show what the world looked like at the moment it was spent, so the choice of when to use it is read off the dials.
pros: Timing has something to read.
Spent powers have a visible effect.
cons: Players may wait for the gauge to turn.
One-off effects can overshoot a gauge.

pairs.tendency: A move is offered, the other player can turn it down, and the gauges show what the accepted move did to the shared world.
pros: Accepting has a visible cost.
Players learn to judge offers by the dials.
cons: Offers may be refused only to stop a gauge.
Choices slow while gauges are checked.

pairs.tendency: A message travels along the table while the gauges show what the world looks like to the sender, so the change on the way can be compared with it.
pros: Garbling can be checked against a reading.
A shared state anchors the whisper.
cons: Gauges can make the message too easy to check.
The point of not knowing may be lost.

pairs.tendency: Players hand cards on before play starts, and the gauges show how what was passed changes the world as the first moves are made.
pros: Early passes show later effects.
The gauges give passing a visible reason.
cons: Few gauges move before play starts.
Passes happen before the dials matter.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up the start and the other picks a side, and the opening gauges show whether the split really is even.
pros: A fair split can be checked against the dials.
Players share an honest reading of the start.
cons: Gauges may only show a gap that is already clear.
Setting up takes longer with readings to match.

pairs.tendency: Pieces reaching the far end turn into stronger ones, and gauges show how those stronger pieces change what the world can bear.
pros: Promotions show a larger effect.
The reason to push forward is clear.
cons: Gauges can feel added on to a promotion.
Promoted pieces may dwarf the dials.

pairs.tendency: Teams run in legs and hand over, and gauges show how the whole team is doing, such as the energy left or the time used.
pros: Team state is easy to read.
Handovers show their cost.
cons: Runners may be too quick for the dials.
Gauges can matter less than the race.

pairs.tendency: Players build shapes that cannot be taken, and gauges show how much of the world is now protected and how much is not.
pros: Safe ground is visible.
Defence and exposure can be read.
cons: A shape already shows what is safe.
Gauges may move little once shapes are set.

pairs.tendency: Tricks are won for named prize cards, and gauges show what each prize does to the world, so the prizes are tied to a reading.
pros: Prizes get a visible weight.
Players see what a prize changes.
cons: Gauges and prize cards can compete for attention.
Prizes may stay the aim, not the gauges.

pairs.tendency: Cards in the middle belong to everybody, and gauges show how the shared cards are changing the table's position as they are used.
pros: Everyone works from one picture.
Shared cards have a visible effect.
cons: The gauges may say less than the cards do.
Players follow the middle more than the dials.

pairs.tendency: Everyone puts into a pot that grows, and the pot's size is read as a gauge for what is at stake for the table.
pros: Growing stakes are easy to see.
Players weigh the pot against the dials.
cons: The pot already does the gauges' job.
A rolling pot can hold attention too long.

pairs.tendency: Seeds are scooped and dropped one by one, and gauges show how the spread is changing the world, such as which pits run empty.
pros: Seed counts stay easy to read.
The pattern of sowing becomes visible.
cons: The pits already show the counts.
Gauges can duplicate what the board shows.

pairs.tendency: An extra hand is taken, swapped or bought before play, and gauges show what that choice does to the world once play begins.
pros: An early choice has a visible effect.
Buying or swapping can be read on a dial.
cons: Few gauges move until play is under way.
The spare hand can be forgotten once play starts.

pairs.tendency: Special squares send players back, keep them safe or make them miss a turn, and each one nudges a gauge, so the track shows its effect on the world.
pros: Each square has a visible effect.
A simple track can teach a system.
cons: Squares can move the dials in odd ways.
Players learn the squares more than the world.

pairs.tendency: Each card or unit has a price paid from a stock the gauges show, so spending is seen draining the dial for everybody.
pros: Spending shows what it takes from a shared stock.
Players weigh price against effect.
cons: Players may spend only to watch a dial fall.
Shared stock can run out before play is deep.

pairs.tendency: Players share a fixed amount between places, and the gauges show how thin the spreading has left each one.
pros: Trade-offs show up on the dials.
Spread and strength are easy to compare.
cons: Gauges can encourage everyone to spread alike.
Players may watch dials more than rivals.

pairs.tendency: Play freezes when a signal comes and the gauges are read at that moment, so players look at the world while everyone is still.

Snapshots show where the system had got to.
cons: Reading gauges can slow a fast game.
A freeze can come before the dials show much.

pairs.tendency: Players put cards back and take new ones, and gauges show what that churn does to the stock of cards or the world around the table.
pros: Swaps show what they use up.
Players see the cost of churning.
cons: Gauges move little if swaps are small.
Players may swap more than the dials can show.

pairs.tendency: Players may pick up the whole discard pile, and a gauge shows how large it has grown, so taking it is a choice made with the size in view.
pros: The risk of a big pile is easy to see.
A shared pile becomes a shared reading.
cons: The pile already shows its own size.
Gauges can slow a simple choice.

pairs.tendency: One suit is named trump, and gauges show how far the dominant suit has pushed the others out, such as which suit is running dry.
pros: The effect of one strong suit is visible.
Players see how play leans one way.
cons: Trump can set play more than the dials do.
Gauges can seem a side matter.

pairs.tendency: Players are on both sides across two boards, and the gauges show how both games add up for one world, so a win on one can be seen as a cost on the other.
pros: Both boards share one reading.
Trade-offs between games become clear.
cons: Hard to follow two boards and the dials.
Players may give up one board to help the gauge.

pairs.tendency: A wild card can stand for any card, and gauges show what the stand-in does, so a wild's effect is read on the dial and not only in the hand.

Players see when a wild changes the game.
cons: Wilds can swing the gauges at the last moment.
Players may hold a wild until the dial suits.

pairs.tendency: The edges of the board are joined and gauges show what that does to the world, such as how a spreading effect comes round and reaches its own source.
pros: The loop shows up on the dials.
Spread can be followed round the board.
cons: Wrapping makes it harder to tell where an effect began.
Gauges may feel less useful when the board never ends.

pairs.tendency: Players narrow down a secret with yes or no questions, and a gauge shows how many questions or possibilities are left.
pros: Progress toward the answer is visible.
The group can see the list shrink.
cons: Gauges can show how close the answer is.
Gauges add little to a simple game of questions.

pairs.tendency: Players race to reach the end while the gauges show what all the racing is costing the world, such as the fuel burnt or the ground used up.
pros: The race has a visible price.
Players see what winning costs.
cons: Racers can ignore the dials until they turn.
Gauges may slow a quick finish.

pairs.tendency: Players score points while the gauges show a separate reading of the world, so a high score can be seen next to a falling level.
pros: Points and world can be compared.
Players see when scoring hurts the system.
cons: Points tend to win the attention.
Players may score while the gauges drop.

pairs.tendency: Players are knocked out one by one while gauges show how the shrinking world is doing, so each exit can be read against the dials.
pros: Each exit can be linked to a reading.
Pressure builds in the open.
cons: Players who are out may only watch.
Gauges can seem harsh as the world runs down.

pairs.tendency: The team keeps the world from collapsing, and the gauges are the thing they watch together, with each move read against the danger marks.
pros: The team shares one picture.
Everyone can see the danger rise.
cons: A falling gauge can feel hopeless.
One player may read the dials for everyone.

pairs.tendency: The group works toward a target, and the gauges show how close the world is to it, so players can see each move bring the goal nearer or further.
pros: Progress toward the goal is plain.
The whole group reads the same dials.
cons: Little tension once the gauge is on track.
Some players may follow the dial without thinking.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a secret aim, and the gauges are the one thing everyone sees, so a move can be read by what it does to the dials.
pros: Hidden aims show up in the open.
Players guess goals from how the gauges move.
cons: Gauges can give secret goals away.
A shared reading can feel at odds with private aims.

pairs.tendency: A story unfolds while the gauges show how the world in it is doing, so players can see the story's cost as well as its plot.
pros: The story has a measure.
The plot has visible stakes.
cons: Gauges can interrupt the telling.
The ending can feel set by the dials.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, and the gauges simply show how the world has changed, so players can talk about what the dials say once play stops.

The world is seen with no score to hide it.
cons: Players may feel the gauges are a hidden score.
With no aim, the dials may go unread.

pairs.tendency: Each player picks a goal, and the gauges show how the shared world is doing, so players can judge their own aim against the dials.

Players see what their aim costs others.

Players may drop a goal when a gauge turns.

pairs.tendency: Everyone avoids being the one loser, and gauges show how close the world is to that point, so players read the danger as it rises.

Players see who is protected.
cons: Gauges can point at the likely loser.
Dials may be read as an accusation.

Players share the job of looking after the world.
cons: Players can feel tied to the dials.
Gauges can turn play into upkeep.

pairs.tendency: Nobody can win, and gauges show what has happened to the world anyway, so the dials are the only result players are left with.
pros: The dials show what play did.
Players are pushed to look at the system.

A game with no win can seem pointless to some.

pairs.tendency: A lone player works against the cards while gauges show how the layout is doing, such as how much is left to clear.

pairs.tendency: Several short games are played in a row and the gauges can be compared at the end of each, showing how the world did across them.

Patterns across rounds show up.
cons: Gauges may be reset and lose the thread.
The match winner can matter more than the dials.

pairs.tendency: Players try to collect the fewest points while the gauges show a separate reading of the world, so a low score can be seen next to the dials.
pros: Players weigh a low score against the system.
Points and dials can be compared.
cons: Two readings that move opposite ways confuse some players.
Players may keep the score low and ignore the dials.

pairs.tendency: Players have to land on an exact number, and gauges show how close the world is to a limit, so players read the dial to avoid going over.

Going over is easy to spot.
cons: Players may count the number and ignore the dials.
A near miss can stall a gauge.

pairs.tendency: The aim is turned upside down, and the gauges show what it takes to lose, so a falling reading may be what players are chasing.

Players think about what winning means.
cons: Players may find the dials hard to read in reverse.
Gauges and the goal can seem to disagree.

Players may blame each other for a reading.

Players see how they affect others.
cons: Gauges can make blame easier to assign.
Players may read dials and miss who caused a change.

pairs.tendency: The whole team runs the world together and the gauges give it one shared picture, so every move is read the same way by everybody.

Easy to discuss what to do next.
cons: One player may read the dials for all.
Little tension while the dials look steady.

pairs.tendency: Players help the world but also want their own gains, and the gauges show who is pushing the shared reading in whose favour.

pairs.tendency: Two teams compete inside one world, and the gauges show the total effect of both teams on it, so each side can see what the contest is costing.
pros: The cost of the contest is shared and plain.
Teams talk over the dials.
cons: Teams may blame each other for a reading.
The contest can matter more than the dials.

pairs.tendency: One player secretly harms the world and the gauges show the damage as it happens, so players try to tell sabotage from chance in the readings.

The dials give clues about who is acting.
cons: Hard to tell sabotage from ordinary movement.
Accusations can grow from one odd reading.

pairs.tendency: One player is absent and the gauges show what is happening in their share of the world, so the missing player's effects can still be read.

Players trust a reading that anyone can check.
cons: The game master may feel bound to the dials.
Setting gauges takes time away from the story.

pairs.tendency: Passers-by join a game in the open and read the gauges as they come, so a newcomer can see how the world is doing without a long explanation.

A crowd can talk over the dials.
cons: Gauges need to be large and easy to read.
Players come and go and lose the thread.

pairs.tendency: One player plays against all the others and the gauges show which side the world is leaning toward, so both sides watch the same dials.
pros: Both sides see the balance.
The lone player has something to read.
cons: The dials can show the outcome too soon.
The group may focus on the gauge, not the lone player.

pairs.tendency: A lone player runs a world and watches the gauges respond to every choice, with nobody else to blame or to talk to about what the dials show.

Players can learn at their own pace.

cons: Players may see no link between choices and dials.
Gauges can feel pointless if nothing is chosen.

pairs.tendency: Luck moves the gauges, but players can soften what comes, so they watch the dials and choose what to prepare for.

Players see what a precaution is worth.
cons: Gauges can swing past any preparation.
More rules to follow beside the dials.

cons: Skilled players tend to read the dials fastest.
Luck can look like an error in a gauge.

pairs.tendency: Only the players' choices move the gauges, so every change in the dials has a cause that somebody can trace back to a move.

cons: Real systems are rarely this predictable.

pairs.tendency: Throws are read as advice, and the gauges give a second reading of the world, so a sign can be set against the dials.
pros: Signs and measures sit side by side.

cons: The two readings can contradict each other.

pairs.tendency: Players try to act in step with each other, and the gauges show how the shared world is responding to that timing.
