pros: The group looks after its own game.
Tired players can say so.
cons: The pause may end up ending the game.
Little to reflect on beyond mood.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they were trying to do in a game where nothing can be won and what they found.
pros: The refusal of the game is noticed.
Players talk about what they expected.
cons: Some feel confused rather than interested.
The pause can sound like a lesson.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while the layout is half cleared, and the player says what they are trying, where they are stuck and what they would change.
pros: Solo thinking is said aloud.
A friend can listen and ask.
cons: Alone, the pause may feel like nothing.
Getting stuck is more obvious when said.

pairs.tendency: Play stops between short games, and players say what they learned from the last one and what they will do next.
pros: Each game is a lesson for the next.
Changes of plan are heard.
cons: Talk can give away tactics.
Winners may not change anything.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while players are avoiding points, and they say what they have picked up, what they have dodged and how.
pros: Avoiding is explained.
Players see how others dodge.
cons: Naming points held invites targeting.
The pause adds little once points are known.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while players are near the target number, and they say how they are working out the last steps.
pros: Near misses are talked about.
Counting methods are shared.
cons: Players can be stuck on the same number.
Talk can help the others to land.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what it is like to try to lose and which of their habits keep getting in the way.
pros: Winning habits become visible.
Players laugh at their own reflexes.
cons: The odd rule may be explained away.
Players can lose track of who is meant to lose.

pairs.tendency: Each player builds alone, and the pause is the first time they look up and compare what each has made.
pros: Players see how others went about it.
Quiet play gets some talk.
cons: Comparing can feel like ranking.
Little in the game to point to.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after some attacks, and players say what was done to them, what they did, and what they meant by it.
pros: Hits are explained from both sides.
The mood at the table is checked.
cons: Talk can reopen quarrels.
Players may defend moves rather than reflect.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while players are shaping the shared board, and they say how others' changes have affected their plans.
pros: Hidden effects are named.
Players see how a board carries influence.
cons: Few attacks mean few reasons to talk.
Players may not notice what was done to them.

pairs.tendency: Play stops and the whole team says how they are working, who is taking the lead and what they might try.
pros: The team checks its own habits.
Everyone has a say.
cons: A lead player can fill the pause.
Less tension to talk about.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while players are both helping and holding back, and they say where they put the group first and where themselves.
pros: Mixed motives are said openly.
Players see where trust is wearing thin.
cons: Honesty can cost a player their private aim.
Talk may be guarded.

pairs.tendency: Play stops and each team talks among themselves, then the teams share what they saw about their own play and the other's.
pros: Teams plan by looking back.
Each side hears the other's view.
cons: Teams may use the pause for tactics.
Talk across teams can sound like taunting.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while a traitor is hiding among the team, and players say what they have noticed about each other.
pros: Suspicion is spoken out loud.
Players hear their own reasons for doubt.
cons: The traitor can use the talk.
Accused players can be upset.

pairs.tendency: Play is slow already, so the pause is a letter or message that says what the writer has noticed before the next move.
pros: Slow play leaves space to think.
Letters keep a written record.
cons: The pause barely differs from play.
Long gaps can make the earlier moves hard to recall.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what the absent player would have noticed and how they are standing in for them.
pros: The missing voice is imagined.
Players think about someone else's view.
cons: Guessing for another person may be wrong.
The pause can turn into talk about the absent player.

pairs.tendency: Play stops and the game master and the players say what each has noticed, with the master also saying what they have been shaping.
pros: The master's choices are explained.
Players say what they want next.
cons: The master can dominate the pause.
Players may hold back from criticising.

pairs.tendency: Play stops in the street, and the players and anyone watching say what they have seen, though some passers-by may not stay.
pros: Onlookers can add a view.
Players hear how the game looks outside.
cons: People come and go during the pause.
Players may feel watched.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and the single player and the team each say how it feels from their side of the table.
pros: The lone player is heard.
The team sees its own weight.
cons: The team may use the pause to plan.
The lone player may feel outnumbered even in talk.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and the one player says aloud or writes down what they have noticed, with no one else to answer.
pros: Thinking gets slowed down.
Notes can be compared with a friend later.
cons: Nobody to respond.
Easy to skip the pause.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after some rounds of mostly luck, and players say which events came from the dice and which from them.
pros: Players separate luck from choice.
Talk is easy when nobody is to blame.
cons: Little in the game to reflect on.
Players may read patterns into dice.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after some poor luck, and players say what they did to soften it and what they would try next.
pros: Ways of coping with luck are shared.
Players see how others prepared.
cons: Talk can fall to complaining about the dice.
Preparation may feel small once named.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say which of their results came from their choices and which from the luck of the draw.
pros: Players test their sense of cause.
Luck gives a gentle excuse to talk.
cons: Some credit luck for their choices.
Experienced players may explain too much.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they have planned and how it is working, with no dice to blame.
pros: Plans can be examined in detail.
Beginners can learn from the strong.
cons: Talk can turn into coaching.
Strong players may hold back what they know.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after a throw has been read as a sign, and players say what it made them think about.
pros: Signs open the talk.
Players say what the reading means to them.
cons: Some may read too much into a throw.
Talk can wander far from the game.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they sensed about each other before acting, though the sense may fade when explained.
pros: Quiet signals are named.
Players hear how others tuned in.
cons: Explaining can break the feeling.
Hard to put into words.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say how the story has turned out so far and which parts came from the dice.
pros: Chance and story are told apart.
The story is retold in many voices.
cons: The table lookup can feel mechanical.
Talk can pass over what the dice did.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they see on a board where everything is visible, and what they think others see.
pros: Everyone starts from the same view.
Different readings of one board are heard.
cons: Little hidden to uncover.
Talk can turn into advice on the next move.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they guess about others' hands while keeping their own, so talk is about guesses and not facts.
pros: Guesses are said aloud.
Players hear how others read them.
cons: Hands may be given away.
Players may say little.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say who they suspect and why, while hidden roles stay hidden.
pros: Reasons for suspicion are heard.
Players see how they come across.
cons: Hidden players can steer the talk.
Suspicions can harden into quarrels.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they have worked out so far and what clues led them there.
pros: Reasoning is shared.
Beginners can follow the clues.
cons: Naming a deduction helps others catch up.
Clever players may spoil the discovery.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they think was bluffed, with the bluffers free to say or to stay quiet.
pros: Players hear how bluffs were read.
The mood of the table is looked at.
cons: Bluffers can be exposed and annoyed.
Talk can break the nerve of the game.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and newcomers say what they think the secret rule is while the one who knows says nothing.
pros: Guesses at the rule are heard.
Players share what they have tried.
cons: The one who knows has to hold back.
The pause can drag if guesses go wrong.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and the guessers say what they make of the hints, while the one who knows listens but still cannot say.
pros: The hinter hears how they were read.
Misreadings are explained.
cons: The one who knows may find it hard to stay silent.
Hints can be given away by the talk.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after some exploring, and players say what they have found and what they guess lies ahead.
pros: Guesses about the unknown are aired.
Players see how the map is growing.
cons: Talk can reveal where to go next.
The surprise of exploring can fade.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say how they are using the open hand and what they think the secret hands hold.
pros: The open hand is a talking point.
Players hear how others read what is hidden.
cons: Talk can reveal the secret hands.
The open hand may be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say who they think is ahead, though nobody can check.
pros: Guesses about the score are heard.
Players notice how they judge others.
cons: Wrong guesses may be believed.
Players may feel uneasy about not knowing.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after a few rounds of turns, and each player in order says what they noticed while waiting and while acting.
pros: Everyone gets a turn to speak.
Waiting players have something to say.
cons: Going round can feel like another turn.
Loud players may fill the circle.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after everyone has acted at once, and players say what they chose, what they saw others choose and what surprised them.
pros: Simultaneous choices are compared.
Surprises are shared.
cons: Players recall only some of it.
Quick play can be hard to explain.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and everyone says what happened in the rush, which few of them could have followed fully.
pros: Fast moments are slowed down.
Different views of the same rush are heard.
cons: Memories of the rush differ.
The pause is a strong contrast and can be jarring.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say how the clock changed what they chose and what they did when time ran out.
pros: The pressure of the clock is named.
Rushed choices are looked at again.
cons: The pause is the one time with no clock.
Players may fall back into rushing afterwards.

pairs.tendency: Play stops at the end of a day or week, and each player says what they noticed since their last move.
pros: Waiting becomes part of the thinking.
The pauses are built into the pace.
cons: Players may forget what they planned.
The pause and the game can blur together.

pairs.tendency: Play already slows players down, so the pause is a longer stop in an already slow game, with talk after the breath.
pros: Slowness lets thoughts settle.
The game suits the pause.
cons: A double dose of slowness can drag.
Impatient players may fidget.

pairs.tendency: Play speeds up round by round, and a pause in the middle slows it for a moment before the rush resumes.
pros: A breath before the fast part.
Players say how the speed is changing them.
cons: The build-up of speed is broken.
Restarting the rush can feel awkward.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after some extra turns, and players say what it felt like to take or to watch a run of moves.
pros: Uneven turns are talked about.
Lucky runs are noticed.
cons: Those who watched may feel left out.
The pause can break up a streak.

pairs.tendency: Play stops at the end of a stage, and players say what they did and what they expect when the rules change.
pros: Stages get a natural stopping point.
Players think about what carries forward.
cons: The stage change already acts as a stop.
The two stops can feel repeated.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they have seen the model do and how it compares with the real system it copies.
pros: Links between board and real system are named.
Players spot patterns early.
cons: Talk can drift away from the model.
Players may not know the real system.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and each player says how things look from their group's side and what they think the others want.
pros: Other groups' views are heard.
Players step into another view.
cons: Players may speak for groups they know little about.
Talk can become arguments between roles.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while the shared supply is dropping, and players say how much each has taken and what they expect others to do.
pros: Shared use becomes visible.
Taking too much is discussed in time.
cons: Players may blame each other.
Talk can come too late for a supply already empty.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what they did some rounds ago and what is only now showing up.
pros: Causes are traced to earlier moves.
The gap between act and result is clear.
cons: Players may have forgotten their earlier moves.
Without notes, the trail is lost.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after a new rule has been tried, and players say what it changed before deciding whether to keep it.
pros: Rules are tested before they are fixed.
Players see effects on others.
cons: The test may be too short to show much.
Talk can turn into votes.

pairs.tendency: Play stops at set points for short talk, and a longer debrief at the end gathers what was said.
pros: Notes from the pauses feed the end talk.
Players recall more at the end.
cons: The two can repeat each other.
Total talk can outweigh play.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after changes that cannot be undone, and players say what was lost or changed for ever.
pros: Permanence is noticed.
Players mark what they gave up.
cons: Regret can surface.
Pausing can make the next move feel heavy.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what the rules seem to be saying about the world, and whether they agree.
pros: The point of the rules is spoken aloud.
Players argue with the game itself.
cons: Players may only guess the designer's point.
Talk can drift from the rules to opinions.

pairs.tendency: Play stops while something real is at stake, and players say how they feel about it and whether to go on.
pros: Real feelings are heard in time.
Players can say they are uneasy.
cons: Some may not speak up.
The pause itself can feel serious.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what the points stand for and whether they have started chasing the points instead.
pros: Drift from the value to the score is caught.
Players question the scoring.
cons: Talk can feel like a lecture.
Players who enjoyed chasing may feel caught out.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say how the way of living they are practising feels so far and what surprises them.
pros: Feelings about a new way are said early.
Problems are spotted while there is time.
cons: Players may be polite rather than honest.
The future can seem finished too soon.

pairs.tendency: Play stops partway through each run, and players compare what they saw in this run with the one before.
pros: Differences between runs are named.
Players track the changed thing.
cons: More pauses make each run longer.
Memory of the earlier run fades.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say where the game seems to differ from the real situation, before it is told what was left out.
pros: Players spot gaps for themselves.
Their guesses can be compared with the game's own list.
cons: Players may guess wrongly and feel foolish.
Talk can stay on what is missing, not what is shown.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and the people the game is about say what rings true and what does not, while others listen.
pros: Those who know the situation lead the talk.
Mistakes in the game get caught.
cons: Some may feel put on show.
Others may talk over them.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and each link in the chain says what orders and goods they have seen and what they expect next.
pros: Each link's view is heard.
Players see how a delay passes along.
cons: Players may blame the next link.
The pause can reveal too much to others in the chain.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and each player says what they can see of their own stock and orders, and what they guess about the rest.
pros: Guesswork about the whole is said aloud.
Players see how little each knew.
cons: Sharing can undo the hidden view.
Wrong guesses are repeated as facts.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say where work is piling up and which step seems to be the slow one.
pros: The slow step is named by those who feel it.
Players test their guesses about speeding up.
cons: The pause can point straight to the answer.
Players may argue over which step is slowest.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say whether they have been making ahead or waiting for orders, and what it has cost them.
pros: The difference between push and pull is felt.
Players compare stock and waiting.
cons: A pause during ordering can confuse who owes what.
Players may defend what they chose.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say what size batches they have been using, and what they paid in waiting or setting up.
pros: Batch choices are explained.
Costs of big and small batches are compared.
cons: Players may only repeat their numbers.
The pause comes too late to change a batch.

pairs.tendency: Play stops after a breakdown, and players say how their plan coped and what they had not allowed for.
pros: Plans that ignored failure are noticed.
Repairs are talked through.
cons: Players may feel unlucky rather than unprepared.
Pausing during a repair can slow it down.

pairs.tendency: Play stops, and players say how much stock they hold, what it has cost them, and whether they ran short.
pros: The balance is explained.
Players compare what each risked.
cons: Numbers can crowd out the talk.
Players may only look at their own stock.

pairs.tendency: Players run the same dice race twice, changing one board space or rule, and compare how long each game took and who finished first.
pros: Easy to see what one change did
Short games allow several rounds
cons: Dice noise can hide the effect
Two runs are too few to trust

pairs.tendency: Players draft from the same cards in round one, then change how many are passed or kept, and compare the hands that result.
pros: Hands from each round sit side by side
Shows which passing rule changes picks
cons: Different cards drawn blur the comparison
Each round takes setup time

pairs.tendency: The group runs the same auction twice with a changed budget or rule, then compares the prices paid and who ended up with what.
pros: Prices make the difference easy to count
Players see how a budget shapes bids
cons: Players remember the first round's prices
Early winners may repeat their plan

pairs.tendency: Players push their luck in two rounds with a different stopping rule, then compare how far each person went before they stopped.
pros: Stopping points are easy to line up
Shows how one rule shifts nerve
cons: A few lucky or unlucky pushes dominate
Results swing too much to read

pairs.tendency: Two games are played on the same map with one change, such as a different start position, and players compare who holds which areas.
pros: Maps from both games can be set beside each other
A start change shows what it favours
cons: Areas take a long time to rebuild
Players copy the first game's moves

pairs.tendency: The same worker game is played twice with one action space changed or removed, and players compare which spaces filled up first.
pros: Crowded spaces show where the pressure sits
Easy to see what one space was worth
cons: Setting up twice is slow
Players choose differently once they know the board

pairs.tendency: Players build patterns in two rounds with a different scoring rule and compare the shapes they made and the points those shapes earned.
pros: Finished patterns are easy to compare
Shows how scoring steers what gets built
cons: Players reuse the first round's pattern
Small changes are hard to spot

pairs.tendency: The same hands are dealt again with one rule changed, and players compare which cards they saved, which they played and when.
pros: Same cards make a fair comparison
Reveals how a rule changes timing
cons: Players remember the earlier hands
Dealing the same hands again takes effort

pairs.tendency: Players replay the same deal of cards with one rule changed, such as a different trump, and compare which tricks each side won.
pros: The same deal makes the change clear
Quick hands allow many comparisons
cons: Players recall the first deal's cards
Needs the original deal kept in order

pairs.tendency: The group negotiates the same situation twice with one change, such as a banned topic, and compares the deals made and who made them.
pros: Deals can be listed and compared
Shows how one limit changes talk
cons: Spoken deals are hard to record exactly
The same people repeat their old arguments

pairs.tendency: Players collect sets in two games with a different set size or card count, and compare how fast sets formed and who finished first.
pros: Set counts are simple to tally
Shows how scarcity changes collecting
cons: Card luck can drown the change
Shuffles differ between the games

pairs.tendency: Two maps are built from the same tiles with one change, such as a different drawing order, and players compare the maps that grew.
pros: Two finished maps sit side by side
Shows how order shapes the map
cons: Different draws make maps hard to match
Tiles take time to clear and reset

pairs.tendency: The same call-and-answer chain is played twice with one new limit, such as a time cap, and the group compares how the chain went.
pros: Players notice what the limit did to the replies
Short chains are quick to replay
cons: Spoken chains are hard to remember exactly
The second chain copies the first

pairs.tendency: A silent game is played twice with one change, such as a shared signal, and players compare how often they got in step.
pros: Silent rounds are easy to count
Shows what one small cue gives
cons: Players cannot discuss what went wrong mid-game
The second round leans on memory

pairs.tendency: Players play two games where the rule changes differ, then compare how each game drifted from its start and where each ended.
pros: Shows how a rule change spreads
Two different endings are plain to see
cons: Games drift too far to compare
Rule changes pile up and get lost

pairs.tendency: The same scene is played twice with a changed character or situation, and the group compares what each version led the characters to do.
pros: Players hear how a role changes choices
Short scenes can be replayed often
cons: A scene never plays out the same way twice
Players slip out of character to compare

pairs.tendency: A dexterity task is done again with one change, such as a different grip or distance, and players compare scores, falls or times.
pros: Scores are quick to measure and compare
Replaying costs little
cons: Tired hands change the result
Practice improves scores more than the change

pairs.tendency: The group draws a map twice from the same starting prompt with one change, and compares the two maps side by side on paper.
pros: Paper maps are easy to keep and compare
Shows how a prompt shapes a place
cons: Hand drawing adds differences that are not the change
Each map takes a long session

pairs.tendency: Players replay the asking game with a changed rule, such as no repeat asks, and compare how many cards each person gathered.
pros: Card counts are quick to compare
Shows how a rule changes asking
cons: A different deal changes what players hold
Players recall what others asked for before

pairs.tendency: The betting game is run twice with different odds, and players compare how much the bank and the bettors each ended with.
pros: Money totals make the effect plain
Shows how odds tilt the game
cons: A few throws can swing the totals
Players change their bets once they know the odds

pairs.tendency: Players bet on a throw in two sessions with one change, such as a different payout, and compare how the bets and totals moved.
pros: Bet sizes are easy to compare
Shows how a payout shapes nerve
cons: Throws are random, so totals vary
Too few throws to see a pattern

pairs.tendency: The same betting game is played twice with a different bet limit, and players compare how many folded, raised and won pots.
pros: Raises and folds can be counted
Shows what a limit does to bluffing
cons: Different cards dealt muddy the result
Players change style once they know the limit

pairs.tendency: Players pick sides in one game, then swap or change one choice and play again, comparing how each build did against the same rivals.
pros: Same rivals make the comparison fair
Shows what one choice added
cons: The second game starts with known weak spots
Sides take time to rebuild

pairs.tendency: The same hands are played with a changed contract, such as a higher call, and players compare which calls were met and which were missed.
pros: Hits and misses are easy to count
Shows how a call changes play
cons: Cards dealt differently change what can be met
Players choose safer calls after a miss

pairs.tendency: Players replay the capture game with one change, such as which pieces can convert, and compare how often the lead changed hands.
pros: Lead changes can be counted
Shows how a rule shapes comebacks
cons: A long game is slow to replay
Early captures can decide each game

pairs.tendency: A jail game is played again with one change, such as a longer jail time, and players compare how many were caught and freed.
pros: Captures and rescues can be counted
Shows what jail length changes
cons: Fast, tiring play leaves little time to compare
Players run harder after the first game

pairs.tendency: Players replay the surrounding game from the same opening with one rule changed, and compare which pieces were taken and where.
pros: A shared opening makes comparison fair
Shows what one rule changed on the board
cons: Positions split apart after a few moves
The first game's tactics get repeated

pairs.tendency: The game is played once with catch-up help and once without, and players compare how close the final scores were and when the lead changed.
pros: The gap between scores is easy to see
Shows what the help actually does
cons: Two games may not show a clear pattern
Players act differently when they know the help exists

pairs.tendency: A game of pure luck is played many times with one rule changed, and players compare results to see whether the change shows at all.
pros: Shows how little one rule matters
Games are quick to repeat
cons: Luck makes any single result meaningless
Players may find the comparison dull

pairs.tendency: The chase is played twice on a different area or with a different rule, and players compare how long each round lasted and who was caught.
pros: Round lengths are easy to time
Shows how space changes the chase
cons: Tiredness changes the second round
Players learn each other's habits

pairs.tendency: The same group plays twice with one change, such as hidden targets, and compares who was picked most and who held a grudge.
pros: Target counts reveal patterns
Shows how choices of target shift
cons: Players target by memory of the last game
Grudges can carry over

pairs.tendency: Players race to link the board edges in two games with one change, such as a different board size, and compare who linked first.
pros: Board size effects are easy to see
Shows how a small change shifts the chase
cons: Early moves matter more than the change
A first mover tends to repeat their gain

pairs.tendency: Players play the rock-paper-scissors style game twice with one added option, and compare how often each choice was played and won.
pros: Choice counts are quick to tally
Shows how a new option reshapes play
cons: Players adapt to each other within games
Short rounds leave little data

pairs.tendency: The same card game is replayed with a changed score for one declared pair or run, and players compare what they declared and when.
pros: Declared sets can be listed
Shows how a score shapes what gets held
cons: Different deals change what can be declared
Players hold the same sets they declared before

pairs.tendency: Players swap powers between games, each playing another person's power, and compare which powers seemed to give the most advantage.
pros: Each player tries every power
Shows what a power really gives
cons: Players learn the powers while playing
Two games are too few to rank them

pairs.tendency: The game is played with doubling in one round and without in the next, and players compare how many offers were made and accepted.
pros: Offers and refusals can be counted
Shows what doubling does to nerve
cons: One lucky double can swing the totals
Players change habits once they know the cost

pairs.tendency: The same position is played again with the forced capture removed, and players compare the moves made and how the game ended.
pros: Same position makes the change plain
Shows how far a forced move steers play
cons: Players know what happened last time
Positions split apart quickly

pairs.tendency: Two campaigns are played with a different growth rate, and players compare how strong characters were at the end and when they struggled.
pros: Strength over time can be charted
Shows how pacing changes challenge
cons: Long campaigns are slow to replay
Players carry knowledge of earlier fights

pairs.tendency: The list game is played twice with a changed rule, such as a time limit, and players compare how long the list grew before it broke.
pros: The final list length is easy to compare
Shows what a limit does to memory
cons: Different players tire at different points
Topics differ between the two games

pairs.tendency: A game is played with a handicap, then with a different one, and players compare how close the result was each time.
pros: The gap in the result is easy to read
Shows how much a handicap evens things out
cons: Players adjust their effort to the handicap
Finding a fair level takes many games

pairs.tendency: The hiding game is played again in a different place or with a different rule, and players compare how long it took to find the hider.
pros: Times to find are easy to compare
Shows how space changes the hunt
cons: Hiders reuse the first game's spots
Searchers remember where to look

pairs.tendency: Players replay the jumping game from the same set-up with one rule changed, and compare how many pieces were jumped and how it ended.
pros: A fixed set-up makes the change clear
Shows what one rule does to jumps
cons: Games split into different positions
Players avoid moves that failed before

pairs.tendency: Players play the reroll game with a different number of rerolls, and compare what scores they held and when they stopped.
pros: Scores by reroll count are easy to list
Shows what one extra roll is worth
cons: Dice luck can hide the change
Too few turns to see a pattern

pairs.tendency: The same race is played with the send-back rule changed, and players compare how often pieces were sent back and who won.
pros: Send-backs can be counted
Shows how a harsh rule changes the race
cons: Dice decide many of the sends
Players dread the rule after one rough game

pairs.tendency: The row game is replayed with a changed rule, such as fewer pieces, and players compare how often a row was made and which pieces were taken.
pros: Rows made can be counted
Shows how piece numbers shape play
cons: Early moves can decide each game
Players copy the opening that worked

pairs.tendency: The word game is replayed with a changed letter set or time limit, and players compare the words found and the scores reached.
pros: Word lists are easy to compare
Shows what a limit does to finding words
cons: Letter luck changes what is possible
Players reuse words from the first game

pairs.tendency: The matching game is played twice with a different tile set or hand size, and players compare how often someone had to pass.
pros: Passes can be counted
Shows how hand size shapes play
cons: Tile luck decides many turns
Little changes between the two games

pairs.tendency: Players meld in two games with one rule changed, such as when others may add to a meld, and compare the sets laid out.
pros: Laid out sets are easy to compare
Shows how a sharing rule changes play
cons: Different deals change the melds
Players hold back after seeing the first game

pairs.tendency: The game is replayed with powers used earlier or later by rule, and players compare when each power was spent and what it did.
pros: Spending times can be listed
Shows when a power tends to matter
cons: Players know the powers from last time
A power wasted early leaves little to compare

pairs.tendency: Players run the game with and without the other player's say, and compare how often offers were turned down or changed.
pros: Refusals can be counted
Shows what the say changes about offers

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled keep a secret and answer yes or no to questions, and the questions outsiders ask show what the outsiders do not yet understand.

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled keep the game going as a shared task, and its lasting length shows how long they would really keep something alive together.

Everyone has a part

Play may stall

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play a game no one can win, and say whether that matches how the problem feels to them.
pros: Honest about hard problems
Starts strong talk

Hard to know when testing is finished

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled work alone against the layout and say whether the pattern they have to clear looks like a problem they face.

Clear goal

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play several short games and see which results repeat, so each round is another check on the design.

Quick to try again

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled try a game where fewer points win, and say whether the points they avoid are the things they would also want to avoid.
pros: Shows what they want to avoid
Easy to compare
cons: Scoring can feel backwards
Points may stand for sore things

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled decide what the exact number stands for, and the game shows when real life too asks for just the right amount.
pros: Exactness mirrors real limits
Tense final turns
cons: Frustrating to miss by one
Testers may fixate on the count

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play to lose and say whether giving things away looks like something they do in real life.
pros: Shows what they give up
Surprise turns it round

Some may find it odd to play

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled each play their own copy side by side, and comparing the copies shows how their situations differ.
pros: Differences are easy to compare
Calm, even pace
cons: Little contact between testers
Their views stay apart

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled attack and sabotage each other in play, and say whether the fights match real quarrels or only look like a game.
pros: Conflict is checked against real ones
Lively talk
cons: Real grudges can surface
Arguments may follow them away from the table

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled affect one another through the board, and the game shows the quiet ways they already shape each other's lives.
pros: Quiet links become visible
Low risk of open quarrel
cons: Effects can be hard to spot
Outsiders may miss them

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play as one team against the game, so the shared problem they face is the whole of what is tested.
pros: Shared problem is clear
Everyone is part of it
cons: Little tension
One confident voice may lead

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled work together but each has a private aim, and the game shows how that tension runs in their own community.
pros: Shows self and group together
Realistic tension
cons: Private aims can strain friendships
Hard to balance in testing

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled split into teams, and the sides in the game match the real groups whose interests meet in their situation.
pros: Sides match real groups
Teams talk among themselves
cons: Teams may harden into real camps
One voice may speak for a team

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled find a traitor among them, and say whether the betrayal in the game looks like trust breaking in real life.
pros: Shows how trust works
Suspense
cons: Accusations can hurt
Real doubts can be stirred up

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled take turns by sending letters, so the game is tested over days and fits around their work.
pros: Fits people with little time
Lets distant people join
cons: Slow feedback
Letters can be lost or delayed

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled leave a place for someone who is not there, such as an elder or a person who moved away, and the game shows what that absence does.
pros: Brings in missing voices
Prompts memories
cons: Absence can sadden players
Rules for the missing one need care

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled can take the game master seat and run the world themselves, so the person who describes the setting is one who knows it.
pros: Setting told by those who know
Fast corrections
cons: A master may steer the test
Role is hard to hand over

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play in the open, and passers-by who join in offer opinions the designer would not otherwise hear.
pros: Extra voices join in
Easy to see who plays
cons: Public play can be rushed
Some may feel watched

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled can take the lone seat or the group side, and the game shows how it feels to be that one among many.
pros: Shows each side's view
Strong roles
cons: Lone player may feel singled out
Others may gang up in earnest

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled try the game alone, in private, and report back later on whether it rang true, without a group watching.
pros: Honest private feedback
Fits their own time
cons: Little to compare with others
Alone, they may not talk it through

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play a game of mostly luck and say whether it matches how much of their life is decided by things they cannot control.
pros: Shows how much is out of their hands
Light to test
cons: Little they do changes the result
Testers may find it empty

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled face hard luck but can prepare for it, and the ways to soften it come from what they truly do in a poor year.
pros: Shows real ways of coping
Choices matter
cons: More rules to check
Their real coping may not fit a card

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play a game of mostly skill with a little luck, and say whether the mix looks like how things go for them.
pros: Mix is checked by them
Some surprise
cons: Experienced players tend to win
Takes many rounds to judge

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play a game where only their choices count, and say whether it matches their own sense of how much a decision changes things.
pros: Choices have clear results
Easy to see who learned what
cons: Real life is rarely this predictable
Skilled players may talk over others

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled read a throw as a sign, and the game shows how they already read luck, omens or timing in their own lives.
pros: Shows their own habits of reading luck
Rich talk
cons: Outsiders may misread a belief
Signs are easy to treat as a joke

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled try to act together without speaking, and the game shows how well they already sense one another's timing.
pros: Shows how well they read each other
Quiet and close
cons: Strangers struggle to join
Hard to record what was learned

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled write the table the dice are read against, so each roll tells an event from their own place and time.
pros: Table holds local events
Stories come easily
cons: Table needs many rows
Rare events may be left out

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled see the whole board, so they can point at any part and say what is right or wrong with it.
pros: Easy to correct together
Nothing hidden from them
cons: Real life is rarely so open
Little surprise

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled hold secret cards, and the game shows how knowledge is spread unevenly among them in real life.
pros: Shows who knows what
Players stay curious
cons: Hard to plan together
Secrets can make some uneasy

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled take secret roles, and the game shows who they think might be on the other side in their own situation.
pros: Shows suspicion they feel
Lively mystery
cons: Real mistrust may spill over
Hard for others to read

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled work out a hidden fact from clues, and the clues are ones they would really use to find it.
pros: Clues come from real life
Satisfying when it clicks
cons: Outsiders may miss the clues
Slow for some

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled bluff, and the game shows how much of their real dealing rests on appearing strong or weak.
pros: Shows how they present themselves
Mind games
cons: Lies among neighbours may sting
Bluffing is hard to read

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled find out a hidden rule by breaking it, which mirrors how outsiders learn the unwritten rules they live by.
pros: Unwritten rules come to light
Strong curiosity
cons: Slow and frustrating
Insiders may find outsiders slow

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled know the answer but may only hint, which mirrors how they sometimes cannot say what they know to those outside.
pros: Shows what is hard to say
Playful
cons: Hints can mislead
Knower may feel stuck

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled uncover a map piece by piece, and those who know the place can say whether the reveal matches what is really there.
pros: Locals check what is found
Sense of discovery
cons: Locals already know the map
Reveals can seem staged

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled see one hand laid open, and the open hand stands for something about their lives that is already in plain view.
pros: Shows what is already known
Shared view eases talk
cons: Open hands remove surprise
One player may speak for it

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled keep some points hidden, and the game shows how much they would share about what they have or earn.
pros: Shows what they keep private
Quiet tension
cons: Totals cannot be checked
Secrecy can breed doubt

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled take turns, so each person is heard in order and each move can be discussed before the next.
pros: Everyone gets a say
Easy to follow
cons: Waiting for a turn slows testing
Quiet players can still be skipped

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled act together and reveal at the same moment, which tests how they would behave when nobody waits for anybody.
pros: Matches busy real life
Quick, and no one waits
cons: Hard to follow every move
Discussion is saved for after

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled act whenever they like, so the quickest speaks first and the design shows who normally gets heard first.
pros: Shows who gets in first
Lively
cons: Slower voices can be missed
Play can be noisy

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled move against a clock, which tests whether their real choices are made under the same hurry.
pros: Shows how they decide in a rush
Brisk
cons: Thoughtful comments can get lost
Clock may press the shy

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled make one move a day over weeks, so the game fits into their own days and tests how they live over time.
pros: Fits real routines
Lets feedback build slowly
cons: Players can drop away
Slow design cycle

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play slowly with pauses built in, which gives space to say what rings true or false before the next move.
pros: Time to think and comment
Calm
cons: Impatient testers may leave
Long sessions

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play as the pace rises, and the rush shows whether it matches how fast things move for them in real life.
pros: Shows how pressure builds
Exciting
cons: Little time to stop and comment
Ending in a rush can hide objections

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled see some players move twice, and say whether that matches who really gets an extra chance in their lives.
pros: Shows who gets extra chances
Quick momentum
cons: Long runs can look unfair
Others wait

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled play in stages, so early rounds can be checked and corrected before the later ones are built.
pros: Each stage is checked
Easier to change one part
cons: More rules to write
Stages may feel cut apart

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled check that the board behaves like the system they live inside, such as water moving between wells and fields.
pros: Model corrected by those inside it
Cause and effect are checked
cons: Their view may differ from the data

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled take their own roles or those of their neighbours, and others can ask whether the role is fair to the real group.
pros: Roles checked by the real group
Rich talk about needs
cons: Roles can turn into stereotypes
People may be asked to play themselves

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled draw on a shared resource, such as the water under a village, and say whether the way it runs out matches what they know.
pros: Rules checked by those who share it
Debate feels real
cons: Real quarrels over water can surface
Sources may be hard to measure

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled say how long real effects take to show, so a delay in the game matches the delays they have lived through.
pros: Delays are set by those who know
Shows slow cause and effect
cons: Long waits tire testers
Their memory of timing may differ

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled agree a rule together and see what it changes, so a rule is tried on the people who would live under it.
pros: Rules tested by those affected
Safe to change
cons: Agreement can be slow
Quieter members may not object

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled talk through the game afterwards, and their comments on what was true and what was not shape the next version.
pros: Feedback comes in a set place
Everyone can reflect
cons: Needs time to run properly
Strong voices may dominate it

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled see changes that cannot be undone, and say whether real changes in their lives work like that.
pros: Shows what cannot be undone
Weighty choices
cons: Test copies get used up

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled read the rules for the argument they make, and say whether the game says what they would say about their own situation.

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled stake real things on play, such as a promise to each other, and the game's choices carry into their lives.
pros: Play has a real effect
Players take it seriously
cons: Real stakes can cause hard feeling
Some may feel pressed to join

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled choose what the points stand for, so the score reflects the values they would name themselves.
pros: Scores show their values
Easy to compare results
cons: Points can shrink a value

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled practise a future they want, and their comments show whether the imagined way of living would work for them.

pros: Shows how little each can see
Guessing feels real
cons: Players may blame one another
Testers may feel lost

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled point out where things really get stuck in their work, so the slow step on the board is the one they would name.
pros: Slow step is named by those who face it
Insights about delay
cons: Their pointing may differ
Rare delays may be missed

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled say whether goods are made ahead or only on order, and the game shows the difference as they know it.
pros: Matches how work is really planned
Easy to compare

Terms may be unfamiliar to them

Players feel waiting and set-up
cons: Real batch sizes may be fixed
Numbers can be hard to agree

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled say how often equipment fails and how long repair takes, so breakdowns match what they have seen.
pros: Failures reflect their experience
Shows plans going wrong
cons: Recalled failures may differ
Real losses can be sore to replay

pairs.tendency: The people being modelled say what holding stock costs and what running out costs, so the balance in the game is set by their own sums.
pros: Costs checked by those who pay them
Balance feels real
cons: Their figures can be private

Stalled pieces leave downstream players idle.

Players meet the cost of a squeeze directly.
cons: Rich links outbid the rest every round.
Bidding can take over from ordering.

pairs.tendency: Each link keeps ordering more in hope of a big sale, and a sudden drop in demand leaves one player holding a pile of stock.

Tension builds as stock piles up.

pairs.tendency: Players hold areas that stand for shops or depots, and a link that supplies more areas gets more orders but is spread thin when stock runs short.

Busy maps hide the order flow.

pairs.tendency: Each link places workers on tasks such as making, packing and shipping, and a spot taken early leaves the next link waiting for goods.

pairs.tendency: Players lay out patterns that stand for routes and stock levels, and the pattern at one link shapes what the next link can build.
pros: Routes and links become visible.
Calm, steady building.

Little feel for orders arriving late.

pairs.tendency: Cards in hand stand for stock and orders, and each link decides which to send now and which to hold back, without seeing the other hands.
pros: Holding back shows why links keep spare stock.

cons: Small hands hide how far the chain reaches.

pairs.tendency: Each trick is a small sale between links, and the winner takes the goods, so strong hands tend to starve the links further down.
pros: Familiar card play with a trading meaning.
Rounds move quickly.
cons: The link to goods and orders can feel thin.
Strong hands decide much of the outcome.

pairs.tendency: Links talk across the chain, trading promises about what they will make and when, and a broken promise at one link shows up as empty shelves at the next.
pros: Players hear how trust keeps goods moving.
Talk shows what each link knows.
cons: Loud players can steer the whole chain.
Talk can go round the rules.

pairs.tendency: Links gather matching sets of parts or goods, and a missing piece at one link holds up every set further along.
pros: One missing part visibly stops a finished set.
Collecting gives each link a clear aim.
cons: Sets can feel like a checklist.
Orders and delays stay in the background.

pairs.tendency: Players place tiles for depots, roads and shops, and the layout decides how far goods travel and how long orders take to come back.
pros: Layout shows why distance costs time.
The chain grows in front of players.
cons: Tile luck can wreck a sound plan.
Building can matter more than ordering.

pairs.tendency: Each link answers the one beside it, an order called up the chain and a delivery called back, so the chain is a back and forth of short messages.
pros: Calls and answers match orders and deliveries.

pairs.tendency: Links cannot speak, so each reads orders only from the cards that arrive, and players guess what the next link needs from what it last asked for.

Players read the chain's signals closely.

Idle links grow bored.

pairs.tendency: Players change the rules of how orders and deliveries work, so one link's new rule can help itself and hurt the next one down the chain.

Players try new ways of ordering.
cons: Rules can pile up faster than the chain settles.
The supply chain may be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: Each player acts as a maker, wholesaler or shopkeeper, speaking for that link, and decisions come from what that character would want from the chain.
pros: Players see the chain from one seat.
Talk stays in character.
cons: Acting can drown out the ordering numbers.
Shy players may sit out.

pairs.tendency: Players move goods by flicking, stacking or balancing, so a shaky hand at one link spills stock and sets the next link back.
pros: Clumsy hands cost goods, like real handling.

cons: Skill with hands can outweigh ordering skill.
Dropped goods can stop the whole chain.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the roads, depots and shops as the game goes, so the chain's shape comes from where each link chooses to build.

Drawing keeps everyone involved.
cons: Messy maps are hard to follow.
Drawing can slow the ordering.

pairs.tendency: On a turn a link asks another for a card it needs, and each ask tells the others what is short, so requests double as orders and as gossip.

cons: Open asks reveal plans to everyone.
A link asked too often runs dry.

pairs.tendency: One player is the bank, setting the odds on demand, while the others bet on what orders will arrive and stock up to match.
pros: Bets show how people guess demand.
The rotating bank shares the risk.
cons: Betting can take over from supplying.
Money stakes can drown out stock.

pairs.tendency: Players bet before a throw sets demand for the round, and links stock up on the strength of those bets before they know the result.
pros: Stock decisions are made under real uncertainty.
Tension rises before each throw.
cons: Chance decides who is right.
Little room for steady planning.

pairs.tendency: Links put chips in as they judge their stock can cover orders, and a link that stays in on weak stock loses what it staked.

Dropping out is a real choice.
cons: Chips can matter more than goods.
Players with few chips stop early.

pairs.tendency: Each player arrives with a chosen link, such as a small maker or a large depot, so chains differ in size and speed from the first round.
pros: Different links feel different to play.
Choices before play give a sense of ownership.
cons: Uneven links can leave one player stuck.
Hard to balance a chain.

pairs.tendency: Before a round, each link promises to deliver a set amount, and a link that falls short leaves the next link unable to meet its own promise.
pros: Promises show how one failure spreads.
Planning ahead feels weighty.
cons: Failed promises can leave players frustrated.
Cautious promises keep the chain slow.

pairs.tendency: Taking a rival's depot or shop makes it yours, so it now supplies your chain, and a leading chain can lose a link in one move.

Players who lose a link may drop out.

pairs.tendency: A link that is caught waits in jail while its goods stop, and a free teammate who gets through can restart the flow.

Teammates have a reason to help.
cons: A jailed player waits and watches.
Chasing can pull play from the chain.

pairs.tendency: Players surround a depot or shop until it cannot send or receive, and cut links stop passing goods and orders along the chain.

Quiet, thoughtful play.
cons: The chain can matter less than the surrounding.
A cut link can stay stuck for rounds.

pairs.tendency: Links that fall behind on stock or orders get a boost, so a chain wobbling from a late delivery can recover before the game ends.

Everyone stays in the game.
cons: Help can hide the cost of a poor order.
Leading players may feel held back.

pairs.tendency: Dice or cards set the orders and deliveries, so the chain runs with no choices from the players.
pros: Shows what is out of the chain's reach.
Easy to explain, quick to play.
cons: Players learn little from their own moves.
The chain's structure may go unnoticed.

pairs.tendency: One player is It and chases the rest, and a link that is tagged stops sending goods until it is free again, which backs up the chain.
pros: Tags show what a stopped link costs.
Lively and physical.
cons: Running can drown out the order flow.
Whoever is It sets the pace for all.

pairs.tendency: Each turn a link picks whom to supply, delay or take from, so choosing a customer also decides which link in the chain gets starved.

Targets give players a reason to talk.
cons: Some links may be picked on.
More players give more targets to track.

pairs.tendency: Players try to link two sides of the board with an unbroken chain of depots, and a gap anywhere stops goods from getting across.

A clear aim for building.
cons: A real supply chain is more than a line.
Cutting a rival's line can take over.

pairs.tendency: Each choice beats one other and loses to a third, so links keep guessing whether the next one will over-order, under-order or hold steady.
pros: Guessing keeps every player alert.
Short and tense rounds.
cons: The cycle hides stock and delay.
Little sense of a flowing chain.

pairs.tendency: Links show a pair or a run of goods they hold to score points, which also tells the others what stock they carry and what they might sell on.
pros: Showing stock sets up honest trades.
Points reward holding the right goods.
cons: Showing stock reveals plans.
Scoring can crowd out the orders.

pairs.tendency: Each link has its own special power, such as a fast truck or a large store, so each reaches for different tricks and the chain plays unevenly.
pros: Each seat feels different, like real jobs.
Players can lean on a link's strength.
cons: Powers can skew the whole chain.
Many powers to explain.

pairs.tendency: A link may offer to double what a round is worth, and the next accepts or concedes, so a hopeful order pushes risk down the chain.
pros: Players see how risk travels.
Tense, short choices.
cons: Doubling can swamp the stock decisions.
A forced concession is felt by one link.

pairs.tendency: A link that can take stock or a depot has to, so its move is set for it, and a rival can use that to push a chain short.
pros: Forced moves show how rules limit a chain.
Tactics are easy to follow.
cons: Fixed moves can wreck a careful plan.
Little room to adjust ordering.

pairs.tendency: A link builds up its own capacity over rounds, such as more trucks or storage, so later orders are easier to meet than the first few were.
pros: Growing capacity gives a clear sense of progress.
Early orders are a real stretch.
cons: Strong links can leave weak ones behind.
Growth can pull focus from the chain.

pairs.tendency: Each player recites the whole list of orders and deliveries so far, then adds one, so the chain's history is held only in everyone's memory.
pros: Memory stands in for the order book.
Light and easy to start.
cons: Long lists lose people.
Little room for real stock decisions.

pairs.tendency: The stronger player's link starts with less stock or slower trucks, which evens out chain play but can leave a skilled player short of goods to make use of.
pros: Weaker players have a real chance.
Strong players find a harder chain.
cons: Handicaps can look unfair to the one handicapped.
A handicap can bend the chain's real behaviour.

pairs.tendency: Stock or an order is hidden somewhere in the chain and the others hunt for it, so links wait while a missing batch is found.
pros: Lost goods are felt as delay.
Players search together.
cons: The chase can take over from supplying.
A hider who is slow stalls the chain.

pairs.tendency: A piece hops over another, which here means a link skipping past the one beside it, and the skipped link is left out of the flow.
pros: Skipping a link shows why middlemen exist.
Jumps give quick, visible moves.
cons: Jumping can ignore the chain's order.
Skipped links may drop out of play.

pairs.tendency: A link rolls dice for what it can make, keeps the ones it likes and rerolls the rest, so output varies and the next link feels the swing.
pros: Players feel output vary at each link.
Rerolls give a sense of control.
cons: Luck can drown out ordering.
Smooth output can look easy to fake.

pairs.tendency: A link that lands on another's space sends it back to the start, so a delivery can be wiped out and the next link waits for a fresh one.
pros: Setbacks are easy to see in the chain.
Short, lively moves.
cons: A sent-back link can feel punished.
Late deliveries can hit the whole line.

pairs.tendency: Making a row of three lets a player take a rival's piece, and here a taken piece is a depot cut out of a rival's chain.
pros: Taking a depot shows what a lost link costs.
Clear, short goals.
cons: The chain can take second place to the rows.
Cut links stay cut for rounds.

pairs.tendency: Players spell words from letter tiles and pass them down the chain, each link adding or fixing letters, so a slip at the maker shows up at the shop.
pros: Errors spread and become visible.
Words give a familiar task.
cons: Spelling skill can outweigh ordering.
The chain can feel like a gimmick.

pairs.tendency: Links add goods only where a number matches an open end, and a link with no match waits, so supply and demand have to meet at one point.
pros: Matching shows why mismatched goods sit idle.
Waiting links are easy to see.
cons: Misses can stall a whole line.
Tile luck can outweigh planning.

pairs.tendency: A link lays out a finished set of goods face up, and others add matching goods, so one link's finished batch can supply the next link.
pros: Open sets show what is on hand.
Adding to sets feels cooperative.
cons: The chain's order flow is hard to see.
Many sets to keep track of.

pairs.tendency: Each link holds a power it can spend once, such as a rush order, so players pick when to use it, and a rush at one link stretches the next.
pros: Timing a rush shows why spare capacity matters.
Each power gives a tense moment.
cons: Spent powers leave links weaker later.
Many powers to track.

pairs.tendency: A link offers a delivery and the next link may turn it down or pick between two, so each side in the chain shapes what the other gets.
pros: Players see that supply needs a partner.
Choices feel shared.
cons: Refusals can stall the chain.
A fussy partner slows each round.

pairs.tendency: An order is whispered link by link up the chain, so what the maker hears can differ from what the shop meant to ask for.
pros: Orders drift the way real orders do.
Funny and easy to follow.
cons: Garbled orders can feel unfair.
No one can check the message en route.

pairs.tendency: Before play, each link hands some cards to the next without seeing what it gets back, so stock arrives that nobody asked for.
pros: Unasked stock shows what a push is like.
Quick to set up.
cons: Players may feel the swap is arbitrary.
Passed cards can break careful plans.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up the chain and the other picks which end to play, so the setter tries to give both ends the same chance of trouble.
pros: Even set-ups give both players a fair start.
Setting up shows how each link differs.
cons: A set-up with many links is hard to balance.
Players may argue over what is even.

pairs.tendency: A piece that gets stock to the far end of the board turns into a stronger link, such as a bigger depot, so there is reason to push goods through.
pros: Reaching the end gives a clear prize.
Players push goods along.
cons: Pushing ahead can leave nothing at home.
A promoted link can leap ahead.

pairs.tendency: Goods run down the chain in legs, each link handing on to the next, and the team that gets its goods all the way through first wins.
pros: The chain and the race match closely.
Teammates cheer each leg.
cons: Speed can matter more than careful ordering.
A slow link holds up the whole team.

pairs.tendency: Links that build a safe shape of depots keep their stock from being taken, so a protected chain can run steadily while others lose stock to rivals.
pros: Safety gives a chain room to plan.
A clear shape gives a clear aim.
cons: Safe shapes cost building time.
The chain can slip down the list.

pairs.tendency: The prizes in the game are named cards, such as the biggest order, and links are drawn to the goods that win them rather than to whatever the chain needs.
pros: Prizes steer where goods are sent.
Clear targets for each link.
cons: Chasing prizes can distort the chain.
One card can swing a round.

pairs.tendency: Cards turned up in the middle stand for the market everyone sells into, and each link combines them with its own stock to meet demand.
pros: An open market shows what everyone faces.
Players read demand together.
cons: Open cards leave little hidden information.
The shared pool can crowd out the chain.

pairs.tendency: Every link puts a counter in a common pot, and if nobody earns it, it grows, so a stalled chain can leave a large prize waiting.
pros: The growing pot shows what idle goods cost.
Players pay attention to every round.
cons: A huge pot can distort ordering.
One lucky win can end the tension.

pairs.tendency: Players scoop seeds and drop them one at a time along a row of pits, so a handful sent from one pit spreads thinly down the line.
pros: Spreading seeds shows how stock thins out.
Familiar, hands-on play.
cons: Counting seeds can swamp the orders.
The chain's direction may be lost.

pairs.tendency: An extra hand of stock sits in the middle, and one link can take, swap or buy it before play, so a lucky pick changes what that link starts with.
pros: Spare stock gives one link an early boost.
Extra choice before play.
cons: The spare hand can skew the chain.
One link may start far ahead.

pairs.tendency: Some spaces on the track keep goods safe, send them back or cost a turn, so a delivery that lands on the wrong space holds up the next link.
pros: Delays and shelters are easy to see.
Squares give the track character.
cons: Squares can crowd out orders.
Hard to link an unlucky square to the chain.

pairs.tendency: Every card or truck has a price, so each link pays to make, move and store goods, and buying more capacity eats the money for stock.
pros: Prices make every choice a trade-off.
Players weigh costs openly.
cons: Counting costs can slow the game.
Poor links may never afford capacity.

pairs.tendency: Each link has a fixed amount of effort to share out between making, moving and storing, so more in one place means less in another.
pros: Sharing out shows the cost of every choice.
Players plan across several jobs.
cons: Splits can feel the same every round.
Rivals sharing out too raises the guesswork.

pairs.tendency: Everyone keeps moving goods until a signal sounds, and the slowest link when it stops is caught holding the stock.
pros: The signal gives a sudden end to waiting.
Fast, noisy and fun.
cons: Panic can cancel careful ordering.
The slowest player is caught every time.

pairs.tendency: Links put cards back and take new ones from a pile, sometimes with a partner's agreement, so stock that does not fit is exchanged for stock that does.
pros: Swapping shows how mismatched stock is fixed.
Choice keeps hands useful.
cons: Swaps can depend on a partner's mood.
Swap rules add steps to every round.

pairs.tendency: Players discard onto one pile and may take it all, so one link can sweep up a heap of stock and leave the others bare.
pros: A heap shows what hoarding does.
Quick, dramatic grabs.
cons: One grab can break the chain.
Careful links may end up with nothing.

pairs.tendency: One suit beats the others, so the goods in that suit are in demand and links with them gain, while others get passed by.
pros: A strong suit shows what a hot product does.
Demand changes the whole hand.
cons: The chain can fade behind the trump.
Links without trumps lose heart.

pairs.tendency: Each player is a supplier on one board and a customer on the other, so one link's choices are felt from both sides at once.
pros: Playing both sides shows how roles depend.
Plenty to think about each turn.
cons: Attention is split across two boards.
Many rules to teach.

pairs.tendency: A wild card can stand for any goods, so a link with a spare can fill a gap in an order that would otherwise leave a shelf empty.
pros: A spare card shows how flexible stock helps.
Gaps feel less final.
cons: Wilds can hide poor ordering.
Players hoard wild cards.

pairs.tendency: A chain runs off one edge of the board and carries on from the other, so the last link and the first link sit beside each other.
pros: The chain can be seen as a loop.
Distances are easy to compare.
cons: Loops can confuse who supplies whom.
Players may lose track of the chain's direction.

pairs.tendency: One link knows what the shop really needs, and the others ask yes or no questions up the chain, so each question narrows what to make.
pros: Questions work like a stream of small orders.
Easy to join in.
cons: Too many questions slow the chain.
Answers do not show stock.

pairs.tendency: Each chain races to get a given amount of goods through to the end first, so every link's delay or delivery shows in who wins.
pros: A clear finish makes delays plain.
Easy to follow who leads.
cons: Racing can push links to ignore orders.
Leaders pull away if one link is quick.

pairs.tendency: Points come from filled orders, stock kept low and goods sold, so the score at the end shows how well each chain served its customers.
pros: Points show what each choice earned.
Players compare their chains.
cons: Points can matter more than the chain.
Scoring can be slow to tally.

pairs.tendency: A chain that cannot fill its orders drops out until one is left, so a link that runs out of stock can end the game for its whole chain.
pros: Running out has a plain cost.
Tense from the first round.
cons: Out players wait and watch.
One mistake can finish a chain.

pairs.tendency: The links work together to keep the chain supplying until the game ends, so any one link's failure threatens every link.
pros: Every link depends on the others.
Plans are made together.
cons: One player can direct the rest.
A failing link can lead to blame.

pairs.tendency: The links share one target, such as getting a fixed number of goods to the shop, so each link's ordering helps or holds back the whole group.
pros: Teamwork matches the chain's shape.
A clear, shared aim.
cons: Players may follow the loudest voice.
Little tension between links.

pairs.tendency: Each link secretly wants something different, such as the lowest cost or the largest stock, so players pull the chain in different directions without saying so.
pros: Different aims show why links disagree.
Hidden motives add mystery.
cons: Hidden goals can hide the chain's own behaviour.
Hard to tell a mistake from a plan.

pairs.tendency: The chain's orders and deliveries unfold as a story that ends when the goods reach the shop, so each round adds a line to the tale.
pros: Stories make the chain easy to remember.
Players recall what happened.
cons: A story can blur how the chain behaves.
The ending may feel fixed.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, and players move goods and orders along the chain and then look at the stock and delays that built up.
pros: Players study the chain without pressure.
Easy to talk about afterwards.
cons: Players may lose their drive to try.
Little reason to make hard choices.

pairs.tendency: Each link decides what a successful run means, such as low stock, quick delivery or low cost, and the chain is then judged by different measures at once.
pros: Different aims show what each link values.
Players think about their own priorities.
cons: Aims can clash and stall the chain.
Hard to compare results.

pairs.tendency: The chain plays on until one link fails, such as the one that runs out first, and the others are safe, so everyone watches the weakest link.
pros: The weakest link becomes obvious.
Tense for every player.
cons: One player can feel singled out.
Players may hold stock back from others.

pairs.tendency: Links aim to keep goods and orders moving for as many rounds as they can, and success means a chain that never stalls.
pros: A steady flow shows what a working chain does.
Players cooperate over the long run.
cons: Nothing marks a finish.
Long games can wear thin.

pairs.tendency: The chain is built so that nobody can fill every order, and each link finds that stock and orders never quite match.
pros: Players see the limits of a chain.
Surprising and thought-provoking.
cons: Players may feel the game is pointless.
Some players quit early.

pairs.tendency: One player runs a whole chain alone against a fixed layout of orders, and wins by filling every one without running out.
pros: Alone, the chain's rhythm is easy to see.
Players can try again and again.
cons: No other links to learn from.
A stuck layout can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: Players run the chain several times and the winner takes the most games, so they carry what they learn about delays from one game to the next.
pros: Repeat games show what experience does.
Players can try new ordering.
cons: One unlucky game can feel big.
Many games take time.

pairs.tendency: Each unsold item or late order adds points against a link, so the chain with the least waste or delay wins.
pros: Waste is easy to measure.
Lean chains are rewarded.
cons: Players may starve the chain to avoid points.
Penalties can feel harsh.

pairs.tendency: A link has to send exactly the number of goods the next link ordered, so sending too many or too few both lose the round.
pros: Exact amounts match real order counts.
Counting is clear.
cons: Small errors can cost whole rounds.
Frustrating when stock falls short.

pairs.tendency: The aim is to be the first link to be rid of all its stock, so players push goods down the chain as fast as they can.
pros: Pushing stock on is easy to see.
A twist on how a chain works.
cons: The aim can confuse a first-time player.
The chain's ordering matters less.

pairs.tendency: Each player runs their own chain side by side, so everyone faces the same orders but no one's stock affects another's.
pros: Chains can be compared like for like.
Calm and easy to start.
cons: Little contact between players.
Links inside one chain are not shown.

pairs.tendency: Players attack each other's chains, delaying orders or taking stock, so a rival's raid shows up as empty shelves down the line.
pros: Attacks show how fragile a chain is.
Lively and dramatic.
cons: Fighting can crowd out the supply.
Players can feel picked on.

pairs.tendency: Players share one chain, and one link's choices change what the others can order or ship without any attack, so causes of a shortage spread across the table.
pros: One link's choice is felt by all.
Quiet, thoughtful play.
cons: Causes of a delay can be hard to see.
Slow turns.

pairs.tendency: The whole team runs one chain together, so every link's order and delivery helps or harms everyone.
pros: Shared effort fits a chain.
Everyone has a part.
cons: One player may direct the others.
Little tension between players.

pairs.tendency: Links work together to keep goods flowing, but each also wants its own gain, so one link can profit while the next runs short.
pros: Self-interest and the chain pull against each other.
Tense, honest choices.
cons: A selfish link can ruin the chain.
Hard to balance.

pairs.tendency: Two teams each run a chain and compete to serve the same customers, so teammates share stock and orders with each other but not with the rivals.
pros: Teamwork across a chain is clear.
Rival chains are easy to compare.
cons: One strong player can take over a team.
Rivalry can hide how the chain works.

pairs.tendency: One link on the team secretly spoils the chain, by over-ordering or holding stock, and the others see only late deliveries and empty shelves.
pros: Delays make everyone suspicious.
Tense and lively.
cons: Hard to tell sabotage from a normal swing.
Accusations can upset players.

pairs.tendency: Links send orders and deliveries by letter, so each wait for a reply stands for the real delay in a chain, and rounds can take days.
pros: The wait is itself the lesson.
Slow, thoughtful play.
cons: Players may lose track of the stock.
The game can drag on.

pairs.tendency: One link in the chain is not at the table, such as a maker from a past game, so players order from a gap and guess what comes back.
pros: An absent link shows what unseen suppliers do.
Players think about who is missing.
cons: Guessing can feel arbitrary.
The absent link can feel like a ghost.

pairs.tendency: One player runs the world around the chain, setting customer orders and events, while the others play the links and answer each round.
pros: The master can shape demand to teach a point.
Players have a steady guide.
cons: The master can sway the whole game.
That player does not get to play a link.

pairs.tendency: The chain is played in a street or a market, and passers-by can join as customers or links, so demand arrives from people nobody planned for.
pros: Real passers-by make demand feel real.
Open to anyone.
cons: Players come and go unevenly.
Hard to keep the chain whole.

pairs.tendency: All but one player form the chain, and the lone player sets demand or sabotages, so the links have to work together against one rival.
pros: The chain has a clear opponent.
Links learn to work together.
cons: The lone player may feel outnumbered.
A weak link wastes the team's effort.

pairs.tendency: One player runs every link in turn, placing orders and receiving goods from themselves, so the delay in the chain is the only thing they cannot control.
pros: Shows how delay alone causes trouble.
Easy to start without others.
cons: The chain can feel too easy to plan.
Misses the guessing that other players bring.

pairs.tendency: Dice or cards set customer demand and delivery times, so each link orders into a random world and cannot tell skill from luck, and poor rolls look like poor ordering.
pros: Shows how much is out of anyone's hands.
Light and quick.
cons: Few choices for players.
Players may feel nothing they do matters.

pairs.tendency: Random demand and late deliveries hit the chain, but links can keep spare stock or order early to soften them.
pros: Spare stock earns its place.
Choices against luck feel real.
cons: Safety stock costs money each round.
Planning can feel small against an unlucky run.

pairs.tendency: Ordering skill drives most of the result, and a little random demand keeps each round from being solved.
pros: Careful ordering shows in the result.
Some surprise stays.
cons: Experienced players tend to win.
A slow, thoughtful game.

pairs.tendency: Demand and delivery follow fixed patterns, so players can work out a strong order rule by thinking and testing.
pros: Every result has a clear cause.
Rewards close study of the chain.
cons: Real chains are rarely this predictable.
Skilled players can dominate.

pairs.tendency: Dice are read as signs about the next round's demand, so a link orders on what a throw seems to say rather than on any stock count.
pros: Players think about how they read signals.
Strange and memorable.
cons: Signs give no real stock information.
Players may order wildly.

pairs.tendency: Links try to sense what the next link needs without being told, and a link that guesses well sends the right amount without an order.
pros: Reading a partner stands in for forecasting.
Warm and close play.
cons: Hard to explain or repeat.
