Players who miss the mood feel left out.

pairs.tendency: A roll on a table says what happens to the chain, such as a late lorry or a bumper harvest, and the story of each round comes from the dice.
pros: Each round gives something new to respond to.
Stories are easy to share.
cons: The table can swamp the chain's own pattern.
Chance can decide the story.

pairs.tendency: Every link can see every stock level and order, so players plan for the whole chain with nothing hidden.
pros: Open numbers are easy to discuss.
Players can compare each link's choices.
cons: Real chains hide most of this.
Little surprise.

pairs.tendency: Each link holds its own stock and orders face down, so no one sees the whole chain and each guesses what the others hold.
pros: Hidden stock matches how chains work.
Guessing adds mystery.
cons: Hard to plan together.
Players can be confused about what is short.

pairs.tendency: Players secretly belong to different sides, some serving the chain and some working against it, so a late delivery might be an accident or a plan.
pros: Suspicion shows in every shortage.
Tense, watchful play.
cons: Hard to tell causes of delay.
Accusations can upset players.

pairs.tendency: Players work out what is happening upstream from the orders and deliveries that reach them, so a pattern of late goods points to a cause.
pros: Clues from orders reward close watching.
Satisfying when a cause is found.
cons: Hard for some.
Slow if clues are thin.

pairs.tendency: A link can claim it has more or less stock than it does, so orders and promises along the chain may not tell the truth.
pros: Players see how false numbers spread.
Mind games between links.
cons: Lies can upset players.
Players may stop trusting the chain.

pairs.tendency: One player knows how the chain really works, such as the delay between order and delivery, and the others find out only by ordering and watching what arrives.
pros: Delays come as a real surprise.
Discovery keeps players curious.
cons: Being told no feels harsh.
The first rounds can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: One link knows the shop's true demand but may only hint, so the others set their orders by guessing from hints, as a real maker guesses from distant orders.
pros: Shows how far demand is from what upstream sees.
Players listen closely.
cons: Hints can mislead.
One player is held back from helping.

pairs.tendency: The map of depots and shops is turned over as links explore it, so nobody knows how long the chain is or where demand sits.
pros: Exploring feels like discovering a chain.
Surprise at each new link.
cons: Hard to plan while the map is hidden.
Early rounds can feel random.

pairs.tendency: One chain's stock lies face up for all, so everyone can see one link's stock while their own stays secret.
pros: An open link shows what stock looks like.
Others can learn from it.
cons: One link becomes a worked example, not a player.
Hidden stock elsewhere stays unexplained.

pairs.tendency: Each link keeps some of its profit or cost secret, so no one is sure which chain is ahead and links cannot tell if their order is working.
pros: Guessing who leads feels like a real market.
Surprise at the end.
cons: Hard to compare chains.
Players may lose track of their own result.

pairs.tendency: Each link acts in turn, ordering and delivering one after another, so a choice made at one end reaches the other end only as the turns pass.
pros: Delay is easy to see turn by turn.
Everyone can follow the chain.
cons: Waiting players lose interest.
Long chains make long rounds.

pairs.tendency: All links choose their orders at the same moment and reveal together, so nobody waits and no link knows what the next has asked for.
pros: Matches how real orders cross.
Everyone stays busy.
cons: Mix-ups are common.
Fast play can hide the flow.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can order or ship at any moment, and the quickest link gets goods first, so stock flows in bursts rather than in neat rounds.
pros: Rush and wait feel real.
Lively and loud.
cons: Quick players can swamp slow ones.
Hard to follow who ordered what.

pairs.tendency: Each link has a clock for its order, and a late move is made for it, so rushed orders and missed deliveries show up down the chain.
pros: Time pressure matches real orders.
Rounds stay quick.
cons: Panic can lead to mistakes.
Slow players are left behind.

pairs.tendency: The chain runs over real days, one order or delivery a day, so a late delivery means waiting until tomorrow.
pros: Delay is felt in real time.
Players think of the chain between turns.
cons: Players may forget the game.
One missing player stalls everyone.

pairs.tendency: Each link is made to pause before ordering, so the chain runs slowly and each order is thought over before it is sent.
pros: Calm gives time to see the whole chain.
Fewer rushed orders.
cons: Players may lose interest.
The slowness can hide the delays that matter.

pairs.tendency: Demand rises and rounds shorten as the game goes on, so links that coped early are swamped late and shortages spread faster.
pros: Pressure shows where a chain strains.
The end comes in a rush.
cons: Late rounds may feel chaotic.
Slow starters cannot catch up.

pairs.tendency: A lucky link gets another go at once and sends more goods before the others move, so stock surges to the next link in a lump.
pros: Surges show how uneven flow arrives.
Lucky moments are exciting.
cons: One player can run ahead.
Waiting players lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Play opens with planning and moves to running the chain, so the stock and prices set in the first stage shape every order in the second.
pros: Early choices show their cost later.
Each stage has its own task.
cons: Planning mistakes cannot be fixed.
Stages add rules to learn.

pairs.tendency: The chain stands for a real one, with real delays and real stock, so what a link does in the game is close to what it would do outside it.
pros: Players see a real system's cause and effect.
Delays and queues become familiar.
cons: Real chains are far larger.
A simple model may mislead.

pairs.tendency: Each link plays a real group such as a farmer, a trader or a shopkeeper, with its own aims, so the chain shows what each seat wants.
pros: Players see each group's view.
Talk is easy to start.
cons: Players may play to a stereotype.
Real groups are more varied than the roles.

pairs.tendency: Every link draws on one limited supply, such as grain or water, so a link that orders big leaves less for the links beside it.
pros: Shortages reach everyone.
Players see why hoarding hurts.
cons: One greedy link can empty the supply.
The chain's order flow can be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: An order placed now arrives only a few rounds later, so links keep ordering more while they wait and then find too much arriving at once.
pros: Players feel why orders overshoot.
The delay is plain on the table.
cons: Players may blame others for their own over-ordering.
Early rounds can feel confusing.

pairs.tendency: Players agree a new rule for the chain, such as a cap on orders, and play on to see how stock and delays change.
pros: A rule's effect is easy to see.
A safe way to test a change.
cons: One round may not show the full effect.
Arguments over which rule to try.

pairs.tendency: After a round of orders and deliveries, players talk through what happened, why the stock swung and how it is like a real shop or factory.
pros: Players find the causes behind the swings.
Real chains become easy to discuss.
cons: Players may blame each other.
Talk can run long.

pairs.tendency: Stock lost or a depot closed stays gone, and the next game starts from the damaged chain, so no round can be undone.
pros: Mistakes carry real weight.
Play has a long memory.
cons: Early mistakes can ruin later games.
New players may feel doomed.

pairs.tendency: The rules for orders, delivery and cost make a point about how chains work, such as that each link acting alone causes swings in the whole.
pros: Players see how rules shape results.
A point is made through play, not talk.
cons: Players may reject the argument.
The point may be too narrow.

pairs.tendency: A late delivery or an empty shelf has a real consequence, such as a chore or a promise, so each link's mistake is felt by the others outside the game.
pros: Mistakes carry weight.
Players think hard about orders.
cons: Blame can leak into real life.
Some players feel pressured.

pairs.tendency: Points stand for things such as fair pay or fresh goods, so links chase points and the chain shows what is lost when a number replaces the value.
pros: Players see how a number can distort a chain.
Discussion about real trade-offs.
cons: Points can overtake what they stand for.
Hard to choose what counts.

pairs.tendency: Players run a supply chain that does not exist yet, such as one that shares stock between villages, to see how orders and delays would feel.
pros: A new chain can be tried safely.
Players spot problems before a real start.
cons: A played chain is simpler than a real one.
Players may trust it too much.

pairs.tendency: Each link sees only its own stock and the orders that reach it, never the whole chain, and has to guess what is happening upstream and downstream.
pros: Players feel why chains swing.
Guessing is tense.
cons: Hard to see the cause of a delay.
Players may blame the next link.

pairs.tendency: The chain has one slow link, so extra stock and speed elsewhere piles up in front of it and nothing reaches the shop faster.
pros: Players see where one link caps everyone.
Fixing the right link shows a clear result.
cons: Players may spend effort on the wrong link.
The slow link's player can feel blamed.

pairs.tendency: Links either make goods to a guess and push them along, or wait for an order and pull them through, and the chain feels different each way.
pros: Players feel the difference first-hand.
Stock levels show what each way costs.
cons: Pull can leave shelves empty.
Push can leave stock unsold.

pairs.tendency: Each link picks how many goods to send at once, so big batches fill lorries but leave the next link waiting, while small ones move goods at higher cost.
pros: Batch choice shows the trade of speed and cost.
Waiting and setup both visibly cost something.
cons: Big batches make demand swings larger.
Small batches can raise costs.

pairs.tendency: A machine at one link fails at random and has to be repaired, so the goods behind it stop and every link further on runs short.
pros: Breakdowns show why spare stock matters.
A plan built on everything working fails visibly.
cons: Random failure can feel unfair.
One broken link can end a round for all.

pairs.tendency: Each link pays to hold stock and pays more when it runs out, so every order is a guess between a full shelf and an empty one.
pros: Both kinds of cost are plain on the table.
Players weigh holding against running out.
cons: Orders can swing between too much and too little.
Players may blame the next link.

pairs.tendency: You roll and move along a path, landing on spaces that change your own stock, while the rest of the system stays out of sight and you guess what others face.
pros: Simple turns while the guessing builds.
Rolls feel like news from elsewhere.
cons: Dice can look like the cause of every shortage.
Players may not link a roll to the orders they get.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards from your hand and pass the rest on, seeing only your own stock, so what the next player needs is guessed from what you are sent.
pros: Passed cards become small clues.
Quick picks keep the game moving.
cons: Picks rest on guesses, not facts.
Effects further down the line go unnoticed.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for stock from their own corner with no view of what others hold, so prices come from guesses about scarcity elsewhere.
pros: Prices act as the one shared signal.
Bids show what each player fears.
cons: Players may overpay out of worry.
Bids can drift away from real shortage.

pairs.tendency: You keep ordering more for your own corner without knowing what others hold, and nobody can tell when the whole system will tip.
pros: Each extra order feels like a real gamble.
Guessing the limit is tense.
cons: Thin information looks like ill luck.
Careful players may never find where the limit lies.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds their own area and sees only what passes through it, so claims elsewhere are known only by their effects.
pros: Fewer things to track at once.
Surprises from other areas keep play lively.
cons: Players may fight over areas they cannot see.
The map is hard to read as a whole.

pairs.tendency: You place workers to run your own corner and see only the orders that reach you, so plans rest on guesses about what others are doing.
pros: Planning is simple because the view is small.
Players feel how narrow their view is.
cons: Spaces get blocked for reasons nobody sees.
Planning can turn into blind guessing.

pairs.tendency: Each player builds a pattern in their own corner without seeing the rest, and only at the end does the whole picture show whether the parts fit.
pros: Calm building with a reveal at the end.
Each player owns a small, clear task.
cons: Parts may not fit together.
The reveal can feel like blame.

pairs.tendency: You hold cards for your own stock and choose when to play them from the orders you receive, never seeing the other hands.
pros: Each card feels like a real decision.
Timing is read from small signals.
cons: Plans fail when others hold back.
Turns can pass waiting for news.

pairs.tendency: Players win tricks while knowing only their own stock, so what the others hold is guessed from what they play, and the wider system is barely felt.
pros: Familiar play with a small, clear view.
Each played card reveals a little.
cons: The system sits in the background.
Strong hands decide much of the game.

pairs.tendency: Players talk and trade with only their own corner in view, so deals rest on what each says about their stock, and nothing can be checked.
pros: Talk fills the gaps in what players know.
Players learn who they can trust.
cons: Claims cannot be checked at the table.
Confident talkers can steer others wrongly.

pairs.tendency: You gather sets for your own corner without seeing the rest, so which pieces others hold or need is a matter of guessing.
pros: Clear goals with a small view.
Players ask around to find what is missing.
cons: Sets can matter more than the system.
Players may sit on pieces others need.

pairs.tendency: Each player lays tiles in their own corner and cannot see the shared map, so the pieces may not join up until much later.
pros: Joined-up pieces come as a surprise.
Each player has a small, calm task.
cons: Tiles may fail to connect.
Nobody can fix what they cannot see.

pairs.tendency: One player acts or speaks and the next answers, so the orders and replies passed along are the only view each player has of the whole.
pros: Passing messages makes the links clear.
Players listen closely to each other.
cons: Messages can change along the way.
One late reply holds up the chain.

pairs.tendency: Nobody may talk and each player sees only their own corner, so the others can only be guessed from what arrives and when.
pros: Players read each order closely.
Quiet play keeps delays easy to notice.
cons: Misreadings cannot be cleared up.
Players can feel cut off.

pairs.tendency: A rule changed on your turn spreads through a system you cannot fully see, so players learn what it did only from what reaches them.
pros: Players see how one change travels.
Rule changes arrive as surprises.
cons: A change can break things nobody can trace.
Arguments over what changed are likely.

pairs.tendency: You speak as a character who sees only their own stock and orders, and you decide what they would do about things they cannot see.
pros: The limited view feels like a real job.
Players act on what a role knows.
cons: Players may fill gaps with invention.
The system itself can be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: Hands decide the outcome of flicks or stacks, while the stock and orders each player sees stay private, so skill and guesswork run side by side.
pros: Physical play breaks up the quiet guessing.
Easy to follow.
cons: The system becomes a side show.
Skilled hands can outweigh sound guesses.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the map as they go, but each draws only their own corner, so the full picture appears only when the pieces are put together.
pros: The whole system appears at the end.
Players see what they could not know.
cons: Corners may not match.
Drawing can matter more than the view.

pairs.tendency: You ask one player for a card, which tells everyone what you hold, so asking is the way to learn about stock beyond your own corner.
pros: Questions become the only way to see further.
Asking shows what others need.
cons: Asking gives your own stock away.
Players may ask the same person each time.

pairs.tendency: The others bet and the bank throws, with each player seeing only their own stock, so bets rest on guesses about how much the bank holds.
pros: Bets show what players think is out there.
The bank role changes how the view feels.
cons: Guesses about the bank are rarely checkable.
The system effect is lost behind the betting.

pairs.tendency: Players stake stock on a throw, but each sees only their own corner, so the stakes tell little about what others can afford to lose.
pros: Simple bets in a murky system.
Players feel the cost of staking blindly.
cons: Luck decides what the system teaches.
Players may stake more than they can replace.

pairs.tendency: Players put chips in while they think their hidden cards can win, and the view of each corner is private too, so little is open to anyone.
pros: Every bet is a guess on thin facts.
Reading other players matters.
cons: So much is hidden that players lose their footing.
Chips can matter more than the system.

pairs.tendency: Each player builds their own side, and sees only that side, so how the other builds fit together shows up only in play.
pros: Choices feel personal.
Mismatched sides show how a system can fail.
cons: Sides may not suit each other.
Players can feel they planned in the dark.

pairs.tendency: You say beforehand what you will do, such as hold a stock level, though you see only your own corner, so the call rests on guesses about orders to come.
pros: Calls turn guesses into something to check.
Players see how forecasts fail.
cons: Missed calls are blamed on others.
Players may call small to stay safe.

pairs.tendency: Captured pieces change sides, and with each player seeing only their own corner, a lead can swing without anyone knowing why.
pros: Sudden swings are easy to see.
Players learn how quickly a position can change.
cons: Swings can seem to come from nowhere.
The system view is lost in the chase.

pairs.tendency: A player who is caught waits in jail until a teammate frees them, and each teammate sees only their own corner, so rescues depend on guessing who is held.
pros: Teammates come to depend on each other.
Rescues feel earned.
cons: Teammates cannot see who needs help.
Waiting in jail is dull.

pairs.tendency: Pieces are taken by surrounding them, but each player sees only their own part of the board, so they cannot tell what is closing in.
pros: Danger builds up quietly.
Taking a piece feels earned.
cons: Surrounds go unseen until too late.
The limited view can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: Players behind get a chance to catch up, but each sees only their own corner, so nobody can tell exactly who is behind or by how much.
pros: The gap stays small.
Support arrives where it is needed.
cons: Help can go to the wrong player.
Leaders are hard to spot.

pairs.tendency: Cards or dice decide everything and each player sees only their own result, so the system behaves with no choices to learn from.
pros: Very easy to play.
Players see how little they know.
cons: Nothing a player does shows up.
The point of the hidden view is lost.

pairs.tendency: One player chases the rest, and each runner sees only what is close by, so the chase is felt before it is understood.
pros: Quick and lively.
Players feel a lack of view in their bodies.
cons: Little stock or orders to think about.
The system is nearly forgotten.

pairs.tendency: Each turn you choose which player is hit or helped, but you see only your own corner, so you pick from guesses about who needs what.
pros: Picking a target shows what you believe.
Mistakes show how little each player sees.
cons: Helped players may not be the ones in need.
Players can feel picked on without reason.

pairs.tendency: Players try to link one side of the board to the other, but each sees only their own stretch, so the gaps appear only when the chain is tested.
pros: Links form in a small view.
The first full chain is a clear moment.
cons: Gaps are found late.
Players cannot tell who broke the chain.

pairs.tendency: Each choice beats one other and loses to a third, and nobody sees the whole system, so players guess what the others will pick from small signals.
pros: Guessing feels fair to everyone.
The cycle keeps play moving.
cons: Guessing alone can crowd out the system.
A lack of information can feel like luck.

pairs.tendency: You show a pair or run you hold and score for it, which tells others a little about your corner, though the rest of the system stays hidden.
pros: Declared sets are small, clear signals.
Players learn what others hold.
cons: Declaring gives your plans away.
The system is not felt.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a power nobody else has and sees only their own corner, so players act on different rules and guess what others can do.
pros: Each role feels distinct.
Players learn how others' powers shape the system.
cons: Hidden powers can feel unfair.
Learning other powers takes many rounds.

pairs.tendency: A player can offer to double what the game is worth, but sees only their own corner, so the offer rests on a guess about the rest.
pros: Doubling makes guesses feel costly.
Nerve and guessing blend.
cons: Doubled stakes can punish thin information.
Offers may seem rash.

pairs.tendency: If you can capture, you have to, so your options are narrowed by a position you cannot fully see, and others can steer your moves.
pros: Forced moves are easy to follow.
Players learn how others steer them.
cons: Forced moves can feel unfair.
Little room to avoid a trap.

pairs.tendency: What you do builds up your character, while you see only your own stock, so the growth is felt but its effect on others stays unseen.
pros: Growth is easy to see.
Players learn how far their own view can go.
cons: Strong players may not know how they affect others.
Later challenges can feel set.

pairs.tendency: Each player recites the whole list and adds an item, and each sees only their own part of the system, so the list shows how much each can remember.
pros: Memory tasks are clear.
Players listen closely.
cons: The list is about memory more than systems.
The recital slows down later turns.

pairs.tendency: The more skilled player starts with less, but each sees only their own corner, so a skill gap can only be guessed, and the help may land wrongly.
pros: A gap may be narrowed without anyone saying so.
Weaker players feel more included.
cons: The right handicap is hard to set.
Hidden help can feel patronising.

pairs.tendency: Someone hides something and the others hunt, with each player seeing only their own patch, so searches overlap or miss whole areas.
pros: Searching feels real and tense.
Players see how a small view misses things.
cons: Players may search the same places twice.
The system is a side matter.

pairs.tendency: Pieces hop over others to land behind them, and with only your own corner in view, jumps come from places you did not see.
pros: Jumps feel sudden.
Players see how hidden moves play out.
cons: Jumps can feel unfair.
The system is lost in the board.

pairs.tendency: You roll dice, keep the ones you like and roll the rest, with only your own stock visible, so each choice is made without knowing what others need.
pros: Choices come in small steps.
Players weigh risk again each time.
cons: Rolls hide the effect of orders.
Players may keep dice for no clear reason.

pairs.tendency: If your piece lands on another's, theirs goes back to the start, and each player sees only their own corner, so a hit comes from out of sight.
pros: Hits feel like news.
Safe spaces become valued.
cons: Players cannot tell who sent them back.
Losses seem arbitrary.

pairs.tendency: Three in a row lets you take an opponent's piece, and each player sees only their own area, so threats build up out of sight.
pros: Rows are simple to aim for.
Taking a piece is clear.
cons: Hidden rows catch players by surprise.
Players cannot tell what to block.

pairs.tendency: Players build words from letters while seeing only their own letters, so what others are building is guessed from what they have played.
pros: Words are easy to check.
Guessing lets players read each other.
cons: Vocabulary decides who does well.
The system is out of view.

pairs.tendency: You add a tile to an open end if the number matches, and each player sees only their own tiles, so missed turns come from guesses about others.
pros: Matches are simple to check.
Missed turns teach a little about stock.
cons: Missed turns can feel like luck.
Players may hold tiles to block others.

pairs.tendency: Players lay sets face up and others add to them, so melds are the only part of the system everyone sees, and the rest of each stock stays hidden.
pros: Melds show a little of each corner.
Adding to others' sets links players.
cons: Melds give plans away.
Most of the system stays unseen.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds a power that works once, and a hidden corner makes the right moment hard to pick, since nobody knows what others will do.
pros: Timing feels weighty.
Guessing the right moment is tense.
cons: Powers can be wasted.
Hidden stock makes timing a coin flip.

pairs.tendency: The other player can refuse a move you offer, yet neither sees the other's corner, so each decision is made with half the facts.
pros: Choices feel shared.
Players explain their reasons.
cons: Refusals are hard to understand.
Talking can slow turns.

pairs.tendency: A message passes along the line by whisper, and nobody can check it until it arrives, which is much how orders travel when each player sees only their own corner.
pros: The delay and change in messages is easy to feel.
Players see how orders can distort.
cons: Mistakes may be blamed on the wrong player.
Players can feel they are only passing things on.

pairs.tendency: You hand chosen cards to another player before play and cannot see what you will get, so each side decides on a partial view of the other.
pros: Giving shows trust or caution.
Each hand is a surprise.
cons: Players may pass cards that hurt others.
Little can be undone after passing.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up and the other picks a side, so the setter has to guess what the other will choose, with only their own view to go on.
pros: Setups come out fair when guesses are sound.
Players learn to think from the other side.
cons: Unfair setups are hard to spot.
The system stays in the background.

pairs.tendency: A piece that reaches the far end turns into a stronger one, but each player sees only their own corner, so the race to promote is run in the dark.
pros: Pushing forward has a clear reward.
Players guess what others are building.
cons: Promotions can arrive with no warning.
The system view is lost.

pairs.tendency: A team runs in legs, passing the baton, and each runner sees only their own leg, so a hand-over depends on guessing the next runner.
pros: Teammates depend on each other.
Hand-overs show where delays appear.
cons: Slow legs hold up the rest.
Waiting players lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Certain shapes are safe from capture, and each player sees only their own corner, so players build for safety without knowing what threatens them.
pros: Safe shapes give a clear target.
Players feel how small their view is.
cons: Safety may be built against the wrong threat.
The system is easy to forget.

pairs.tendency: Tricks are won for named prize cards, and with only your own stock in view, the prizes others hold are guessed from what they play.
pros: Prizes are clear to aim for.
Reading others adds depth.
cons: The system is hardly felt.
One card can swing a whole round.

pairs.tendency: Face-up cards in the middle are the one open view in the game, so each player's own corner is matched against a common part everyone can see.
pros: A shared view anchors the guessing.
Players compare what they know.
cons: The shared cards can crowd out the hidden corner.
Hidden and shared parts can be hard to balance.

pairs.tendency: Everyone adds to a pot and one player wins it, with each player seeing only their own stock, so nobody knows who can afford to stay in.
pros: The pot grows steadily.
Players guess at each other's stock.
cons: A growing pot can crowd out the system.
Players may stay in blindly.

pairs.tendency: Seeds are scooped and dropped one by one into pits, and each player sees only their own row, so players guess how their sowing alters the others.
pros: Counting is clear and calm.
Each sowing has a visible result.
cons: Players cannot see what sowing does to the other row.
The whole system is hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: An extra hand is dealt face down and one player may take it, so players decide on stock they cannot see in a system they only partly know.
pros: The spare hand adds a real gamble.
Swapping shows how players feel about risk.
cons: Taking the hand is a blind choice.
One player's gamble can upset all the others.

pairs.tendency: Some spaces have rules of their own, and each player sees only the squares near them, so surprises come from the part of the track they cannot see.
pros: Special squares add surprise.
Players remember where they landed.
cons: Squares can seem unfair when unseen.
Effects may be hard to trace.

pairs.tendency: Everything has a price, and each player sees only their own funds and orders, so they spend without knowing what others have available.
pros: Each cost is clear.
Spending shows each player's priorities.
cons: Players may overspend on a guess.
Costs may seem unfair when others' budgets are hidden.

pairs.tendency: You share a fixed amount between places while sharing is hidden from others, so each guesses where the others put their effort.
pros: Splitting shows risk plainly.
Guessing the others' split is tense.
cons: Players may spread too thinly.
A wrong guess cannot be fixed later.

pairs.tendency: Everyone keeps moving until a signal comes, and each sees only their own corner, so the stop catches players in different states of stock.
pros: Stops are sudden and easy to read.
Players see how stock varies at one moment.
cons: The slowest player is caught for reasons they cannot see.
Little time to think.

pairs.tendency: You put cards back and take new ones, with only your own stock in view, so swaps rest on guesses about what others need.
pros: Swaps are small, quick choices.
Swapping may help another player without notice.
cons: Players cannot tell who gains from a swap.
Swaps may be wasted.

pairs.tendency: Players may take the whole discard pile, and each sees only their own stock, so a pile grown by others can be a surprise gift or a burden.
pros: Taking the pile feels like a risk.
The pile shows what others threw away.
cons: The pile can be a heavy burden.
Players cannot tell what they will get.

pairs.tendency: One suit beats the rest, and each player sees only their own cards, so the strength of the suit in other hands is guessed.
pros: Trump gives a simple edge to track.
Players read the table from what is played.
cons: Trump can overshadow the system.
Strong trumps decide a lot.

pairs.tendency: You play two games at once, attacking in one and defending in the other, and each player sees only their own corner of each, so tracking is hard.
pros: Two views give plenty to think about.
Attack and defence are seen side by side.
cons: The load can be too much to follow.
Both corners can be hard to read.

pairs.tendency: Some cards can stand for any other, and with each player seeing only their own corner, a wild card fills gaps others cannot know exist.
pros: Wild cards solve problems quickly.
Players feel relief when one arrives.
cons: Wild cards may hide a mismatch.
Players may hold wilds for too long.

pairs.tendency: The board edges join up, and each player sees only their own stretch, so a line leaving one corner can reappear in another unseen.
pros: Surprise arrivals add interest.
The board has no safe edge.
cons: Players cannot tell where lines come back.
The loop is hard to picture.

pairs.tendency: One player knows a secret and the others ask yes or no questions, so each answer reveals only a little of what lies beyond their own corner.
pros: Each answer narrows the guesses.
Question skill matters more than luck.
cons: Players may ask the same thing twice.
Narrowing takes many rounds.

pairs.tendency: Players race to the end while each sees only their own stock and orders, so none can tell how far ahead or behind the others are.
pros: Simple goal.
Racing shows how a small view misleads.
cons: Players may rush past the limits.
The leader is hard to spot.

pairs.tendency: Points are counted at the end, and during play each player sees only their own corner, so nobody knows who is ahead until the count.
pros: Final count is a clear reveal.
Players guess about each other.
cons: Playing blind can feel pointless.
Points can matter more than learning.

pairs.tendency: Players are knocked out one by one, and with only your own corner in view, you cannot tell who is next to fall or why.
pros: Tension builds with each loss.
Players see how failure spreads.
cons: Early losers wait.
Falling out can seem to come without cause.

pairs.tendency: The team tries to keep the system alive, yet each player sees only their own corner, so they depend on reports to learn how it is going.
pros: Reports become valuable.
The team feels the gaps in what it knows.
cons: Collapse can come with no warning.
One player's report can mislead the group.

pairs.tendency: The group works on one target while each sees only their own corner, so players share what they know to reach it.
pros: Talk about the target comes naturally.
Each player's view adds something.
cons: Reports can be wrong or late.
A few voices can take over the sharing.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a secret goal and a view limited to their own corner, so nobody knows what others hold or want.
pros: Mystery on top of mystery.
Players learn how much is hidden in real work.
cons: Too much is hidden to read.
Players may give up guessing.

pairs.tendency: A story unfolds until it ends, and each player knows only their own part of it, so the whole story is pieced together at the end.
pros: The full story shows at the close.
Each player holds a small part.
cons: Parts may not fit.
The end can feel set in advance.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, and each player sees only their own corner, so the game is a chance to notice what could not be known.
pros: Players reflect on what they missed.
No pressure to guess right.
cons: Play can seem aimless.
Players may not know when to stop.

pairs.tendency: Each player sets what doing well means and sees only their own corner, so players judge themselves on goals others cannot see.
pros: Goals feel personal.
Players learn what they value.
cons: Goals cannot be compared.
Players may set goals too easy to miss.

pairs.tendency: Play goes on until one player loses, and each sees only their own corner, so who is about to lose is hard to tell.
pros: Tension for everyone.
Others are safe once someone falls.
cons: The loser may not know why.
The loser can feel singled out.

pairs.tendency: Everyone aims to keep play going and sees only their own corner, so they have to trust what reaches them to keep the system running.
pros: Players care about shared upkeep.
Gaps in knowledge are felt and mended.
cons: Play can drift with no end in view.
One quiet player can stall the rest.

pairs.tendency: The game cannot be won, and each player sees only their own corner, so what players learn comes from the muddle and not from any result.
pros: Players notice what the view hides.
No contest over the outcome.
cons: Players may find it pointless.
There is little to measure progress.

pairs.tendency: You play alone against the cards and see only your own part, so the hidden parts of the layout are guessed from what turns up.
pros: Solo play is calm.
Each reveal teaches something.
cons: The hidden view has little to hide from.
Luck of the layout can decide.

pairs.tendency: Several short games are played and each starts with the view limited to your own corner, so lessons from one round can help the next.
pros: Each round builds on the last.
Players can try other guesses.
cons: Repeats can wear thin.
Early wins may end the series.

pairs.tendency: Every point counts against you, and each player sees only their own total and orders, so nobody knows who is safest.
pros: Careful play is rewarded.
Players guess at the others' totals.
cons: Players may hold back for too long.
Little is seen of the system.

pairs.tendency: You have to land on an exact number, and with only your own corner in view, players overshoot or fall short without knowing what others are doing.
pros: Exact targets are easy to check.
Waiting for the right number is tense.
cons: Players may be stuck close to the target.
The hidden view adds little.

pairs.tendency: The aim is turned upside down, and with each player seeing only their own corner, losing on purpose depends on guessing what others will do.
pros: Losing on purpose changes how stock is seen.
Players think from another angle.
cons: Players may lose by accident.
Hidden stock makes the aim hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: Everyone plays at once on their own board and sees only their own corner, so there is little to learn about how choices reach others.
pros: Calm and quick.
Each player moves at their own pace.
cons: Players have little reason to guess about others.
The point of a hidden system can be lost.

pairs.tendency: Players attack or sabotage each other and see only their own corner, so a hit comes from someone unseen and the reply is a guess.
pros: Attacks come as surprises.
Players learn how blame spreads.
cons: Players may blame the wrong person.
Fights can bury the system.

pairs.tendency: Players change the board for each other while seeing only their own corner, so the effects of others' moves arrive without a name on them.
pros: Effects spread in a way players can feel.
Quiet play with real links.
cons: Players cannot trace what changed.
Blame may fall on the wrong person.

pairs.tendency: The whole team plays against the game, yet each player sees only their own corner, so they have to share what they know to keep the system going.
pros: Sharing becomes a real task.
Everyone holds a piece.
cons: One player may take over the sharing.
Reports can be wrong or late.

pairs.tendency: Players work together but each has a private reason to win more, and each sees only their own corner, so nobody can tell if a report is honest.
pros: Trust becomes a real question.
Players feel pulled two ways.
cons: Selfish reports can harm the whole.
Hard to tell mistakes from tricks.

pairs.tendency: Two teams compete and each player sees only their own corner, so teammates have to pool what they know to guess at the other side.
pros: Team talk is useful.
Pooling gives a wider view.
cons: Pooled views may still be wrong.
One loud player can take over.

pairs.tendency: One player secretly works against the team and everyone sees only their own corner, so trouble is hard to tell from a plain mistake.
pros: Suspicion has something to feed on.
Players weigh each report.
cons: Mistakes look like sabotage.
Accusations can upset people.

pairs.tendency: Players send letters over weeks and each sees only their own corner, so every reply is the only news from elsewhere, and it is already old.
pros: Delay becomes part of the system.
Players read every letter with care.
cons: Slow play loses attention.
Old news can lead to wrong choices.

pairs.tendency: One player is away or a ghost, so their corner is empty or known only by hints, while the others see only their own corners too.
pros: The missing view is felt plainly.
Players learn to allow for gaps.
cons: An empty corner can stall the line.
Players may feel the gap is their fault.

pairs.tendency: One player runs the world and knows all of it while the others see only their own corner, so the game master is the one who sees the whole system.
pros: Someone holds the full picture.
The master can steer play gently.
cons: The master's view can swamp the others.
Players may lean on the master for answers.

pairs.tendency: Passers-by join a game in a public place and each sees only their own corner, so new players arrive without knowing what has happened.
pros: Newcomers can join at once.
Players explain their corner to each other.
cons: Late joiners have no view of the system.
The game is hard to keep tidy.

pairs.tendency: One player faces all the others, who see only their own corners, so the lone player cannot see how the team is organised.
pros: The lone player has a clear target.
Team members have to share what they see.
cons: The lone player may feel shut out.
The team's view can be wrong.

pairs.tendency: You play against the pack with a view of only your own corner, so everything beyond it is a matter of chance and your own guesses.
pros: Calm and easy to start.
Nobody else is needed.
cons: There is nobody to share guesses with.
The hidden view has no other players to affect.

pairs.tendency: Dice and draws decide most of the game, and each player sees only their own stock, so shortages arrive that no choice could have prevented.
pros: Easy to play.
Players feel how little they control.
cons: Nothing learned about causes.
Players may think it is all luck.

pairs.tendency: Random events hit stock, but players can prepare, and each sees only their own corner, so preparing is a guess about what others will also face.
pros: Preparing feels worthwhile.
Players see how stock cushions shocks.
cons: Preparing for the wrong shock is easy.
Preparation costs stock that others may need.

pairs.tendency: Careful choices mostly decide play, with a little luck, and each player sees only their own corner, so skill is shown by reading small signals.
pros: Skill in reading signals is rewarded.
A little luck keeps results open.
cons: Practised players may read signals faster.
Newcomers may not see why they fell behind.

pairs.tendency: Choices alone decide the game, yet each player sees only their own corner, so skill lies in reading what arrives and guessing what does not.
pros: Players learn to infer from little.
Results can be traced to choices.
cons: The hidden view can still feel unfair.
Practised players gain a lot.

pairs.tendency: Dice or cards are read as signs, and each player sees only their own corner, so readings are applied to a system they cannot see.
pros: Readings spark talk about what is unseen.
Each player reads the signs their own way.
cons: Readings can be mistaken for facts.
The system is hard to link to a sign.

pairs.tendency: Success comes from sensing when others will act, and with only your own corner in view, you sense it from small signs in orders and pauses.
pros: Players learn to read each other.
Warm and quiet play.
cons: Sensing is hard to explain.
Hidden stock may make the signals too faint.

pairs.tendency: Dice are looked up on a table that says what happens next, and each player sees only their own corner, so each hears a different part of the story.
pros: Each corner has its own tale.
The table adds surprise.
cons: Stories may not match.
Dice decide more than orders.

pairs.tendency: Everything is visible to everyone, which is the opposite of this block, so the two blocks pull against each other and one of them has to give.
pros: The hidden view and the open board can be set apart.
Players compare what they see and what they guess.
cons: The blocks cancel each other.
Players may not know which view to trust.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds cards nobody else sees, on top of a corner nobody else sees, so most of the game is hidden.
pros: Hidden hands add to the sense of guessing.
Reading other players matters.
cons: Too much hidden at once is hard to handle.
The system is hard to understand.

pairs.tendency: Some players have a secret role and each sees only their own corner, so a player cannot tell if a report comes from friend or foe.
pros: Reports carry real doubt.
Players weigh each other's words.
cons: Honest reports may be doubted.
Hidden roles can cloud the system.

pairs.tendency: Players use clues to work out hidden facts, and a view of only your own corner means every clue is a trace from the unseen rest of the system.
pros: Clues explain how the whole works.
Working it out feels rewarding.
cons: Clues can be too thin.
Players may stall without enough to go on.

pairs.tendency: Players lie about what they hold, and with each seeing only their own corner, lies about stock and orders cannot be checked until too late.
pros: Bluffs have real effects.
Players learn to doubt reports.
cons: Lies cause real shortages for others.
Bluffs can upset players.

pairs.tendency: A secret rule is found by breaking it, and each player sees only their own corner, so the rule is learned from effects that arrive later.
pros: Discovery is a real puzzle.
Players share what they found.
cons: Learning the rule takes many mistakes.
Players may feel unfairly caught.

pairs.tendency: One player sees the answer but cannot say it, so the others each guess from their own corner and the hints given.
pros: Hints are the only bridge between corners.
Guessing builds in a calm way.
cons: Hints can be misread.
The knowing player may grow frustrated.

pairs.tendency: The map is hidden until explored, and each player sees only their own corner, so the whole map is unknown to everyone until late.
pros: Exploring feels fresh.
Players see how a small view grows.
cons: Nobody can plan ahead.
Exploring alone can be slow.

pairs.tendency: One hand is face up for all, so the open hand is the one clear view of stock, while every other corner stays hidden.
pros: One hand gives a point to reason from.
Players can compare an open hand with guesses.
cons: The open hand may be misread as typical.
The hidden corners still hide most of the system.

pairs.tendency: Some points are kept secret, and each player sees only their own corner, so nobody knows who is ahead and the end result is a surprise.
pros: Everyone stays in the game.
The final count is a reveal.
cons: Players may not feel their choices matter.
Hidden scores add to the confusion.

pairs.tendency: One player acts at a time, so each waits and sees only their own corner, and orders arrive between turns as the only news.
pros: Waiting makes the delay plain.
Turns are easy to follow.
cons: Waiting players lose interest.
Orders may pile up between turns.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses at the same moment, each seeing only their own corner, so orders cross in the dark and arrive together.
pros: Players see how orders overlap.
Quick play.
cons: Orders may cause jams nobody can follow.
Players may feel rushed.

pairs.tendency: Anyone may act at any moment while each sees only their own corner, so orders and stock move on without anyone seeing the whole.
pros: Fast and lively play.
Players feel the pressure of fast news.
cons: Quick players take over.
Players may lose track of their own stock.

pairs.tendency: Each turn has a clock, and each player sees only their own corner, so little time is left to guess about the rest.
pros: A clock keeps the guessing short.
Players act on what they have.
cons: Players may panic and over-order.
Slow thinkers fall behind.

pairs.tendency: The game runs over real days, with one move each morning, so each player sees only their own corner and orders arrive after real waiting.
pros: Waiting makes delay felt.
Players notice slow effects.
cons: Players may lose interest between moves.
It is hard to keep everyone playing.

pairs.tendency: The game slows players down on purpose, so each has time to think about a corner they cannot fully see.
pros: Time to think about gaps.
Calm, thoughtful play.
cons: More time does not add information.
Players may grow bored.

pairs.tendency: The game speeds up as it goes, so players see only their own corner as orders arrive faster and faster.
pros: Rising pressure is easy to feel.
Players see how small errors grow.
cons: Players may lose track near the end.
The rush can hide the lesson.

pairs.tendency: Some throws give another go, so one player moves several times while the others, seeing only their own corners, do not know why orders jump.
pros: Streaks add excitement.
Players feel how one burst reaches others.
cons: Players may not see where the surge came from.
Lucky players can run ahead.

pairs.tendency: The game has stages with different rules, and each player sees only their own corner, so what they learn in one stage may not carry over.
pros: Stages let players try again.
Early lessons set up later ones.
cons: Players may feel lost between stages.
Hidden stock can carry over unnoticed.

pairs.tendency: The board works like a real system, yet each player sees only their own corner of it, so the whole behaviour is seen only when the game is over.
pros: A real system gets felt from the inside.
The reveal at the end can show how the parts joined.
cons: Players may not understand the parts.
Players can feel they never saw the system.

pairs.tendency: Each player plays a real group that sees only its own part of the problem, so no group can tell what the others need.
pros: Each group's view feels real.
Players feel why groups miss each other.
cons: Groups may blame each other.
Players may only guess the others' needs.

pairs.tendency: Everyone draws from one limited store but sees only their own use of it, so nobody can tell when it is close to running out.
pros: Overuse is felt before it is understood.
The shared store becomes a puzzle.
cons: The store may run dry without warning.
Players may blame each other.

pairs.tendency: What you do shows up later and each player sees only their own corner, so effects arrive late from places that cannot be seen.
pros: Late effects are easy to feel.
Players learn to wait and watch.
cons: Players may blame the wrong cause.
Effects are hard to trace back.

pairs.tendency: Players agree a new rule and see its effect, but each sees only their own corner, so they judge the rule from a narrow view.
pros: Rules can be tested in play.
Players compare what they saw.
cons: A rule may look harmful or helpful by chance.
Players may disagree about what it did.

pairs.tendency: After play, players talk through what happened, and each brings only their own corner, so the talk puts the whole system together for the first time.
pros: The whole picture appears after play.
Players hear what others could not see.
cons: Players may remember their own corner most.
The talk may not cover every corner.

pairs.tendency: Changes cannot be undone and each player sees only their own corner, so a choice may harm a part nobody could see, and nothing can mend it.
pros: Choices carry weight.
Players take more care.
cons: Harm may go unseen.
Players may become afraid to act.

pairs.tendency: The rules make a point about the world, and with each player seeing only their own corner, the point is that no one sees the whole.
pros: The rules say something clear.
Players feel the point, not just read it.
cons: Players may not catch the argument.
Muddle can look like a design flaw.

pairs.tendency: Something real rests on the result and each player sees only their own corner, so real stakes depend on guesses about the rest.
pros: Guesses feel serious.
Players learn about trust.
cons: Real stakes can cause arguments.
Players may feel unfairly judged.

pairs.tendency: A value such as health becomes points, and each player sees only their own corner, so they chase their own points without seeing the cost elsewhere.
pros: The cost of chasing a number shows up.
Players see how local gains can harm others.
cons: Players may blame each other for it.
Points may still be chased.

pairs.tendency: Players practise a way of working that does not exist yet and see only their own corner, so they feel how hard it is to coordinate.
pros: Players feel the future from inside.
The gaps in it show up early.
cons: Players may take muddle for failure.
The rehearsal may feel confused.

pairs.tendency: The slowest step sets the pace, and each player sees only their own corner, so nobody can tell where the slow step is.
pros: Players feel a jam before they find it.
Finding the bottleneck is a puzzle.
cons: Players may speed up the wrong step.
Blame may fall on the wrong player.

pairs.tendency: Goods are made ahead to a guess or only on an order, and each player sees only their own corner, so a guess at others' needs drives the choice.
pros: Players feel the difference between guess and order.
The cost of guessing is clear.
cons: Players may overstock out of worry.
Players may wait for orders that never come.

pairs.tendency: Players choose how many to make at once, but each sees only their own corner, so big batches may land where they are not needed.
pros: Batch choices are easy to compare.
Waste or waiting shows plainly.
cons: Players may build big batches on a guess.
Others may suffer from the batch size.

pairs.tendency: Equipment fails at random and each player sees only their own corner, so a breakdown elsewhere is felt only as a late order.
pros: Breakdowns are felt as gaps.
Players learn to allow for slack.
cons: Players may not know a machine failed.
Waiting may be blamed on the wrong player.

pairs.tendency: Holding stock costs a little each round and running out costs more, and each player sees only their own corner, so the right amount is hard to judge.
pros: Balancing stock is easy to feel.
Players learn what safety stock does.
cons: Players may over-order out of worry.
Shortages may repeat down the line.

pairs.tendency: Pieces move by dice, but one narrow space on the track holds everyone up, so lucky long rolls only bring players to the queue sooner.
pros: Players see a queue form on the track.
Dice make the jam feel unplanned.
cons: Rolling gives no way to ease the jam.
Waiting players have nothing to decide.

pairs.tendency: Cards pass round the table, but one player or one slot takes the longest, so the packs pile up in front of them.
pros: Everyone sees where the slowdown sits.
Piles of waiting cards make the cause plain.
cons: Players behind the slow one sit idle.
Quick pickers gain nothing from being quick.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the chance to use the one slow step, so its price rises while everything after it waits on it.
pros: Prices show how scarce the slow step is.
Bidders learn what a place in the queue is worth.
cons: Rich players can buy the queue every round.
Bidding can take longer than the step itself.

pairs.tendency: Players keep pushing for more output, but the slowest step caps what can pass, so extra pushing only adds stock that waits in front of it.
pros: Pushing harder visibly changes nothing past the cap.
Stalled stock makes the cost of greed clear.
cons: Players may keep pushing and not see why.
Busts can seem to come from nowhere.

pairs.tendency: Players hold parts of a map, and one narrow pass or crossing carries all the traffic, so whoever holds it sets the pace for everyone.
pros: One spot on the map matters most.
Fights have a clear prize.
cons: The key spot draws every fight.
Other areas can feel pointless.

pairs.tendency: One action space has room for a single worker, so it is taken every round and every plan that needs it queues behind whoever got there first.
pros: Shows a shared slow step well, with one space and many users.
Turn order carries real weight.
cons: The same player can hold the key space again and again.
Other spaces can sit unused.

pairs.tendency: Players build patterns, but one kind of piece arrives slowly, so every pattern that needs it stalls while pieces for the rest pile up.
pros: Players see what one missing piece holds up.
Building toward a gap feels tense.
cons: Spare pieces gather with no use.
Patterns can stay half finished.

pairs.tendency: Players hold cards, and one kind of card is rare and needed for most plays, so hands fill with cards that cannot be used until it turns up.
pros: Saving the rare card feels weighty.
Players plan around what they lack.
cons: Full hands of unplayable cards frustrate.
Draws decide when the jam clears.

pairs.tendency: Players play tricks, but one hand or suit controls who leads, so the whole round waits on whoever holds it and the others just follow.
pros: Shows how one holder sets the pace.
Familiar play makes the point simple.
cons: The link to a queue can feel thin.
Followers can feel they have nothing to do.

pairs.tendency: Players trade for access to the one slow step, so talk centres on who goes through it first and what each will pay to jump the queue.
pros: Players argue about fair order.
Deals show who is waiting on whom.
cons: Talk can go on longer than the slow step.
Loud players can keep their place at the front.

pairs.tendency: Players gather sets, but one item is slow to arrive, so every set stays one piece short and the rest of the collection sits waiting.
pros: Shows how one gap holds up a whole set.
Players feel the near miss.
cons: Waiting can be dull.
Holding spare pieces gives no sense of progress.

pairs.tendency: Players build a map, and one tile type that opens the way forward is scarce, so building elsewhere adds length but no progress.
pros: The map shows where the jam is.
Players choose between waiting and building around.
cons: Tile draws can decide who is stuck.
Extra building can look like progress and not be.

pairs.tendency: One player answers each call, so the slowest answerer sets the speed of the whole exchange and quicker players wait for them.
pros: The slow voice is easy to hear.
Players learn to wait for one another.
cons: Slow answerers can feel put on the spot.
Quick players lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Nobody may talk, so players can only sense that a slow step is holding things up and cannot say where, and the jam shows in what piles up.
pros: Players read the jam from the table.
Quiet play makes waiting visible.
cons: Players cannot ask for help.
The cause of a stall can stay unclear.

pairs.tendency: Players can change a rule on their turn, so someone may widen the slow step and the whole game speeds up until the next one tightens.
pros: Players test ways to clear a jam.
Rule changes show their effect fast.
cons: One change can undo the whole point.
Players may change rules without finding the cause.

pairs.tendency: Each player acts as a character, and one character's slow job holds everyone else up, so the others stay in role while they wait.
pros: Waiting is felt, not just counted.
Players see the slow role's side.
cons: The slow role can feel blamed.
Waiting in character can bore people.

pairs.tendency: Players use their hands for a task, and the slowest or shakiest hands set the pace for those who need what they make.
pros: Hands make the slow step physical.
Players feel the strain of the slow job.
cons: The slowest player can feel judged.
Skill gaps decide where the jam sits.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the map as they go, and a narrow road or crossing they draw becomes the jam that every route has to pass.
pros: Players draw their own jams.
The map shows what slowed things down.
cons: Drawing can take longer than play.
Players may avoid drawing a jam on purpose.

pairs.tendency: Players ask each other for cards, and one player holds what everyone needs, so they are asked again and again while the rest wait.
pros: Players see who is being asked most.
Waiting on one holder feels real.
cons: One player gets asked too often.
Others have little to do.

pairs.tendency: The bank can only settle so many bets in a round, so winners queue for their pay and the bank's speed caps how fast play can go.
pros: The bank's pace shapes the round.
Players feel the cost of a slow payout.
cons: The bank player carries the load.
Long waits take the fun out of winning.

pairs.tendency: Players bet before each throw, but only one throw can happen at a time, so every bet waits on the same slow turn of the dice.
pros: Bets and the single throw are easy to follow.
Waiting builds tension.
cons: Nothing speeds the throw up.
Players have little to decide while waiting.

pairs.tendency: Players bet on hidden hands, and the slowest player to decide holds up each round of betting for everyone else.
pros: Players see how one slow chooser sets the pace.
Waiting can feed bluffs.
cons: Slow deciders cost others time.
Pressure to hurry can lead to rash bets.

pairs.tendency: Each player builds a side, and everyone's plan has to pass through the same scarce part, so every build gets shaped around it.
pros: Players see the same limit in every build.
Builds differ in how they deal with it.
cons: Builds can look alike when everyone avoids the jam.
Choices narrow fast.

pairs.tendency: Players promise what they will do, but the slow step limits how much anyone can deliver, so contracts that ignore it tend to fail.
pros: Players learn to promise what the slow step allows.
Failed contracts show the cause.
cons: Players may promise too much by habit.
A miss can feel like plain misfortune.

pairs.tendency: Captured pieces change sides, but only a few can be moved through the narrow point, so winning a battle there matters more than winning elsewhere.
pros: The narrow point becomes the key fight.
Swings in who holds it are clear.
cons: One lost fight can turn the game.
Pieces elsewhere may stand idle.

pairs.tendency: Captured players wait in jail, and the one gate that frees them is narrow, so rescuers queue while the jail fills up.
pros: Jam at the gate is easy to see.
Players on the same team have to take turns.
cons: Prisoners wait a long time.
Waiting can feel dull.

pairs.tendency: Players trap pieces by surrounding them, and a narrow gap on the board is easy to seal, so one block can hold up a whole group.
pros: Narrow spots become targets.
Players see what blocking does.
cons: A sealed gap can end a plan at once.
Surrounded players may have no move left.

pairs.tendency: The game helps players who are behind, but the slow step still caps everyone, so help can bring players level but not past the limit.
pros: Help is easy to see.
Players stay in the game longer.
cons: Help may do nothing against the cap.
Leaders can be held back as much as trailers.

pairs.tendency: Chance decides what passes the slow step, so players watch a queue grow and shrink with no choice that could change it.
pros: Players feel what a jam is like.
Nobody is blamed for a hold up.
cons: Nothing the player does makes a difference.
Waiting without a choice gets dull.

pairs.tendency: Players chase each other, and a narrow gap or doorway slows everyone through it, so it is where the chaser catches people.
pros: A narrow door changes the whole chase.
Slowing down at the gap feels real.
cons: Players pile up there.
The chase can stall in the gap.

pairs.tendency: Players pick who to help or hit, and picking the player who holds the slow step changes everyone's pace, so they get most of the attention.
pros: Targets have a clear reason.
Players see who holds the pace.
cons: The slow player is picked on.
Other players can be ignored.

pairs.tendency: Players try to link two sides of the board, and one narrow crossing is the only way, so the fight for it decides who connects.
pros: One crossing makes the aim clear.
Blocking has a real effect.
cons: Play can narrow to a single spot.
Other moves lose meaning.

pairs.tendency: Each choice beats one and loses to another, and the slow step limits how many of any choice can be made, so a player's options are capped.
pros: Players read each other's limits.
Guessing feels sharp.
cons: A narrow step blunts the cycle.
Predictable players are easy to beat.

pairs.tendency: Players declare combinations for points, but the scarce card that completes most of them arrives slowly, so declarations cluster after it appears.
pros: Players see when the scarce card matters.
Scores come in bursts.
cons: Players hold hands they cannot declare.
Long waits for one card.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a unique power, and the player whose power works at the slow step sets the pace, so their power counts for more than the others.
pros: Powers matter unequally.
Players see whose power is key.
cons: One power can dominate.
Other powers may feel small.

pairs.tendency: Players can double the stakes, and a slow step makes the end of the game late, so doubling early means a long wait before it pays.
pros: Stakes grow with waiting.
Timing a double feels sharp.
cons: Players may double and then wait a long time.
The jam can turn doubles into guesses.

pairs.tendency: Players have to capture when they can, and a narrow spot can be set up as bait, so one forced move there can hold up a whole line.
pros: Forced moves make jams predictable.
Players can plan around a trap.
cons: Bait at the gap is hard to avoid.
Players lose choices just when they need them.

pairs.tendency: Players grow stronger over time, but the slowest step limits how fast they can use that strength, so growth beyond it adds no pace.
pros: Players see growth meet a limit.
Rising strength feels real.
cons: Extra strength can sit unused.
Players may feel growth has no point.

pairs.tendency: Each player adds to a growing list, and the longest list takes the longest to say, so the slowest speaker sets the pace of the whole round.
pros: The slow step is easy to hear.
Players feel the list drag.
cons: Long lists slow everyone down.
Players with poor memory are left out.

pairs.tendency: The stronger player starts with less, and a bottleneck caps them anyway, so handicaps and the jam can both slow the same player.
pros: Players see two limits at once.
The weaker player has a chance.
cons: Limits can stack up on one player.
Players may not know which one slowed them.

pairs.tendency: Someone hides and the others search, but one door or passage has to be checked first, so the search queues there.
pros: The search has a clear order.
Waiting at the door builds tension.
cons: Searchers wait while one looks.
Hiding near the jam is hard to tell apart from luck.

pairs.tendency: Pieces hop over others, and only one landing space is open at the narrow point, so a line of pieces waits behind the one that goes first.
pros: Hops can clear a jam fast.
Players see a line of pieces waiting.
cons: One piece can block many.
Jumps may feel hard to plan.

pairs.tendency: Players keep some dice and reroll the rest, but a limit on how many results pass the slow step means extra strong rolls go to waste.
pros: Players see strong rolls wasted.
Keeping dice feels clever.
cons: Rolling more adds nothing.
Players can feel cheated.

pairs.tendency: Landing on a piece sends it back, and a narrow point where pieces gather means the same few players keep getting sent back.
pros: Danger at the gap is easy to see.
Players weigh waiting against rushing.
cons: The same players are sent back.
A single landing can undo a long wait.

pairs.tendency: Players make rows to take pieces, and a narrow spot decides who can form a row, so whoever holds it takes pieces while others wait.
pros: One spot has clear value.
Players take turns around it.
cons: A blocked row cannot be made.
Players can get locked out.

pairs.tendency: Players make words from letters, and one rare letter is needed by most words, so long words wait on it while the rest pile up.
pros: Players see a rare letter hold up play.
Word hunting has a clear gap.
cons: Many letters go unused.
Players with the letter hold the game.

pairs.tendency: Players add tiles to open ends, but only one end is open at the narrow point, so everyone waits for the one tile that fits it.
pros: The single open end is clear.
Waiting feels real.
cons: Players with no match pass again and again.
The line can stall completely.

pairs.tendency: Players lay out melds, but one rare card is needed to finish most of them, so hands hold unfinished sets until it arrives.
pros: Players see sets wait on one card.
Laying a meld feels like a release.
cons: Hands fill with unfinished sets.
Long gaps between melds.

pairs.tendency: Each power works once, and using one at the slow step is worth the most, so players hold their powers until the jam is reached.
pros: Timing a power feels weighty.
Players see where a power helps.
cons: Powers can be wasted away from the jam.
Players may wait too long to use them.

pairs.tendency: A move is offered and the other player can turn it down, so a slow reply holds up the one step everyone else is waiting on.
pros: Players see who holds things up.
Replies carry real weight.
cons: A slow reply stalls the table.
Turning down the offer can feel like blocking.

pairs.tendency: A message passes down a line, and the slowest passer holds up everything after them, and the message may change while it waits.
pros: Players see where the message slows.
Delay can change the message.
cons: Passers behind the slow one wait.
The slow player can be blamed for changes.

pairs.tendency: Players hand cards on before play, and the slowest player to choose holds up everyone who is waiting to receive.
pros: Passing shows who is the slowest.
Players learn to decide in time.
cons: Waiting players have nothing to do.
Slow players can feel hurried.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up and the other chooses a side, and a narrow point in the setup means the setter tries to make both sides equally stuck.
pros: Fair setups get tested.
The setter has a reason to be careful.
cons: The chooser can read the jam in advance.
Setup can take longer than play.

pairs.tendency: Pieces become stronger at the far end, but a narrow route to that end means pieces queue and only a few reach it.
pros: Players feel a long wait for promotion.
Getting through feels like a win.
cons: Few pieces are promoted.
Pieces behind the queue seem pointless.

pairs.tendency: A team runs a race in legs, and the slowest runner sets the team's time, so speeding up other runners changes nothing.
pros: The slowest leg is easy to name.
Teams learn to help the slow runner.
cons: The slow runner can feel blamed.
Fast runners can feel their effort is wasted.

pairs.tendency: Safe shapes cannot be captured, but a narrow area leaves little room to build one, so the jam itself decides where shapes can form.
pros: Players see how space limits safety.
Safe shapes feel like a goal.
cons: A narrow area can make safety impossible.
Players may crowd into the same space.

pairs.tendency: Scoring cards are named in advance, and the slow step limits how many can be won in time, so players pick which prizes to aim for.
pros: Players choose prizes with the limit in mind.
The goal is clear from the start.
cons: Chasing every prize can mean winning none.
Cards out of reach can be dropped.

pairs.tendency: Shared cards sit in the middle, and everyone uses them, so one slow player taking too long over them holds up the whole table.
pros: Everyone sees the same cards.
Waiting is shared and visible.
cons: One slow player holds everyone up.
Others may rush to use the cards first.

pairs.tendency: Everyone adds to the pot, but only one player can take it, and the slow step decides who gets there first, so the pot may grow for many rounds.
pros: A growing pot shows the wait.
Tension rises each round.
cons: The pot can reach a size nobody can win fairly.
Waiting players may lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Seeds are dropped pit by pit, and a full pit slows the whole round of sowing, so seeds heap up there while other pits sit empty.
pros: Heaps show where it is stuck.
Players can plan around a full pit.
cons: Empty pits sit useless.
One heap can decide the game.

pairs.tendency: A spare hand is up for grabs, and taking it takes time, so the player who takes it is slowed while the others play on.
pros: Players weigh the cost of taking it.
Choice has a clear price.
cons: The slow player falls behind.
Spare hands may be ignored.

pairs.tendency: One special square on the track sends players back or holds them, so it works as a bottleneck itself and every piece has to pass it.
pros: The jam sits in a square players can name.
Players plan their moves around it.
cons: The track can become a queue.
Luck decides who is held there.

pairs.tendency: Every item has a price, and the slowest step can only use so much, so spending more on the others buys nothing and the money is wasted.
pros: Players learn where spending helps.
Costs make the limit plain.
cons: Money piles up unused.
Players may spend before they see the cap.

pairs.tendency: Players share a fixed amount across places, and putting most of it at the slow step is the only way to widen it, so other places go short.
pros: Choosing where to put forces has a clear reason.
Players see what the others lose.
cons: Other places are left bare.
Players may weaken the wrong place.

pairs.tendency: Everyone moves until the signal, and the slowest to stop or reach a spot holds up the next round for everyone.
pros: Slow players are easy to see.
Rounds have a clear start and stop.
cons: The slowest player sets the pace.
Waiting players may get restless.

pairs.tendency: Players swap cards for new ones, but only a few swaps can pass through at a time, so a queue forms at the pile where cards are traded.
pros: Swaps show how a queue forms.
Players learn when to swap.
cons: Players wait at the pile.
The rare card they want may not come.

pairs.tendency: The whole discard pile can be taken, but only one player at a time can reach it, so the pile sets who gets what and when.
pros: The pile is easy to watch.
Taking it feels like a big move.
cons: One player at a time holds the pile.
Others wait with weak hands.

pairs.tendency: One suit beats the others, and cards of that suit are few, so whoever holds them decides each trick and the others queue behind.
pros: The key suit is clear.
Players see who holds the power.
cons: Few cards decide most tricks.
Players without trumps can feel shut out.

pairs.tendency: Two boards run side by side, and one slow board holds up the other, so a fast move on one cannot be used until the slow one catches up.
pros: Players feel two paces.
Waiting for the other board is clear.
cons: The slow board sets both.
Players can lose track of which board holds them.

pairs.tendency: Wild cards can stand for any card, so a player can use one to pass the slow step, and the few wilds become the most sought cards.
pros: Wilds are clearly valuable.
Players plan around when to use them.
cons: Wilds can remove the jam.
Players with no wilds can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: The board edges join, so pieces circle round and meet the same narrow point again and again, and the jam builds up each lap.
pros: Players meet the jam on each lap.
Circling makes the cost clear.
cons: Pieces can pile up in a ring.
The jam has no end.

pairs.tendency: Players ask yes-or-no questions, but only one question is answered at a time, so the answerer holds up every guess waiting behind.
pros: Players see a queue of questions.
Waiting makes players think harder.
cons: The answerer carries the load.
Idle players may lose focus.

pairs.tendency: Players race to finish, but all of them have to pass the one slow step, so the race turns into a queue and speed before it counts for little.
pros: The race has a clear sticking point.
Players learn where to put effort.
cons: Speeding ahead of the jam gives no lead.
Winning may depend on queue order.

pairs.tendency: Players score points, and the slow step caps how many anyone can make per round, so scores stay close and the order at the step counts.
pros: Caps keep scores close.
Players plan around the step.
cons: Scores may depend on queue order.
Extra effort elsewhere adds no points.

pairs.tendency: Players drop out one by one, and the slow step keeps supplies from reaching them, so those furthest from it fall first.
pros: Players see who the jam hits first.
The cause of dropping out is plain.
cons: Players at the end of the queue go out early.
Early exits can feel unfair.

pairs.tendency: The team works to survive, but all help has to pass the one slow step, so the whole group has to plan around it or the jam brings them down.
pros: The team shares one clear problem.
Planning together has a purpose.
cons: The jam can feel hopeless.
One player may take over the plan.

pairs.tendency: The group works toward one goal, and the slow step caps how fast they can reach it, so effort elsewhere adds nothing.
pros: The group finds the limit together.
Effort is aimed at one place.
cons: Players away from the jam can feel idle.
One player can end up directing.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a secret goal, and the slow step limits everyone, so players may quietly gain a place in the queue to reach their goal.
pros: Secret aims shape who goes first.
Players guess each other's reasons.
cons: Hard to tell a jam from a trick.
Hidden goals may be ignored in the rush.

pairs.tendency: The story moves forward, but one event or character holds it up, and every scene waits on it.
pros: A stall can become part of the story.
Players see why the plot waits.
cons: The story can drag.
Players may skip the jam to keep the story moving.

pairs.tendency: Nothing is won, and the slow step still limits what players can do, so they notice where things pile up with no score to chase.
pros: Players watch the jam without pressure.
Talk can turn to why it forms.
cons: Waiting without a goal can be dull.
Players may not see the point.

pairs.tendency: Players choose their own aims, and the slow step limits what anyone can reach, so aims that ignore it tend to fall short.
pros: Players learn what the limit allows.
Aims can be changed to fit.
cons: Players may set aims they cannot reach.
Missing an aim can feel like failure.

pairs.tendency: The game goes on until one player loses, and the player stuck at the slow step tends to fall behind the rest.
pros: Players see who is held up.
Everyone else stays safe a while.
cons: The player at the jam is singled out.
The loss may feel unearned.

pairs.tendency: The aim is to keep play going, and a slow step keeps it going by making players wait, so smoothing it out could end the game sooner.
pros: Waiting becomes useful.
Players notice what holds play up.
cons: Players may not want to clear the jam.
Play can drag without a push.

pairs.tendency: The game cannot be won, and the slow step caps what anyone can do, so players come to see that effort elsewhere does nothing.
pros: The limit shows itself over time.
Players think about why.
cons: Players may feel the game is pointless.
Frustration can build.

pairs.tendency: One player works against the layout, and a single blocked card or space holds up everything behind it, so the layout is cleared in an order set by the block.
pros: The blocked spot is easy to find.
Planning around it feels clever.
cons: One block can end the game.
Spare moves are wasted.

pairs.tendency: Players play several short games, and the same slow step shows up in each, so they can try a different plan in each round.
pros: Players try fixes between games.
Each round teaches something.
cons: The same jam can repeat.
